title: Nested spinning hexagon ball physics simulation
author: blueemi99
prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file (Three.js via CDN, no other assets) that is the 2026 version of the "ball bouncing inside a spinning hexagon" test.

Scene: a large hollow hexagonal prism (a 3D hexagon) slowly spinning on two axes at once. Inside it, a smaller hexagonal prism spins the opposite way, and inside that, a tiny one. Three nested spinning cages. The cage walls are see-through panels drawn only as clean outlines with a very light flat tint, so every ball inside stays clearly visible.

Physics (write your own, no physics library):
- Start with 1 ball inside the innermost cage. Every 2 seconds a new ball spawns, up to 300, each with its own random size, mass and color.
- Real gravity, friction, restitution and spin. Balls must collide with each other and with the rotating walls, picking up the wall's velocity at the contact point so they get flung realistically. No tunneling through walls, no jitter when balls rest on each other.
- When a ball hits a wall hard enough, that wall panel cracks and eventually breaks into flat shards that also obey physics, so balls can escape into the next cage outward.
- The outer cage never breaks. Escaped balls pile up at the bottom of it.

Look, clean cel-shaded style:
- Toon shading on everything: 2 or 3 hard shading bands per object, crisp dark outlines (inverted-hull or edge detection), flat colors from a small tasteful palette.
- A plain flat light background (soft off-white or pale gray), with a simple flat floor shadow under the cage.
- No bloom, no glow, no neon, no lens flares, no motion blur, no particle haze, no gradients, no transparency stacking. No visual artifacts: no z-fighting, no flickering outlines, no shadow acne, no aliasing (use antialiasing and a sensible pixel ratio).
- Impacts get small, flat cartoon "pop" marks that vanish quickly, not sparks.
- It should look like a clean animated illustration, not a tech demo.

Camera: a slow, smooth orbit by default, plus drag to orbit and scroll to zoom.

Sound: synthesize everything with the Web Audio API. Each collision makes a soft pitched tone based on ball size and impact speed, so it turns into gentle generative music as it gets chaotic. Breaking panels get their own sound. Keep it quiet and pleasant, never clipping.

UI: a small, minimal flat panel in the corner (no glassmorphism) with sliders for gravity, spin speed, bounciness and ball count, a "slow motion" toggle, a "reset" button, and an FPS counter. It must stay at 60fps with 300 balls on a laptop.

title: Real-time WebGPU soft-body kiwi jelly wedge demo
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build "Kiwi Jelly Wedge" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS, no libraries): a real-time WebGPU soft-body gummy kiwi wedge you can grab, stretch, lift and twist.
Object
One sixth of a thick kiwi slice: a pie-shaped wedge with 30° half-angle, radius ≈ 1.8 and thickness 0.56. Rounded corners (iq's exact pie SDF minus a rounding radius) and bevelled top/bottom edges.
Regions, measured from the tip in rest space:a cream core at the tip with a slightly lobed edge;
thin pale rays fanning out of the core every 2π/56, each with its own random brightness and length;
a darker, glassier ring around the seeds (blushes red in the Ruby variety);
bright juicy outer flesh with radial cell grain and a lighter band just under the skin;
a thin brown fuzzy skin on the arc wall.

Seeds:small flattened black teardrops, pointed end toward the core, in radial rows between the rays, at four depths;
the face layers break the cut surfaces like real seeds; the others float inside and show through the jelly;
wet glossy shading.

A few small air bubbles in the outer flesh.
Varieties: Green, Gold, Ruby.
Physics (XPBD tetrahedral soft body)
Mesh: 2D Delaunay of the rounded outline plus a hex lattice, extruded into prisms → tets.
Co-rotational per-tet shape matching (warm-started quaternion) plus volume constraints.
Stiffer skin and core tets; edge-velocity damping; floor contact with Coulomb friction.
Soft patch grab with bounded reach; scroll or a second finger twists the held patch.
Fixed 60 Hz step with 10 substeps; gentle settling.
Seeds and bubbles are separate meshes embedded in the tets by barycentric weights, so they ride with the flesh.
Rendering (WebGPU / WGSL)
Procedural photo-studio cyclorama with softboxes. Soft PCSS key shadow tinted green, plus contact AO from a top-down height map.
Seeds and bubbles are drawn in the scene pass. A back-face pass gives the view-ray thickness.
Jelly:refraction of the scene, with per-tap Beer–Lambert absorption by material (flesh, glassy seed ring, milky core and rays, opaque skin);
scattering, back-lit glow at thin edges, Fresnel studio reflections and GGX highlights;
a velvet sheen on the fuzzy skin;
sparse sugar glints in the flesh.

Post: exposure, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, sRGB, dither.
UI (editorial "Material Studies / No. 028", English)
Italic serif title "Kiwi / Jelly." with the caption "An emerald wedge. A halo of seeds. A gentle wobble."
Status pill "WEBGPU · LIVE".
Panel "The Specimen": variety chips (skin / core / flesh bands); Firmness ("trembling → set") and Internal damping ("lively → syrupy") sliders; Give it a nudge, Reset, Pause; ¼ speed and Show mesh.
Readouts: Mass (g, 1 unit ≈ 1.6 cm at 1.3 g/cm³), Volume (% of rest), Kinetic (µJ).
A collapsible "Inside the experiment" with notes on the method.
Fallback "This kiwi needs WebGPU." Stacked mobile layout with no horizontal scroll.

The result should feel like a sunlit storybook painting while still being a smooth, detailed real-time scene. Do not make it dark, crushed, noisy or visibly low-poly, and never a stained-glass look.  Include a large still lake ringed by natural deciduous trees with visible trunks and real branching, each crown an irregular layered mass of clustered autumn colour rather than a single sphere or cone on a stick, varied in height, some half-bare; a mallard hen leading a line of ducklings, several drakes with green heads and white neck rings, and one white farm duck, all leaving V-shaped wakes that spread and fade; ducks that paddle in smooth arcs toward wandering waypoints, tip tail-up to dabble, preen on a rock or the dock, splash gently if they bump, and never leave the water; cattails and reeds along the edges, lily pads in the shallows, a small wooden dock with a footbridge, a mossy log, a short stone path with a bench, and mushrooms at the tree roots; a heron standing in the shallows; dragonflies skimming the reeds; and leaves falling, spiralling down, settling on the water, drifting in rafts and pushed aside as a duck passes. Build every tree, bird and plant from geometry and materials in code; never hotlink a model or an image. Reflect the coloured trees softly on the water, broken by the leaves and the wakes.  Add slow cinematic motion: a high three-quarter camera that starts wide on the whole lake, pushes in and orbits closer over 25 to 30 seconds until the ducks and the near shore fill much more of the frame, then eases back out and repeats from a new angle, never dipping low and never showing the sky; a warm directional sun from the upper left throwing crisp shadows on the water and shore, with a soft ambient floor so no shadow is ever black; and a seamless loop with a little camera drift. title: Browser-based jelly peach with physics and material-studies UI
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a single-file WebGPU page "Peach Jelly" in the style of a "Material Studies" specimen sheet (light studio backdrop #E2DFDA, italic serif title, a specimen control panel on the right, live readouts bottom-left, collapsible "Inside the experiment" notes; responsive with a stacked phone layout and a no-WebGPU fallback card).

Subject: half a peach made of translucent jelly, cut along its suture, lying skin-down with the cut face up and its stone seated in the hollow.

Geometry: a signed distance field for the fruit — a sphere slightly longer from stem to blossom end, with a stem dimple, a faint point at the blossom tip and the suture crease along one side of the rim, belly gently flattened on the floor — cut at the equator, minus an almond-shaped hollow for the stone (flattened, broad faces parallel to the cut, blunt toward the stem). Simulation mesh: a snapped hex lattice, 5 tets per cell (~700 particles / ~2500 tets), node layers exactly on the floor and the cut face, nodes forced out of the stone. Render surface by surface nets, embedded in the tets by barycentric weights, with one normal-smoothing pass per frame so reflections don't pick out tet kinks. The stone gets its own high-resolution mesh: deep wormy furrows (mostly lengthwise) and little pits carved by displacement, a low keel round its edge, a small point at the blossom end; groove depth rides in the vertex material id for shading.

Physics (CPU, XPBD, 60 Hz, 10 substeps): per-tet co-rotational shape matching + volume constraints, stiffer skin, edge-relative damping, floor friction, pointer grab with twist. The stone is a rigid body (position, quaternion, ellipsoid inertia) with frictional contact against every particle and sampled floor contacts. Nodes lining the hollow are held by soft adhesion bonds that peel (floor of the hollow first, lip last) under a sustained net pull measured in the half's best-fit rigid frame — never from brief knocks; a loose stone resting in the hollow is drawn home and re-bonded with a soft grace period. Grabbing the stone moves it as a whole and it can be thrown. Buttons: nudge, reset, "Pop the stone" / "Put the stone back", pause, ¼ speed, show mesh; sliders for firmness and damping; readouts mass, volume %, grip %.

Rendering (WGSL): shadow map + top-down contact-AO map, scene pass (floor, stone, bubbles) with linear depth in alpha, back-face thickness pass, refracting jelly with Beer–Lambert absorption and scattering. Regions from rest-space SDFs: golden flesh; a ruby ring hugging the stone, broken up irregularly, with fine red fibres streaking out; the skin's blush bleeding a little way into the flesh. Skin: yellow with patchy red blush and pale flecks, a velvet sheen at grazing angles (nectarine: smooth and glossy). Stone: woody reddish-brown, dark furrows with shreds of red fibre, soft key shadows, low sheen. Varieties: Yellow, White, Nectarine. UI text in English.

title: Interactive miniature town where typed commands change the world
author: dominikmartn
prompt:
# Build an Interactive World Model Playground

Build a complete, working browser experience called **Small World**.

It is a beautifully rendered miniature town that people can change through natural language and direct interaction. The world responds through connected systems: pedestrians, traffic, weather, destinations, water, and lighting.

The central experience:

**Change one thing. Watch everything react.**

Act as the product designer, creative coder, simulation engineer, and art director. Make implementation decisions independently within the constraints below.

Implement the experience in the current environment. This is a request for functioning software, not a proposal, mockup, video, or implementation plan.

## 1. The creative premise

Imagine a meticulously designed architectural model that has come alive.

Tiny people have destinations. Cars travel between neighborhoods. A river passes through town. Bridges connect its banks. People visit the park and gather in the square.

Then the user types:

> “Start a festival in the park.”

A small stage and lights appear. People change destinations and begin converging on the park. Nearby paths become busier.

The user continues:

> “Now make it rain.”

Cloud shadows move across the town. Rain begins. Umbrellas appear. Festival visitors leave exposed areas and walk toward reachable shelters.

Then:

> “Close the north bridge.”

Barriers appear. Approaching vehicles stop and choose another route. Pedestrians change their paths. The longer crossing becomes busier.

**These are not separate visual effects. They are consequences unfolding inside the same persistent world.**

That connected behavior is the product.

The experience should be compelling as a silent screen recording, but remain genuinely interactive when someone uses it themselves.

## 2. Priorities and scope

Build one small, exceptionally polished world rather than a sprawling, incomplete city builder.

Prioritize, in this order:

1. A visually distinctive, living miniature.
2. Real, legible cause and effect.
3. Reliable language commands and direct interaction.
4. Smooth motion and immediate feedback.
5. A reproducible showcase sequence.

The required scope is one town and the six interventions described below.

Do not add accounts, multiplayer, a large procedural map generator, economic systems, extensive dashboards, or a general-purpose construction editor.

The town should feel like a carefully composed physical diorama, not a generic low-poly asset pack.

Create a compact landscape with:

- A river separating two neighborhoods.
- Two bridges, with visibly different alternative routes.
- Approximately 12–20 buildings with varied silhouettes.
- A park, a small market square, and a riverside parking lot.

title: Interactive jelly hammerhead shark physics study

prompt: Make an interactive WebGPU soft-body study of a great hammerhead shark cast in two layers of jelly, resting on its belly in a soft photo studio. Give it an oversized cephalofoil — a wide, flat hammer whose span is about 40% of the body length, with a nearly straight front edge, a small notch in the middle, ends swept slightly back, full and round at the front and thinning toward the back, with a large glossy eye at each tip. Simulate it as an XPBD tetrahedral mesh (snapped hex lattice, co-rotational elasticity, volume preservation, floor friction), with firmer fins. Let the user grab and stretch the jelly, twist with the scroll wheel or a second finger, drop beads of jelly bait, and switch between three colourways (steel, amber, gummy blue). title: 15-second orange-dot motion design reel with typography and
author: ultimaxbt
prompt:
opus 5.5 is insane as a motion designer

this 15-second video turns one orange dot into an entire motion system

toggle → typography → spring graph → shape morph → kinetic type → halftone → end card

here's the prompt to recreate the idea ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for: a short label for the opening toggle, one hero word, a percentage for the graph, the text for the final card, one accent color, and a track with a clear beat.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 2D motion design film in 16:9. Use a warm off-white canvas, near-black backgrounds, bold typography and one vivid orange accent. The orange dot connects every scene: it starts in the UI, becomes the dot over a letter, traces a spring graph, grows into a shape and returns on the end card. A cursor makes the opening click feel real. Keep the motion sharp and controlled, with small spring overshoots and no dead time.
Banned: stock footage, gradients, glows, particle bursts, random transitions and motion that isn't connected to an element already on screen.
</direction>

<structure>
Around 15 seconds, with a visual change on every major beat.
Open: a cursor clicks the orange toggle beside "Reduce Motion". The letters bend and move into place until only "Motion" remains, with the orange dot above the "i".
Spring: the dot jumps away from the word and lands on a graph. Its path draws a spring response, overshoots the target and settles beside a "+22%" callout.
Shape: the dot shoots across a line, grows into an orange circle and fills the frame. A black rounded square rotates inside it, then stretches into a pill. The scene contracts to a single orange dot on black.
Type: words like "SPRINGS", "EASING", "KINETIC TYPE", "3D" and "SOUND" orbit the dot. The circle of type opens out into a field of tiny dots.
Reveal: the halftone field expands and flips to black, revealing the final card: "Opus 5.5", "Motion designer." and "0 keyframes".
Return: the orange dot moves back through the halftone, graph and toggle. Match the final frame to the first so the video loops cleanly.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1920x1080 at 60fps. Compute every visual from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form springs for the toggle, bouncing dot and graph. Draw the graph from the same spring function that moves the dot.
3. Animate letters individually for the "Reduce Motion" to "Motion" transformation. Keep the orange dot attached to the "i" until it begins its jump.
4. Make the orange circle, rotating square and pill different states of the same shape. Preserve its position and motion through each transformation.
5. Place the orbiting words along a circular path, then move their letters outward to hand the frame over to the halftone grid.
6. Draw the halftone as a grid of dots whose sizes respond to the orange dot. Let it grow past the frame edges before revealing the end card.
7. Sync the click, dot landing, graph peak, shape changes and final title to measured beats. Render one frame per beat to check the pacing before the full export.
</build>

<gotchas>
The graph and dot must follow the same motion or the spring will feel fake. Keep the orange accent consistent across every scene. Give outgoing and incoming text separate timing so letters don't overlap. When a shape fills the screen, scale it past all four corners. Match the cursor, dot and typography in the first and last frames to avoid a loop stutter.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and four stills (toggle, graph, kinetic type, end card) before building the full video.

title: Morphing journey from creature to cosmos
author: leo_xiaolei
prompt:
Opus 5.5 直出，秀到飞边子了！我愿称之为最强！！！

参考提示词如下（温馨提示额度消耗和耗时会有点大）：

你现在是 Claude Opus 5.5，作为资深创意编程工程师（Creative Coder）、动态设计师（Motion Designer）与前端动画工程师。
你的任务是复现我所提供的参考视频中的视觉语言、节奏律动、转场逻辑以及整体氛围质感。
核心目标不是做一个常规网页。
核心目标是使用代码构建一部全程序化生成、具备电影质感且能够自动播放的动画短片。
最终成片应呈现出精致的手作动态设计（Motion Design）质感，而非一堆网页组件的拼接。
1. 项目目标
基于参考视频，构建一部时长 25–30 秒的程序化动画短片。
整段动画需串联多个视觉意象：
可爱角色
→ 神经元 / 电流脉冲结构
→ 三棱镜与彩虹色散
→ 几何色彩构型
→ 向日葵
→ 螺旋星系
→ 黑洞
→ 宇宙隧道
→ 地球升起（地出）
→ 回归角色
最核心的要求：
绝对不要做成互相割裂的幻灯片切换。
每一个场景都必须自然地在视觉上形变过渡至下一个场景。
运用手段包括：
形状渐变（Morphing）
粒子过渡（Particle transitions）
缩放过渡（Scale transitions）
镜头推进（Camera pushes）
径向展开过渡（Radial transitions）
溶解渗透（Dissolves）
实体到实体的几何形变（Object-to-object transformations）
色彩连续性（Color continuity）
运动动量延续（Motion continuity）
整部动画应当呈现为一次连贯流动的“意识流”。
2. 技术栈
技术选用：
Vite
TypeScript
HTML Canvas 2D
requestAnimationFrame
确定性时间轴系统（Deterministic timeline system）
程序化图形生成（Procedural graphics）
可复用的场景模块
仅在对以下视觉实现有实质性帮助时，才允许引入 Three.js：
星系
黑洞
地球
镜头景深
切勿无端引入重型依赖库。
除非有不可替代的理由，否则避免使用 React。
这是一项动画短片工程，而非 UI 应用。
3. 画布参数设定
设计基准分辨率：1920 × 1080
画面宽高比：16:9
目标帧率：30 FPS
动画必须支持自适应响应式缩放，同时严格保持 16:9 的设计坐标系。
必须正确处理 devicePixelRatio，确保动画在高分屏（Retina / High-DPI）上清晰锐利。
4. 视觉风格
参考范本具有插画风科普动画的质感。
目标视觉特征：
手绘质感
微带瑕疵的不规则形状
细微的线条抖动感（Line wobble）
柔和的肌理纹理
有机自然而非机械生硬的几何体
灵动俏皮却不失高级感
干净通透的构图
清晰鲜明的剪影造型
克制但极具表现力的配色方案
避免出现：
泛滥的通用 SaaS 插画风
扁平化企业图标感
冗余的 UI 界面元素
拟真写实风格（Photorealism）
赛博朋克美学
过度的霓虹光污染
千篇一律的 AI 生成式渐变
带有素材库库感的素材
5. 配色导向
主背景色：
暖奶油色 / 米白色
例如：#F2E8CF
深色宇宙场景：
深海蓝
暗紫色
近乎纯黑的夜空蓝
点缀高光色：
橙色
向日葵黄
紫罗兰
青色
洋红
柔红
克制且克制地使用渐变色。
色彩在不同场景间应保持过渡流动，而非突兀瞬变。
6. 肌理与质感
生成细腻的程序化纸张质感。
可选实现路径：
低透明度的随机噪点
背景亮度的细微不均
轻微的颗粒感叠加层（Grain overlay）
质感需清晰可感知，但绝不能喧宾夺主。
禁止加载体积庞大的纸张实拍贴图资源。
尽量全部采用程序化计算生成。
7. 动画时间轴
搭建统一的中控时间轴系统。
时间参考规划：
0.0s – 4.0s：角色登场
4.0s – 7.5s：神经元 / 电流脉冲网络
7.5s – 10.0s：三棱镜 / 光线色散
10.0s – 13.5s：色彩几何 → 向日葵
13.5s – 17.0s：向日葵 → 螺旋星系
17.0s – 20.5s：星系 → 黑洞
20.5s – 23.5s：黑洞 → 宇宙隧道 / 光柱
23.5s – 27.0s：地出（Earth Rise）
27.0s – 30.0s：回归角色
以上时间分配非死板硬性规定，若有助于增强视觉韵律与节奏感，可按需微调。
8. 场景 01 — 角色
时长： 约 0–4 秒。
绘制一个简洁可爱的矩形橙色小生物。
特征：
圆角矩形身体
小短腿
极简的面部特征
轻微不对称的手绘轮廓线条
亲和灵动的性格表现
动画细节：
小生物从画外缓缓走向画面中央。
行走动画需包含：
身体起伏颠簸（Bounce）
双腿交替摆动
轻微的身体倾角晃动
细腻的挤压与拉伸（Squash and stretch）
避免机械僵硬的匀速运动。
充分应用缓动曲线（Easing）与次级跟随动作（Secondary motion）。
场景尾声：
小生物对身旁浮现的事物产生反应。
该反应动作将直接触发下一阶段的转场。
9. 角色 → 神经元转场
不要生硬剪辑。
过渡方案：
角色身旁亮起一个微小的光点。
光点逐渐扩散放大。
细小的分支线开始从中抽枝蔓延。
镜头向前推近。
在逐渐膨胀铺展的网络对比下，角色身形显现得越来越小。
最终，神经元脉络结构铺满整个屏幕。
10. 场景 02 — 神经网络
时长： 约 4–7.5 秒。
具象化一种介于以下元素之间的视觉形态：
神经元 / 生物电 / 分支生物形态 / 闪电脉冲。
使用程序化分形/分支算法生成。
节点伴随脉冲呼吸。
信号流沿各个分支游走传导。
要求：
动态电脉冲流动
有机自然的分支几何体
微小的飞溅火花粒子
线条粗细富于节奏变化
兼具可控的随机感
切勿做成千篇一律的机器学习拓扑网络拓扑图。
它应当充满生物活力与能量感。
11. 神经元 → 三棱镜转场
选中其中一条极为明亮的电脉冲分支。
让这条分支逐渐拉直伸展。
流动其中的能量凝聚为一束纯净的白色光束。
神经网络的其余部分逐渐消隐在暗色背景中。
白光光束横穿画面。
精准投射射入一座三角形三棱镜。
12. 场景 03 — 三棱镜
时长： 约 7.5–10 秒。
绘制一个手绘透明感的三棱镜。
白光自一侧射入。
经三棱镜折射并色散为：
红、橙、黄、绿、青、蓝、紫。
不要只画死板固定的彩虹线。
需制作动态效果：
光束到达的冲击动态
三棱镜受光泛出的辉光
色散铺开的过程
细微的折射光线游移
柔和的光晕泛光（Bloom）
展开的光谱将作为承接后续画面的关键转场媒介。
13. 三棱镜 → 色彩几何
折射出的彩虹光束发生弯曲。
逐步转化为同心圆弧。
圆弧相互嵌套，化作多层旋转的同心圆环。
镜头向视觉中心推近。
三棱镜自然消隐退出视野。
14. 场景 04 — 色彩光环
时长： 约 10–11.5 秒。
构建层层嵌套的彩色同心圆环。
运动方式：
缓慢旋转
正反方向交错旋转
微弱的呼吸式缩放
有机微动的抖动摆动（Wobble）
圆环线条需带有轻微的手作不完美质感。
避免数学上绝对冷硬工整的圆周。
15. 光环 → 向日葵
缓慢改变圆环的几何拓扑结构。
外侧圆环渐变分离为独立的花瓣。
中心圆环转化为密布的向日葵葵花籽花盘。
黄色逐渐占据视觉主导。
整个演化形变过程需清晰可见。
避免使用透明度淡入淡出（Crossfade）的偷懒手法。
让观者能够直观看到一种几何形态如何演变为另一种生命形态。
16. 场景 05 — 向日葵
时长： 约 11.5–14 秒。
生成一朵风格化的程序化向日葵。
视觉构成：
明亮的金黄花瓣
温暖橙黄的花心
深色螺旋状排列的花籽
隐约可见的纤细花茎或植物形态
动画表现：
花瓣舒展盛放
轻柔的生命呼吸感
整体微微旋转
籽粒螺旋排列运动
若条件允许，葵花籽可采用斐波那契数列 / 黄金角分布算法生成。
17. 向日葵 → 螺旋星系
这将是整部短片视觉张力最强的转场之一。
向日葵中心加速旋转。
外围花瓣逐渐剥离脱散。
每一片花瓣解构为一颗发光的星尘粒子。
中心的花籽阵列向外螺旋扩张。
色调柔和渐次推移：
黄色
→ 橙色
→ 紫色
→ 深蓝
整朵向日葵无缝蜕变为一座旋转的旋涡星系。
切忌使用简单的画面叠化淡出。
18. 场景 06 — 螺旋星系
时长： 约 14–17 秒。
构建一座程序化生成的旋涡星系。
要求：
在性能允许的前提下布置成千上万个微型粒子
采用对数螺线 / 旋臂分布规律
极度明亮致密的星系核心
错落点缀的背景繁星
呈现深邃的空间纵深感
镜头缓慢向前推进
整体缓慢转动
粒子需拥有丰富的透明度梯次与大小半径。
避免机械匀质的死板星点分布。
使用带有固定种子（Seeded Random）的随机算法，确保每次播放呈现的画面细节完全一致。
19. 星系 → 黑洞
星系中心区域的自转角速度逐渐加快。
中央区域急剧暗沉塌缩。
周围粒子开始加速环绕运转。
沿切线方向将运动的粒子微微拉伸拖尾。
中央的纯黑视界向外扩张。
整个星系逐步转化为狂暴的吸积盘。
20. 场景 07 — 黑洞
时长： 约 17–20.5 秒。
构建一座风格化的黑洞。
要素：
吞噬一切的纯黑球体核心
炽热发光的吸积盘
橙金交织的内层强光
紫蓝晕染的外围辉光
沿弯曲引力轨迹运动的粒子流
可选实现：做近似引力透镜效果的视觉扭曲。
无需苛求物理层面上严格精确的广义相对论模拟。
以呈现上乘的视觉美感为第一优先级。
镜头向视界面缓慢平稳推近。
21. 黑洞 → 宇宙隧道
镜头彻底穿透坠入中心黑暗。
吸积盘受透视拉伸拉长为同心光环。
周围星尘被径向拉伸成向外散射的放射线。
营造出跃入时空隧道的穿梭沉浸感。
22. 场景 08 — 宇宙隧道
时长： 约 20.5–23.5 秒。

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: twoclipping
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (nightshift) (one lowercase word, it becomes a black wordmark with a period), the one job a user hands it before bed (book 10 sales calls this week), the three results it reports by morning (200 leads found / 200 emails sent / 10 calls booked), two photos of the same place at night and by day (aligned, so a crossfade reads as a real sunrise), one sunny daytime photo for outside the logo, and a song with a big hit near its start. If I skip any, use the defaults.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 24 second square product launch video, 1440x1440 at 60fps, 2D only, one continuous take that loops. The whole video happens inside the period of the wordmark. Outside it's daytime (the sunny photo behind a black wordmark). Inside it's the night photo under iOS-style glass panels (the blurred photo behind each panel, a tint, a rim light). Nothing cuts: every scene grows out of the last, shapes morph, dots fly, colours change under floods. Every morph glides 0.8s on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1) and the camera zoom rides the same curve. Geist, the real macOS pointer, soft shadows that grow with each shape's height.
Banned: flat or gradient backgrounds made in code, camera zooms into tiny points, hard cuts, crossfades between scenes, bouncy springs, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, cropped type.
</direction>

<structure>
Beats are the song's. The song enters on its big hit as the first pill appears.
Open: the letters slide into the period and vanish into it while it glides to the middle. The period opens like an iris onto the night inside it, and "you log off at 6", then "[product] doesn't", roll through one mask line over the night photo.
Ask: a glass "Ask [product]" pill springs in. The cursor clicks it, it glides into an input and the job types out.
Find: send shrinks the input to a dot that ripples into a 23x15 grid. A scan line sweeps it, 200 dots light up and a counter counts them.
Write: the lit dots pour into a glass email composer. A second, purple cursor labelled "[product]" types a personal opener and presses Send, and the counter runs to 200/200.
Night: the composer becomes a glass orb with a progress ring. A clock chip swaps 11:42 PM, 3:17 AM, 5:02 AM, 6:59 AM while the sky relights from night to dawn and "while you sleep" rolls in.
Results (beat 20): the orb turns black and goo-splits into the three result pills. The checks pop green.
Morning: the pills merge into a Dynamic Island that grows into a phone lock screen: the day photo, the date, a big 7:00, the bezel growing out of the screen edge. Three glass notifications stack in, and the cursor taps the first, which opens like iOS.
Proof: a week calendar (10 meetings pop in, a hover shows one's time), then a pipeline chart ($48,200 counts up, the line draws, a hover follows it). A black flood from the line's end becomes "Start your night shift →" and the cursor clicks it.
Out: the button shrinks into a dot, the whole scene closes down into it like an iris, and the letters slide back out of the period. The tagline rises. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Everything is a pure function of time inside seek(t): no timers, no state between frames.
2. One element morphs through every state (size, radius, colour, material) from a table of beat times, so retiming is one edit.
3. Render the inside world into an offscreen canvas and reveal it through the period with a circular mask. Never zoom the camera into the dot.
4. Glass: a pre-blurred copy of the photo clipped to the shape, then a tint and a gradient rim.
5. Goo: blur + alpha threshold on an offscreen layer for the split and the merge.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event, each placed by its measured peak. The song enters on its hit. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 4 motion-blur subframes. Scan every frame for single-frame jumps and fix each one.
</build>

<gotchas>
A camera zoom into an off-centre dot swings sideways and spikes, so open the dot instead. Ease a closing iris by area, not radius, or its first frames jump. A helper that sets globalAlpha must restore the caller's, or fading cards pop. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's, or the digits smear.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, find, write, results, phone, out) before you render.
</start>

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: twoclipping
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a voiceover or song with a spoken line (the audio file) and its transcript, 10-12 small objects that sum up my life, two silhouettes to light like a heat camera (a head in profile and a raised hand), and the 3 words I want to land hardest. If I skip any, use the defaults: vinyl, book, camera, cat, coin, game controller, cap, heart, money, plant, clapperboard, skateboard; free CC0 silhouettes from Openverse; action, intention, curiosity.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 20 second 4:3 film, 1440x1080 at 60fps, cut to the voice. Off-white paper, black, one red, one yellow, Geist for every word. Film grain on everything, a soft vignette, and a camera that never rests: a slow handheld float under everything plus a slow push inside every scene.
No scene cuts to the next: each handoff starts on the exact last frame of the scene before. The only hard cuts are the beat flips on the last word.
Every object is pixel art you draw yourself: a 16x16 grid per object, every cell a hand-placed colour, rendered as a 3D block (a darker extrusion down-right, a thin bevel on every cell) with a soft contact shadow.
The silhouettes are lit like a heat camera: the heat comes from how thick the body is at each point, so the nose, the hair and the fingertips run cooler, plus one hotspot and a slow moving noise, mapped through a black > red > orange > cream ramp. The edge stays razor sharp, with a soft glow outside it.
Motion rules: nothing pops in (eased glides of about 0.5s with a soft start), fast moves get real motion blur instead of ghost copies, and captions type with the voice behind a block cursor.
Banned: stock footage, AI video, 3D camera moves, particles, glitch.
</direction>

<structure>
Hang every scene on the transcript's word timings (measure them with faster-whisper word timestamps, one short chunk at a time):
1. The first word fills a yellow card. The card wipes off to the left and the question types underneath on two centred lines that glide to stay centred as they grow, the key word underlined in red as it's spoken.
2. The objects streak past in lanes above and below the words, a cyan four-point flare sweeps in, then the page burns away: black closes in from the edges onto the head, behind a hot red edge.
3. The head heats up on black while the answer types low on the left. A thin white orbit draws itself around the head, its far half passing behind it. On the last word, paper blooms out from inside the head with the objects in it, and the camera falls through: the head rushes past the lens until the paper is all we see.
4. The objects sit on a tilted ring seen in perspective (the front ones bigger and lower, drawn last), slowly turning, each one bobbing; the coin flips and lands with sparks.
5. On each of the 3 words, that object flies out of the ring to the left and grows, the page floods black from it, and the word types beside it (camera: a red shutter star; book: a red ribbon sweep; record: two white orbits and red notes). Then the flood drains back into the object as it flies home, and the camera dives closer into the ring. Put each hero object in the slot that is front-left when its word lands.
6. The ring pulls in a touch, bursts outward, every object turns to ink, and ink blots grow and swallow the page.
7. The hand rises into frame, hot, with the line split either side of it. The heart drops into its palm, then lifts to the centre at the size the next scene holds it.
8. The last word, one letter per beat, the background flipping paper / black / red, the heart holding its place across the cut, the centre object morphing pixel by pixel into the next one.
9. Thin brush strokes sweep through, the letters drift apart and float, then settle back into the word with the heart above it. The camera keeps pushing through the hold.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. Bake each pixel sprite once to an offscreen canvas (the extrusion layers, then the face), then draw it scaled and rotated.
3. The heat: precompute each silhouette's base heat once (a distance transform of the mask, held at the edge value outside it so nothing dark bleeds in when it is upscaled). Every frame, add the hotspot and two octaves of value noise at quarter resolution, map it through a 256-step lookup, upscale it, and cut it with the full-resolution mask.
4. The fall through the head: draw the ring scene into an offscreen layer, mask it with the head scaled up about a point inside the skull, and grow that scale on a cubed curve until the head covers the frame. The ring inside zooms less than the head does, so it reads as depth.
5. The pixel morph: pair every cell of object A with a cell of object B and glide each one's position and colour, with a small random delay per cell.
6. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 8 motion-blur subframes, then lay the original audio back on with ffmpeg.
</build>

<gotchas>
A mask PNG with no alpha channel fills the whole box with heat, so put the silhouette in the alpha. A limb cut by the photo's border shows as a straight edge, so extend the mask past the frame. A handoff only reads as smooth when the last frame of one scene is the first frame of the next: draw the outgoing scene under the transition, and give scenes that show the same ring one shared zoom function. A flood that's still retreating when the next scene starts reads as a hard cut, so let it finish first. A fast ease-out flood reads as a jump; use a soft start.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, measure the word timings, then show me 8 stills before you render.
</start>

title: Explainer video of 9 football rules
author: lukasersil
prompt:
Postav mi video, které vysvětluje pravidla sportu stylem televizní analýzy s AR grafikou. Bez AI video modelů a bez stahování assetů: 3D scénu, postavy, textury, grafiku i zvuk vytvoř kódem. Pracuj samostatně a průběžně mi ukazuj kontrolní snímky.

## Parametry (pro jiný sport změň tuhle sekci a sekci Scénář)
- Sport: fotbal
- Pravidla (9): ofsajd, faul, pokutový kop, vhazování, rohový kop + kop od branky, hra rukou, přímý volný kop, žlutá a červená karta, gól (celý míč za čarou)
- Jazyk všech textů: čeština (plná diakritika, desetinná čárka)
- Délka: cca 68 s (úvod ~4,5 s, každé pravidlo 6 až 8 s, závěr ~4 s)
- Formát: 1920×1080, 30 fps, MP4 (H.264 + AAC)
- Styl postav: PS2 éra ve stylu GTA San Andreas (low-poly tvarované tělo, ručně malované textury)
- Týmy: Červení (červený dres s bílými lemy, bílé trenky), Modří (královsky modrý dres, tmavě modré trenky), rozhodčí černý s limetkovými lemy, brankáři zelený a fialový

## Technologie a pipeline
- Three.js (npm). index.html obsahuje WebGL canvas 1920×1080 a nad ním DOM vrstvu pro HUD.
- Deterministická funkce `window.renderFrame(t)`: stav scény i HUD je čistá funkce času, žádný stav mezi snímky.
- `render.mjs`: lokální statický HTTP server + puppeteer-core se systémovým Chrome (headless, na Macu `--use-angle=metal`). Pro každý snímek zavolej renderFrame(t), počkej 2× requestAnimationFrame, udělej JPEG screenshot a pošli ho rourou do ffmpeg (libx264, CRF 18, yuv420p). Režimy: `stills t1 t2 …` (PNG na kontrolu), `video`, `info` (zapíše časovou osu do out/timeline.json).
- Cesty řeš přes fileURLToPath (složky s mezerami v názvu).
- WebGLRenderer s `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`, ACES tone mapping, PCF soft shadows. EffectComposer s MSAA (samples 4, HalfFloat): RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, vlastní grade pass (vinětace, jemné zrno, chromatická aberace, záblesk, whip blur, VHS efekt), OutputPass.
- Zvuk: Python (numpy + scipy) syntetizuje celý soundtrack do WAV, ffmpeg ho přimíchá (AAC 192k).
- Výstupy: plná kvalita + webová verze (CRF 23 až 24, maxrate 10M).

## Struktura projektu
src/util.js (easing, tmap pro freeze a zpomalení, track() pro pohyb hráčů po časovaných waypointech s fází běhu podle uražené vzdálenosti, seeded rng), src/world.js, src/player.js, src/ar.js, src/hud.js, src/grade.js, src/segments.js, src/main.js, render.mjs, https://audio.py/, PROGRESS.md (průběžně zapisuj, co je hotové a jak se to pouští, ať se dá navázat po přerušení).

## Svět
- Hřiště 105×68 m. Tráva jako canvas textura (pruhy po 5,25 m, šum, skvrny) + dlaždicová detail textura přes onBeforeCompile. Čáry jako ostrá geometrie, ne textura. Vnější hrana čar = hranice hřiště.
- Branky se sítí (LineSegments), rohové praporky.
- Stadion: dvoupatrová mísa podle superelipsy, dav jako canvas textura lidí v řadách, LED pás mezi patry, střecha s žebry, řady reflektorů na hraně střechy (emisivní, bloom), vnější fasáda s osvětlenými okny, noční obloha, světla města kolem, tmavá zem.
- LED mantinely kolem hřiště s českými nápisy (PRAVIDLA FOTBALU, RESPEKT, FAIR PLAY, ZNEJ PRAVIDLA, #PRAVIDLAFOTBALU), pomalu se posouvají.
- Světla: 4 směrová světla z rohů střechy se stíny (shadow kamera zaostřená na akci daného segmentu), hemisférické světlo, jemná mlha.
- Analytický grade: do všech materiálů světa vlož přes onBeforeCompile sdílený uniform uFreeze (odbarvení do chladné šedozelené + ztmavení). AR materiály ho nemají, takže při zastaveném obrazu zůstanou syté.

## Postavy (styl GTA San Andreas)
- Hierarchický rig: root → body (pánev) → trup → hlava a ramena → lokty, kyčle → kolena → kotníky. Póza = sada úhlů (náklon a rotace trupu, flexe a abdukce ramen, lokty, kyčle, kolena, kotníky, náklon těla, výskok).
- Geometrie: trup jako LatheGeometry (široká ramena, užší pas), zúžené končetiny, klouby jako koule, dlaň s palcem, kopačka s podrážkou a zúženou špičkou, tvarovaná hlava (užší brada), nos, uši, vlasy jako slupka (krátké, objemné, ježek, holá hlava).
- Ručně malované canvas textury: obličej (oči s duhovkou a odleskem, obočí, stín nosu, rty, tváře, strniště nebo vousy, vlasová linie), dres (V-výstřih, boční pruhy, znak, sponzor, jméno a velké číslo na zádech, vrásky látky), rukávy, trenky s číslem, štulpny s pruhy.
- Každý hráč jiný: pleť, vlasy, účes, oči, vousy, barva kopaček, postava. Česká jména na zádech (NOVÁK, DVOŘÁK, RŮŽIČKA…).
- Procedurální běh (fáze z uražené vzdálenosti, ať nohy nekloužou) + knihovna póz: kop (nápřah, úder, dokopnutí), skluz, zakopnutí a pád, vhazování, výskok s paží nad hlavou, zvednutá karta, postoj ve zdi, výskok zdi, robinzonáda brankáře, hlava dolů.
- Zvýraznění: obrysová slupka (inverted hull, tloušťka podle vzdálenosti od kamery), průsvitný hologram „ducha“ pro naznačení restartu, rozsvícení paže.

## AR grafika (additive blending, depthWrite false, kreslí se postupně přes progress)
GroundLine (zářící čára na zemi), Curtain (svislá rovina: ofsajd, branková a postranní čára), GroundRing (prstenec nebo disk s pulzem, čárkováním a výsečí, třeba kruh 9,15 m), Area (vyplněné území s okrajem a skenem), Trail (trubice trajektorie míče), GroundArrow (šipka s běžícími chevrony), Marker (zaměřovač kontaktu), Beam (světelný sloup), ScanGrid (skenovací mřížka), Segment3D (měřicí úsečky), Silhouette (válec obrysu těla).
Barvy: tyrkysová = měření, červená = přestupek, jantarová = míč a území, zelená = platné rozhodnutí.
DŮLEŽITÉ: shadery musí být NaN-safe (clamp UV, žádné pow ze záporného čísla). MSAA na hranách extrapoluje UV a NaN se v bloomu rozleje do černých bloků přes půl obrazu.

## HUD (DOM, styl sportovního přenosu)
- Logo vlevo nahoře „PRAVIDLA FOTBALU / AR ANALÝZA ZÁPASU“ + počítadlo „01 / 09“.
- Vpravo nahoře stav (ŽIVĚ, ZÁZNAM, ZPOMALENĚ ×0,6, STOP · AR, PŘETÁČENÍ ◀◀, KONEC ZÁPASU) a herní čas.
- Lower third vlevo dole: číslo pravidla, název, jednověté vysvětlení, ukazatel postupu z 9 dílků.
- Panel rozhodnutí vpravo dole v barvě rozhodnutí (OFSAJD, PENALTA, GÓL…) s podtitulkem.
- Při zastavení obrazu: záblesk, rohové závorky, štítek „ZASTAVENÝ OBRAZ · AR ANALÝZA“, krátký technický řádek dole.
- AR štítky ukotvené na 3D bod (projekce kamerou) s odkazovou čarou. Drž je v bezpečné zóně (ne pod spodní grafikou, ne pod logem) a nesmí se překrývat.
- Velká grafika karty (žlutá a červená) s důvody, úvodní titulek, závěr „TEĎ ZNÁŠ PRAVIDLA.“ s mřížkou 9 pravidel, stinger přechod (šikmé pruhy navy, tyrkysová, bílá + logo) na každém střihu.
- Čitelnost: minimální velikosti (název pravidla 66 px, popis 29 px, štítek 33 px + podtitulek 21 px, technický řádek 22 px). Text vždy na tmavém podkladu, krátké texty. Line-height aspoň 1,05, aby diakritika (Ž, Č, Ř) nebyla oříznutá. Titulky neodhaluj maskou, vypadá to jako ořez: použij fade + rozostření + lehký zoom.
- Fonty: systémové s českou diakritikou (na macOS DIN Condensed + Avenir Next Condensed). Pokrytí znaků ověř předem přes fc-query.

## Scénář (vnitřní časy segmentů, natažení na čtení viz další sekce)
Úvod (3,5 s): dron sjíždí z noční oblohy přes střechu do stadionu na široký záběr středu hřiště. Skenovací mřížka přejede hřiště, pod hráči naskočí kroužky, štítek „MÍČ SLEDOVÁN“. Titulek „PRAVIDLA FOTBALU“, nad ním „TV ANALÝZA PRAVIDEL“, pod ním „9 KLÍČOVÝCH PRAVIDEL · AR ANALÝZA“.
1. Ofsajd: televizní kamera, Červený #8 přihrává, zastavení v okamžiku přihrávky. Kamera se přesune do osy ofsajdové linie. Tyrkysová rovina u nejzazší části těla předposledního obránce (Modrý #4), červená u předsunutého kolena útočníka (Červený #9), měření „+1,59 m“ (spočítej z kloubů, paže se nepočítají). Rozhodnutí OFSAJD: nepřímý volný kop, Modří.
2. Faul: záznam ×0,6 nízko u trávníku. Modrý #10 vede míč, Červený #6 jde skluzem zezadu do kotníku. Zastavení v okamžiku kontaktu: zaměřovač „KONTAKT“, „MÍSTO FAULU“ (kruh + sloup), šipka dráhy skluzu, červený obrys. Kamera obkrouží, pak pád. FAUL: přímý volný kop.
3. Penalta: Červený #9 ve vápně, Modrý #3 ho podrazí. Zastavení, jeřáb nahoru. Zvýraznění pokutového území, oblouk z místa faulu na pokutovou značku s drátěným míčem, „11 m“. PENALTA.
4. Vhazování: přihrávka Červeného #2 přejede postranní čáru (trajektorie se kreslí živě). Zastavení až ve chvíli, kdy je celý míč venku, střih na kameru za čarou. Červená rovina, „+15 cm“, „CELÝ MÍČ VENKU“, „POSLEDNÍ DOTEK · ČERVENÝ #2“, modrá šipka do hřiště a hologram modrého hráče s míčem nad hlavou. VHAZOVÁNÍ (Modří).
5. Roh + kop od branky: střela Červeného #10 tečovaná Modrým #4 za brankovou čáru → ROHOVÝ KOP. Pak efekt přetáčení (VHS) a stejná střela bez teče → KOP OD BRANKY (zvýrazněné brankové území).
6. Hra rukou: střela, Modrý #5 ve výskoku s paží nad ramenem, míč do předloktí. Paže zčervená, ramenní linie, čára paže „ÚHEL PAŽE 135°“, průsvitný válec „OBRYS TĚLA“. RUKA: přímý volný kop.
7. Volný kop: zeď na 8,00 m „ZEĎ MOC BLÍZKO“, nakreslí se kruh 9,15 m, zeď ustoupí, číslo naběhne na 9,15 m a zezelená. Kamera za exekutora, zahraný oblouk přes zeď zpomaleně, zastavení „PŘES ZEĎ“. PŘÍMÝ VOLNÝ KOP.
8. Karty: detail rozhodčího se žlutou kartou proti hráči se svěšenou hlavou + velká grafika ŽLUTÁ KARTA / NAPOMENUTÍ se 3 důvody. Střih, červená karta, vyloučený odchází + ČERVENÁ KARTA / VYLOUČENÍ.
9. Gól: střela, brankář vyrazí, míč padá na čáru. Kamera u brankové čáry. První zastavení: polovina míče na čáře, červená rovina, „−11 cm“, „ZATÍM NENÍ GÓL“. Míč se dokutálí. Druhé zastavení: celý míč za čarou, rovina zezelená, „+3 cm“, blesky foťáků v hledišti. GÓL.
Závěr (2,5 s): kamera stoupá nad hřiště (návrat k úvodnímu záběru), mřížka, „TEĎ ZNÁŠ PRAVIDLA.“ + mřížka 9 pravidel, stmívačka.

Každé zastavení obrazu: krátký záblesk, odbarvení scény, kamera se dál pomalu hýbe kolem zmrazených hráčů, AR prvky naskakují postupně. Mezi segmenty vždy stinger.

## Čas na čtení
Akce (běh, kopy, skluzy) běží ve skutečné rychlosti. Analytické části každého segmentu natáhni 1,5× až 2,1× přes warp funkci (výstupní čas → vnitřní čas segmentu), aby každé pravidlo bylo na obrazovce 6 až 8 s a všechny texty se daly v klidu přečíst. `node render.mjs info` exportuje výslednou časovou osu do out/timeline.json.

## Zvuk (procedurální, https://audio.py/)
120 BPM broadcast groove (kopák, virbl, hi-haty, basa se sidechainem, arpeggio, pad), riser v úvodu, závěrečný akord. Při zastaveném obrazu hudba ztlumená low-passem. Dav (filtrovaný šum s vlněním, řev při gólu), whoosh + boom na každém střihu, kovový úder na každém zastavení, krátké „razítko“ při rozhodnutí, píšťalka, kopy do míče, zvuk přetáčení. Časy všech zvuků načti z out/timeline.json, ať sedí na obraz i po změně délky. Cílová hlasitost kolem −14 LUFS.

## Postup práce a kontrola
1. Nejdřív rozjeď pipeline (server, render, ffmpeg) s jednou scénou a ověř, že WebGL v headless Chrome běží.
2. Po každé změně vyrenderuj kontrolní snímky v klíčových časech a prohlédni je, včetně výřezů na 100 % kvůli textu a diakritice.
3. Celé video kontroluj přes kontaktní listy (ffmpeg filtr tile) a snímky kolem přechodů.
4. Hotové video ověř dekódováním (`ffmpeg -v error -i video.mp4 -f null -`) a délku a stopy přes ffprobe.
5. Do PROGRESS.md průběžně zapisuj, co je hotové a jakými příkazy se to pouští.

■ CADデータ
- 【題材】をイメージした配置図・平面図・立面図をDXFで作図（単位mm、表題欄つき）
- 3Dモデル（OBJ/STL/3D DXF）は不要

■ 動画（Blender 4.2、1920×1080、24fps、約20秒）
1. 冒頭：和紙の巻物が上から広がり、墨で描かれた配置図が現れる（題字・落款つき）
2. 図面の線が墨のワイヤーフレームとして立体に立ち上がる
3. 基壇→柱→壁→屋根→装飾の順に肉付けされ、線は実体に吸収されて消える

5. 最後にタイトル【題材名】を表示

■ 描写（リアル寄り）
- 樹木・植物は、枝ぶりと葉の1枚1枚が見える作りに（球の塊にしない）
- 遠景の山や森は木を密に並べ、空気遠近の霞をかける
- 空は物理的な空。時間帯は夕方の低い日差しで、影を長く
- 水面の映り込み、苔・岩・落ち葉など地面の細部も作る
- 建物は題材に合わせた細部（例：垂木・軒付・格子）まで
- テクスチャはプロシージャルで（朱漆・瓦・石・金など、題材に合わせて）
- 金属や金箔は白飛びさせず、素材の色が出るように
- 外観の参考画像：【画像を添付】

■ 音
- 外部素材なしでPython合成。場面の切り替わりに合わせた和風BGM＋効果音

■ 進め方
- テスト静止画を確認してから本番レンダリング
- 完成したらMP4で送って

title: Tiny scenes for a bento feature grid
author: Kubai087
prompt:
# Small animations for a product site's feature tiles

Give every tile in my site's feature grid a small animation: a tiny scene that shows what the feature does.

## 0. Before you build
- Read the project: find out the tech stack (plain HTML/CSS, React, Vue, Svelte, Astro, Tailwind, Framer Motion…) and build it the way the project already does. Don't add an animation library unless the project already uses one.
- Ask me which look to use:
A. The Lumno material below, as written.
B. My product's own style: take the colors, radii, borders and shadows from my existing design tokens and components, and keep only the structure and motion rules from this prompt.
C. A mix: the Lumno material in my brand's accent color and radii.
- Picking features: if I named features, animate those. If not, read the product's site, docs or code, list 3–5 features that a short scene can explain, and let me pick.

## 1. Lumno material (option A)
Overall: quiet, neutral, precise. Hairlines instead of borders, soft shadows tinted warm, no gradients or color washes, one accent color.

- Grid: one card with an outer radius of 28px. Cells are separated by 1px hairlines (a 1px grid gap over a hairline color). Cells are white. The card has a faint hairline ring and a soft shadow.
- Art panel: inset 8px from the cell edge, with a radius of the card radius minus the inset (20px), so corners stay concentric.
- Fill #fafafa, plus an inner 1px ring: box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(32,38,46,.07).
- Texture: background: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, rgba(32,38,46,.06) 0 1px, transparent 1px 7px).
- The scene sits centred on the panel, about 126×118px.
- Text bars: body bars 4px tall with a 2px radius in #e5e9ef; heading bars 5px tall in #cdd4de. Vary the widths (34–92px).
- Mini windows and cards: white with a 9px radius.
- Shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(47,42,34,.06), 0 8px 20px -10px rgba(47,42,34,.25).
- Tab strip: 20px tall, #eef1f5. Tabs: 16px tall with 6px top corners; the active tab is white.
- Favicons: 10px.
- Inner surfaces such as charts or fields: #f4f6fa. Secondary data: #b9c9e0. Accent: #3462ad, used only on the result.
- Icon chip (top-left of each tile): 32px, 10px radius, 1px border rgba(32,38,46,.1), white, shadow 0 1px 2px rgba(32,38,46,.05), a line-style glyph in #4b5563.
- Text color: a warm near-black, #2f2a22.
- Hover: the cell darkens to about 2.5% grey; the panel goes to #f4f5f6 with its ring at .09; the icon chip grows 32→36px from its top-left corner, its glyph turns to the text color, and its shadow deepens slightly.
- Dark mode (suggested values; keep the same relationships):
- Cells #17181a, panel #1d1f22, inner ring rgba(255,255,255,.06), texture rgba(255,255,255,.04).
- Body bars #2c2f34, heading bars #3a3e45.
- Windows #24272b with a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.06) outline and a shadow of 0 8px 20px -10px rgba(0,0,0,.6).
- Tab strip #1a1c1f, accent #6f9bea, text #ecebe8.

## 2. Scene
- One idea per tile: 2–4 moves that show "action → result", such as "click → a small window opens" or "change here → the other side syncs".
- Abstract wireframes only: no screenshots and no real text. Use at most one small icon where something needs to be recognisable.
- Motion: ease-out for movement, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); a slight spring for appearing, cubic-bezier(.34,1.4,.64,1). Each move takes 250–600ms; the whole scene is done in about 3s.
- Icon chip: when the tile plays, its glyph redraws stroke by stroke (draw, pop or slide per part), then hands back to the solid icon.

## 3. Playback
- Resting styles are the final frame. Animations only describe where things come from (fill-mode: both or equivalent), so reduced motion shows the result and an interrupted play never jumps.
- The art panel fades in (opacity, plus translateY 6px and scale .97 to none) as its tile first plays.
- Play once in view: when about 70% of the tile is visible, wait ~200ms, then play. Tiles that enter together go ~250ms apart, in reading order. Stop on the final frame.
- One "played" state (a class or data attribute) drives every animation in the tile. To replay: remove it, force a reflow, add it back (or re-key in a framework).
- On mouse hover (mouse only) or keyboard focus, replay: blur the final frame out over ~160ms (blur 6px, opacity 0), restart under the blur, then clear it. Don't restart a play that hasn't finished.
- Optional loop on hover: while the pointer stays on the tile, replay again ~600ms after each play ends. When the pointer leaves, finish the current play and rest on the final frame.
- Touch: a tap follows the tile's link; nothing depends on hover.
- prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: no animation; show the final frame.

## 4. Colors and dark mode
- Every color is a variable on the art panel (panel, ring, texture, bars, windows, tab strip, accent, shadow); no hard-coded colors in the rules.
- Follow prefers-color-scheme, and the project's manual theme switch too (a class or data-theme), if it has one.
- Check it in both light and dark.

## 5. Delivery
- Mark the art as decorative (aria-hidden) and keep translatable text out of it.
- Check it in a real browser: first play, hover replay, keyboard focus, reduced motion, dark mode and a phone-width layout.

title: Architectural presentation video from plans to completed building
author: Ayu_AI_0912
prompt:
# 依頼：【計画名】の CAD 図面と、図面から建物が立ち上がる約 20 秒の設計プレゼン動画

添付：①外観イメージ画像（1 枚目）②キャラクターの差分画像（白背景、全身、複数ポーズ）③（あれば）敷地資料・ロゴ
環境：Windows、Python 3.10（ezdxf・numpy・scipy・Pillow・matplotlib・imageio_ffmpeg）、Blender 4.2
（`C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 4.2\blender.exe`、画面は開かず `blender -b --python` で使う）

## 目的
施主に「建物の形・空間のつながり・完成後の雰囲気」を伝える。図面から建物が立ち上がり、最後に
「ここで過ごすとどう感じるか」が想像できる構成にする。すべて「計画・提案段階のイメージ」として扱い、
仮に決めた寸法は仮だと明記し、確認が必要な項目を一覧にする。

## 成果物
- 2D 図面 DXF（A2 × 3 枚、単位 mm、表題欄つき）。3D モデル（OBJ/STL/3D DXF）は作らない
  - A-001 配置図兼 1 階平面図・2 階平面図 S=1:100（設計概要・確認事項一覧・デザインのモチーフ表つき）
  - A-002 1 階・2 階平面図 S=1:50（通り芯・寸法・室名・建具記号・家具を点線で）
  - A-003 立面図 4 面 S=1:100（高さのレベル記号・仕上げの引出し）
- MP4：【1280×720 または 1920×1080】/ 24fps / 本編 20 秒 + ロゴのエンドカード 3.5 秒、音つき

## 進め方（各段階で画像を目で見て直す。PC の負荷に配慮する）
1. 外観イメージを読み、構成（棟・屋根形状・張り出し・玄関・窓・色・特徴的な飾り）を書き出す。
   キャラクターがいる場合は「建物のどこがキャラのどの特徴に対応するか」を対応表にする
   （例：三角の切妻 2 つ＝猫耳、屋根色＝髪、外壁＝服、足もとの柄＝スカートの裾、アーチ玄関＝ランドセル、縦樋＝しっぽ）
2. 形状モジュールを書く → matplotlib の簡易模型を 3 方向から描き、外観イメージと量感を照合する
3. DXF とプレビュー PNG → 文字の重なり・はみ出しを目で見て直す
4. Blender シーン → 代表フレームを 50% で試し描き → 直す、を繰り返す
5. 低解像度プレビュー動画（25%、1 コマおき、音と文字つき）を作って見せる
6. フル解像度で連続 12 コマを描いて 1 コマあたりの実時間を測る。
   「約○分・PC が重くなる」と伝えて、私の了承を待つ（了承なしに本番を始めない）
7. 本番 → 文字を重ねる → 音 → MP4 → 長さと映像・音声を確認し、数秒おきのコマを並べて見てから送る

## 1. 形状モジュール `<名前>_geom.py`（寸法の唯一の定義。単位 m、Z が上、南 = -Y、GL = 0）
CAD と Blender の両方が import する。純 Python。
- 910 mm モジュールの通り芯（X1..、Y0..）、高さ（GL・ポーチ・1FL 500・天井・2FL・軒高・棟）、屋根勾配、軒の出
- 敷地・道路（仮）、図面台紙の範囲 SHEET（動画冒頭の紙）
- ROOMS（室名・範囲・帖数）
- WALLS：(階, 始点, 終点, 厚み, 外壁か, 外向き)。外壁 150、間仕切り 100
- OPENINGS：(階, 壁の向き "x"/"y", 壁の座標, 中心, 幅, 床からの下端, 上端, 種類, 記号)。
  種類は 引違い / 掃き出し / 縦すべり出し / 高窓 / 玄関ドア / 室内ドア / 開口
- 3D 部材は Mesh クラス（box・cyl・tube・slab など）で作る。各部材に次を持たせる：
  - stage（base 基礎 / floor 床 / col 柱 / wall 壁 / roof 屋根 / finish 外装・開口 / furn 家具 / site 外構）
  - sub（段階の中での順番 0..1）と grow（伸び方 "z" / "xyz"）
  - 壁は「開口を抜いた箱の集まり」で作る。外壁は外向きの面だけ外装材、室内側と開口の見込みは白
  - 玄関ドアの扉は別部材にし、蝶番を回転の中心（pivot）にする（開く動きのため）
  - 屋根は勾配ごとの厚みのある板＋白い破風。妻壁は三角。飾り（金の三角枠など）は薄い押し出し
- 平面図の壁の塗り・建具と 3D の壁の穴は、同じ WALLS / OPENINGS から作るので必ず一致する
- 確認事項 CHECKLIST とモチーフ表 MOTIF もこのモジュールに持たせる

## 2. DXF（ezdxf）
- 文字スタイルは BIZ UDゴシック。寸法スタイルは "EZDXF" を複製し、dimscale を縮尺に、dimlfac = 1 に戻す
- A-001 は敷地を「実際の座標」に描く（モデル空間 1:1）。こうすると SHEET の範囲がそのまま動画の台紙になる
- 図面と表題欄に「計画・提案段階のイメージ。寸法・仕様は仮設定を含む」と明記する
- プレビューは ezdxf の drawing + matplotlib で PNG にし、黒背景で目視確認する

## 3. 図面台紙のテクスチャ
DXF の SHEET 範囲を 150 px/m で 2 回描く：
- 塗り（HATCH のみ、淡く）→ `tex_sheet_fill.png`
- 線と文字（HATCH 以外、黒）→ マスク `tex_sheet_lines.png`
Blender 側で紙の白・紺の線・左から描かれていくワイプを付ける。

## 4. キャラクターの切り抜き
- 白背景を外周から塗りつぶして背景にする（min(RGB) > 226 かつ彩度差 < 14）
- 閉じた白い隙間は「ほぼ真っ白で平坦な塊のうち、周囲が濃い輪郭線（< 150）で 55% 以上囲まれたもの」だけ抜く
  → 袖や襟の白は残る
- 1px 縮めて 1.2px ぼかし、余白を詰めて下端 = 足もとにする

## 5. Blender シーン（EEVEE Next）
### タイムライン（504 フレーム。完成時に頭 1 秒を切る）
| フレーム | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 1-60 | 図面台紙の線が左から描かれる（斜め上から）。キャラが台紙の脇で図面を案内するポーズ |
| 44-140 | 各部材の辺が水色の光のワイヤーとして台紙から立ち上がる |
| 84-280 | 白い模型で 基礎 84 → 床 94 → 柱・2 階床 106 → 壁 150 → 屋根 198（上から静かに降りる）→ 外装・開口 238 |

title: Code-based UI motion design loop
author: 0xAiky
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to transform into (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, no cuts: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a quick blur.
A cursor controls every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist).
Springs everywhere, with only a tiny overshoot. The camera zooms so each state fills the entire frame. The last frame matches the first frame, so it loops perfectly.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs expand into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is calculated from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
Springs use closed-form step responses. A value that changes targets multiple times is the sum of one spring per change, so it remains a pure function of time.
The tab indicator's two edges follow different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Use the same trick for the toggle knob.
Drags use direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is calculated from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
Analyze the song with numpy to find the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Position every UI sound by its measured peak.
Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or difficult to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text becomes blurry.
Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps.
Make the final frame identical to the first, including cursor position and speed, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before writing any code.
</start>

title: 30-second vertical narrated animal-facts cartoon short with host
author: finnardley
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for my animal or topic ("Why is the X the most disturbing animal in the ocean?", "Why is X terrifying?"), or pitch 3, each with 5 true facts that get worse as they go. Ask which image model I have (GPT Image 2 or any model that takes a reference image at 4K, about $0.03 an image) and which voice I have (ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free). Then write the script and the shot list with seconds, and show me both before anything costs money.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 1080x1920, 60 fps, 30-35 s vertical Short in the style of the big narrated animal-facts channels where a guy in a hoodie with a mic pops into every scene. Here everything is a flat 2D cartoon: thick dark brown outlines (#1f1418), flat colours, simple cel shading, big round googly eyes.
The host: a cartoon young man with messy brown hair, glasses, a plain heather grey hoodie with no logo, dark jeans, white sneakers, always holding a black mic.
- He is about 1000-1050 px tall on screen. His feet sit below the frame edge, so he is cut off at the shins.
- He pops up from below the frame in 0.32 s with an overshoot ease.
- His mouth flaps on the voice whenever he talks to camera.
- His face always stays above the caption pill.
The animal: one character in 9 poses (neutral, shocked, angry, plus costume poses for the facts: old with a beard and cane, a powdered wig, a teen with braces, drunk, a front view of the face, defeated on a plate). One costume per fact is the joke.
A new place every 1.5-3 s. Never repeat a composition.
Something always moves:
- Animals swim with a tail wave and bob ±10 px.
- The camera pushes in 2-4% per shot.
- Pose swaps squash.
- Hits shake the frame.
Titles are one or two big words per beat in Luckiest Guy (Google Fonts), 104-190 px at y 430, tilted ±0.03-0.05 rad:
- They wobble ±0.025 rad.
- The outline is 0.22 of the size in #1f1418, with a darker copy of the colour 0.09 of the size underneath.
- Colours are pairs of fill and shadow: yellow #ffd21f/#c27a10, red #ff4a3d/#8e1a14, white #ffffff/#9aa6b4, pink #ff7ab8/#a8336d, green #7dff6a/#2e9a2a.
Captions:
- 1-4 words in a white pill at y 1470: Luckiest Guy 66 px, dark text, a 7 px outline, pill height 1.55x the text.
- The key word is yellow with a dark outline.
- The pill pops from 0.82 to 1 in 0.13 s.
A red marker ellipse circles the animal when its name is said.
Banned: photoreal cutouts mixed into cartoon art, a real person's face, the real channel's logo or name on screen, a still frame over 1 s, the host covering the animal's face on its key word.
</direction>

<structure>
Length: 30-35 s, about 115 words at about 3.5 words a second. Times are from a 33.5 s film; scale them to the voice.
0-1.9 s, the hook "Why is the X the most disturbing animal in the ocean?":
- The animal glides in from off screen in 0.75 s while the host pops up bottom right, already talking.
- On the animal's name: a red ring, the name as a title, and the host swaps to pointing at it for 0.7 s.
1.9-3.7 s: a punch-in on "disturbing". The water is graded red, the angry pose, an impact starburst, the word in red.
3.7-8.2 s, fact 1, the shocking number:
- A counter rolls up to it.
- Then a comparison everyone gets ("older than America") shown as a costume pose and a prop that springs in.
8.2-12.7 s, facts 2 and 3 played as gags:
- One is a costume in a new place.
- One is a race the animal loses. On "slower than you walk", the host strolls past it.
12.7-15.6 s: the gross detail, with a zoom into the face.
15.6-16.7 s: "But it gets worse." A red alarm grade with a pulsing vignette. The animal yells into the lens and the host swaps from talking to horrified.
16.7-21 s, the worst fact:
- The host cowers behind the victim, which then vanishes in a poof.
- An x-ray shot shows what is inside.
21-27.7 s: the human angle, each line with a person from the cast acting it out. The host joins in (drunk next to the drunk Viking).
27.7-29 s: someone happily eats it while the host turns green and gags.
29-33.5 s: the callback joke that ties back to the hook. The host talks to camera, then cracks up on the last word. Hold 1.15 s after the last word.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy, soundfile. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Art, 4 images in total (about $0.12). Every prompt starts with "Match the exact art style of the reference image: flat 2D cartoon, thick dark brown outlines, flat colours with simple cel shading, big expressive googly eyes, clean vector look". Feed the first sheet you like back in as the style reference for the rest.
   - Animal sheet: 1:1 at 4K, "a 3 by 3 pose sheet of the SAME cartoon X, 9 separate poses on plain pure white, plenty of white space, nothing touching, no grid lines, no text, no ground shadows", every pose a full side view facing right except the front face.
   - Cast sheet: 1:1 at 4K, 9 different characters and props for the facts, same wording.
   - Background grid: 9:16 at 4K, "a 3 by 3 grid of 9 equal tall vertical panels separated by thin white gutters, each panel an EMPTY scene, no characters, no text, keep the lower middle open".
   - Host sheet: 9:16 at 4K, 9 full-body poses at the same size: (1) facing the viewer, mic below the chin, mouth CLOSED, (2) EXACTLY the same pose with only the mouth WIDE OPEN, (3) talking and pointing to the side, (4) horrified with a hand on the cheek, (5) crouching and cowering with sweat drops, (6) running in side view facing right, (7) laughing and leaning back, (8) gagging with a green face holding a toothpick of food, (9) drunk with spiral eyes.
3. Cutouts:
   - Flood the white from the border (seeds every 64 px around the edge) with a floating range of 7, so soft glows go too.
   - Feather a 3 px band outside the shapes with alpha = clamp((250 - min(R,G,B)) / 150). Un-mix the white from that band: colour = (c - 255(1 - a)) / a.
   - Group the pieces by the grid cell their centre falls in and drop pieces under 150 px.
   - Split the background grid on its white gutters (rows and columns whose minimum channel averages over 232). Crop 4 px in, cover-fit to 1080x1920 with Lanczos, unsharp mask (radius 2, 60%).
4. Host lip-sync:
   - Align pose 2 onto pose 1 by template-matching the glasses and eyes. Paste only its mouth onto pose 1 through a feathered ellipse (sigma 4). Now open and closed are the same drawing, so the outline never wobbles.
   - Mouth track at 60 fps from the voice: RMS per frame, smoothed over 3 frames. Open when it is over (70th percentile in dB - 15) and over 0.55x the loudest frame within ±0.1 s.
   - Hold every state at least 3 frames. Break open runs longer than 14 frames with a 3-frame close every 12 frames. That gives about 8 flips a second.
   - Anchor every host pose by its feet and its head centre x (the alpha centre of the top 28% of the cutout), so pose swaps never jump. Measure that per pose.
5. Voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v4 with the timestamps endpoint, a calm deep documentary narrator, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, one take (about 300 credits for 600 characters).
   - Cut pauses (10 ms frames under -40 dB, longer than 0.2 s) down to their first and last 0.06 s, with 8 ms fades.
   - Then atempo 1.15 and a 0.15 s lead-in.
   - Rebuild word times from the character alignment through the same cuts and tempo. When a start lands after the next word's start, pull it back.
   - Free route: Kokoro, then whisper for the word times.
6. Film: one HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV with the sound times. One function per shot.
   - Sprite tail wave: draw the cutout in 28 vertical slices. Each slice moves dy = sin(8t - 4.5u) * wig * k, where k = (max(0, u - 0.3) / 0.7)^1.5 and wig is 3-14 px.
   - Pop: 1 - 0.6 e^(-9Δt) cos(20Δt). Pose-swap kick: 1 + a e^(-10Δt) cos(22Δt), with a = 0.1-0.22. Shake: A e^(-7Δt) sin(61Δt), with A = 22-34 px.
   - Props drawn in code: a rolling number counter, a waving flag, a flipping calendar, green fumes, buzzing flies, confetti, red rings, arrows, an impact starburst, poof clouds, bubbles.
   - Red alarm grade: grayscale(.5) sepia(1) hue-rotate(-35deg) saturate(3.2) brightness(.55).

title: Procedural plush dragon browser demo with combable fur and
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build "Plush Dragon" — Material Studies No. 014: a single self-contained HTML file, native WebGPU, fully procedural (no assets, no libraries), in the same editorial style as the series (serif masthead, side specimen panel, live readouts, "Inside the experiment" notes).

The specimen:
- A chubby plush baby dragon sitting on a table, all made from one signed distance field.
- Minky body: a big round head with a short snout and two felt horns, a pale belly quilted in horizontal bands, stubby arms, round haunches with padded feet and tiny felt claws.
- A tail curled round to one side, ending in a soft spade.
- A row of flat felt spikes down the head, back and tail.
- Face: glossy bead eyes, blushing cheeks, embroidered nostrils, a stitched smile with one little felt fang.
- Two quilted plush wings sewn on at the shoulders.

Physics:
- Body: XPBD soft body on a hex-cell lattice (co-rotational shape matching plus tetrahedral volume), 60 Hz, 6 substeps. Gravity and floor friction; the seat keeps its footing and the toy slowly rights itself like a weighted plush.
- Muscles instead of forces: the belly breathes (cells' rest shapes and rest volumes swell); the tail wags by lengthening cells on one side of its centre line and shortening them on the other, faster when the dragon is happy.
- Wings:
  - each wing is a small XPBD cloth cut from a curved fan-shaped 3D pattern (stretch, shear and bend links), its two root rows embedded in the body lattice;
  - a pose (fold back about the vertical, flap about a hinge along the body, both riding a shoulder frame from embedded points) pulls every point toward its target: firmly at the root, barely at the edge, so the stuffed wings lag and flop;
  - collider spheres riding the body keep the wings off it.
- Flapping: downstrokes lift the dragon with a hover controller (about 6 cm off the table, bobbing with each beat), then it drops back onto its seat.
- Pulling a wing past its slack tows the body by that shoulder.

Rendering:
- Shell fur (base + N instanced shells, alpha-to-coverage under 4× MSAA): fur lie carried by the deformation gradient, damped-spring tip lag, Kajiya–Kay highlights, velvet sheen, a comb tool.
- Regions painted in rest space: belly with quilting seams, short-nap felt horns and spikes in the wing colour, padded soles, cheeks, smile groove.
- Wings drawn each frame as stuffed slabs swept from the cloth:
  - a rolled leading edge in the body colour;
  - three panels puffed between stitched ribs;
  - a scalloped trailing edge;
  - a shorter pile of the same minky.
- Glossy eyes, embroidery thread, felt fang and claws.
- Soft PCSS key-light shadows, contact occlusion on the studio floor, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping.
- NaN-safe WGSL (clamped pow/smoothstep, clamped post).

Interaction:
- Hand: lift and squash the dragon, or grab a wing to stretch it open (pull harder to tow the dragon).
- Finger: a finger reaches in from the viewer; poke to dent the stuffing; hold it pressed in to tickle —

title: Interactive WebGPU jelly watermelon that can be cut and grabbed
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a real-time WebGPU soft-body "jelly" study of a watermelon wedge that you can cut with a steel knife, in an editorial "Material Studies" page style (serif title "Melon Jelly.", muted paper backdrop, side panel, English UI, mobile-friendly). Geometry: a thick triangular watermelon wedge with a rounded green rind, a pale white layer, and translucent red flesh with dark seeds and a few air bubbles. Sim: CPU XPBD on a tetrahedral mesh, fixed 60 Hz step with 10 substeps. Each tet uses a co-rotational shape-matching constraint with finite compliance, which also flips inverted elements back out, plus a near-incompressible volume constraint so a stretched slice necks in. The rind is about 3× stiffer than the flesh. Damping acts only on relative velocity along edges. Floor contact uses Coulomb friction. Grabbing is a soft, reach-limited attachment to a patch of particles, and scroll or a second finger twists it.

Two tools, Hand and Knife:
- Knife: the user draws a stroke across the slice. Read on the surface, that stroke defines a vertical blade plane. Every piece is stored as a rounded convex outline in the slice's rest plane. For each piece the plane crosses, fit the piece's current pose with a best rotation, carry the plane back to rest space as a straight line, and split the outline along it.
- The cut: prebuild both halves as fresh tet meshes on release. An animated steel knife lines up over the stroke, comes down, and first presses a groove into the jelly. When it breaks through, swap in the new pieces, which inherit the position and velocity of the flesh they came from, and the blade wedges the faces apart on its way to the board. Draw the blade behind the jelly surface so the buried part is seen refracted.
- Pieces: every piece is its own soft body that can be grabbed, stretched and cut again, and pieces collide with each other instead of passing through.

Render: a smooth surface mesh plus the seeds and bubbles, each vertex embedded in a tet by barycentric weights so they ride the wobble. WGSL passes:
- floor, seeds and bubbles first;
- back faces, to get the thickness each view ray crosses;
- front faces with refraction by that thickness, Beer–Lambert absorption, milky scattering in the pale layer, a back-lit glow at thin edges, Fresnel reflections of a procedural studio, and GGX highlights;
- a soft key shadow on the floor tinted by the jelly, plus contact AO from a top-down height map.

Varieties: Crimson, Golden, Rosé. Controls: Hand/Knife tool toggle, firmness and internal damping sliders, "Give it a nudge", Reset, Pause, ¼ speed, Show mesh, plus mass/volume/kinetic readouts and an "Inside the experiment" notes drawer explaining the physics, cutting and rendering.

Traverse gltf.scene; for each mesh: clone geometry, delete 'uv','color','tangent' attributes, mergeVertices(g, 1e-4), computeVertexNormals(), applyMatrix4(mesh.matrixWorld). Merge all parts with mergeGeometries. - Centre the geometry on its bounding box and scale uniformly so its largest dimension = 1. - Scene graph: scene → pivot (screen position + scale) → spinner (rotation) → cube mesh. On load add class "done" to #loader. 4c. Cube placement (in layout(), on load and on resize) - visH = 2*tan(fov/2)*10; visW = visH*aspect. - Screen-fraction centre: sx = mobile ? 0.5 : 0.517, sy = mobile ? 0.45 : 0.488. pivot.position = ((sx-0.5)*visW, (0.5-sy)*visH, 0). - On-screen edge length px = min(H*0.44, W*(mobile ? 0.45 : 0.29)); pivot.scale = (px/H)*visH. - Initial spinner rotation: Euler(-0.42, 0.62, 0.18). 4d. Glass material — custom ShaderMaterial, screen-space refraction with 6-band chromatic dispersion, rendered in two passes (back faces, then front faces). Vertex shader: varying vec3 vNormal; varying vec3 vEye; worldPos = modelMatrix*position; mvPos = viewMatrix*worldPos; gl_Position = projectionMatrix*mvPos; vNormal = normalize(normalMatrix*normal); vEye = normalize(https://mvpos.xyz/); Fragment shader: uv = gl_FragCoord.xy / uResolution (drawing-buffer size). n = normalize(vNormal); if (uBackside > 0.5) n = -n; // do NOT use gl_FrontFacing, three.js flips winding for BackSide eye = normalize(vEye). LOOP = 16 iterations; slide = i/LOOP * 0.045. For each band compute refract(eye, n, 1.0/ior) with iorR/Y/G/C/B/P and sample uTexture at uv + refr.xy * (uRefractPower + slide*k) * uChromatic, with k = 1 (R), 1 (Y), 2 (G), 2.5 (C), 3 (B), 1 (P): r = tex(R).x*0.5 y = (tex(Y).x*2 + tex(Y).y*2 - tex(Y).z)/6 g = tex(G).y*0.5 c = (tex(C).y*2 + tex(C).z*2 - tex(C).x)/6 b = tex(B).z*0.5 p = (tex(P).z*2 + tex(P).x*2 - tex(P).y)/6 R = r + (2p + 2y - c)/3; G = g + (2y + 2c - p)/3; B = b + (2c + 2p - y)/3 color += vec3(R,G,B) color /= LOOP; saturation adjust: mix(luma(color), color, uSaturation) with luma weights (0.2125, 0.7154, 0.0721). Specular (Blinn-Phong, light vector = normalize(-light), view = -eye): spec = specular(uLight, uShininess, uDiffuseness) + 0.6 * specular(vec3(1,1,-1), uShininess*0.6, uDiffuseness*0.5) spec(x) = pow(max(dot(n,halfVec),0), shininess) + max(0,dot(n,lightVec))*diffuseness color += spec * (backside ? 0.35 : 1.0) Fresnel: f = pow(1.0 + dot(eye, n), uFresnelPower); color = mix(color, vec3(1), f * (backside ? 0.25 : 0.55)). color += vec3(0.004, 0.005, 0.007). gl_FragColor = vec4(color,1); then #include <colorspace_fragment> on its own line. Uniform values: uIorR 1.15, uIorY 1.16, uIorG 1.18, uIorC 1.22, uIorB 1.22, uIorP 1.22, uRefractPower 0.30 (front) / 0.22 (back), uChromatic 0.5, uSaturation 1.08, uShininess 90, uDiffuseness 0.02, uFresnelPower 5.0, uLight (-1, 1, 1), uBackside 0 (frontMat, side FrontSide) / 1 (backMat, side BackSide). 4e. Render pipeline (every frame) - Two WebGLRenderTargets sized to drawing buffer (W*DPR × H*DPR), type HalfFloatType, default (linear) colour space: rtBack, rtFront. - backMat.uTexture = rtBack.texture; frontMat.uTexture = rtFront.texture. 1) render bgScene → rtBack 2) render bgScene → rtFront, then (autoClear=false) cube with backMat → rtFront 3) render bgScene → screen, then (autoClear=false, clearDepth) cube with frontMat → screen - This gives the look: text seen through the cube is magnified, mirrored and split into blue/yellow fringes, inner rounded edges of the cube are faintly visible, and the bevelled edges glow white. ================================================== 5. title: Interactive pixel art swimming club
author: N1njaCodex
prompt:
Make a pixel-art 3D diorama of an open-air lido on a floating island, the same series and engine as my other pixel dioramas (three.js, orthographic isometric camera turned in quarter steps, small render target with no anti-aliasing snapped to whole pixels, depth-based outlines, a fixed 64-colour palette matched in OKLab, hard sun shadows, day/dusk/night, rain with puddles). Call it "Deep End".

The lido: a 25 m four-lane lap pool (shallow end roped off for children, lane ropes whose floats ride the waves, backstroke flags, starting blocks) and a 5 m deep diving pool, with 1 m and 3 m springboards that bend and a 1930s concrete tower with platforms at 5, 7.5 and 10 m and an open stair. Around them: striped changing cabins with a clock, a kiosk, the judges' table, the lifeguard's high chair, loungers, parasols and umbrella pines.

Real water: each pool is a height field run with the wave equation, so dives, strokes, raindrops and clicks make rings that reflect off the walls. The surface shades from its normals, with sun glints and a mirrored render of the scene; the tiled floor gets caustics.

Dives are flown, not animated. The diver takes off with an upward speed and an angular momentum chosen to land the somersaults, the momentum is conserved through tuck, pike and straight shapes, and the body rotates about its real centre of mass, with twists about the spine. Kick-out timing errors tip the entry angle, which sets the splash and five judges' cards; drop the highest and lowest and multiply by DD. Run a six-diver, five-round meet on the 10 m platform or the 3 m springboard (with the approach and hurdle), with standings, then a medal moment, then free swim with pencil jumps, cannonballs and belly flops.

Also: lap swimmers doing freestyle, breaststroke and backstroke with flip turns; divers who swim to a ladder, shower, sit in the hot tub and climb again; children who get whistled at for running; wet footprints on the deck that dry; pool lights glowing at night. Click the water to make a splash. English UI; must work on phones.

title: Fictional rocket CAD drawings and launch animation
author: Ayu_AI_0912
prompt:
架空の大型ロケット（2段式の液体ロケット＋固体ブースター2本、白い機体、名前なし）と
その射点について、CAD図面と Blender 動画を作ってください。

【図面】2D の DXF のみ（3Dモデルの書き出しは不要）。単位 mm、A2 の図枠と表題欄つき。
線は青緑系の「電子の図面」風にし、プレビュー画像は濃紺の背景にする。
1. 射点配置図 S=1:500（ロケットを原点に置き、実際の位置で描く。
移動発射台・排煙溝・アンビリカルタワー・避雷塔・照明塔・水タンク・建屋・海岸線）
2. 射点立面図（南から）S=1:400
3. ロケット外形図・断面図 S=1:250
特記事項に「架空の機体・射場のイメージで、実在の図面ではない」と書く。
寸法は Python の形状モジュール1つで決め、図面と動画の両方がそれを読み込む。

【動画】Blender（EEVEE）、1920×1080・24fps・本編20秒＋ロゴ3.5秒、音つき MP4。
1. 暗闇の床に、シアンに光る射点配置図が中心から走査されて描かれる（真上から）
2. 図面の線が光のワイヤーとして立ち上がる
3. 光の粒（Geometry Nodes）が渦を巻いて昇り、発射台・タワー・ロケットが下から積み上がる
（積み上がった高さより下だけが実体になる。カメラは寄る）
4. 図面がマス目ごとにデジタルに溶け、夜の射点が現れる（海・丘・星空。カメラは引く）。
照明塔が点いて白い機体が浮かび、塔の頂部の赤い灯が明滅する
5. アクセスアームが離れる → カウントダウン → 点火 → リフトオフ。
炎は発光する円錐、噴煙は排煙溝と発射台から湧き、上昇する機体の後ろに煙の柱が残る
6. 上昇するロケットを海の上から見上げたところでタイトル → 最後に指定のロゴ
音は外部素材を使わず Python で合成する
（電子音の BGM、波、カウントダウンの電子音、点火から上昇までの轟音、タイトルの和音）。

【進め方】
- 図面のプレビュー画像を目で見て、文字の重なりを直す
- 本番の前にテスト静止画を数枚描いて確認する（照明の明るさ、炎や光の白飛び）
- 本番レンダーは軽い設定で、PC を休ませながら回す。始める前に所要時間を伝えて了承を取る

title: Plush pigeon physics demo in a WebGPU browser engine
author: vib3coded
prompt:

title: Temporal grid music video edit for Gojo

prompt:
Create a high-energy 16:9 temporal poster-grid music video, exactly matching the full duration of the supplied music.

GRID STRUCTURE:
Divide the entire frame into a dense 20×12 matrix of near-square cells separated by ultra-thin grey lines. Preserve one continuous, recognizable image across the grid rather than displaying unrelated images. The grid acts as a unified visual canvas with independently animated temporal fragments.

TEMPORAL CHOREOGRAPHY:
Keep the central 4×4 region anchored to the primary action, maintaining recognizable movement and visual continuity. Surrounding cells explore different moments of the same footage through staggered time offsets, rapid repetitions, reversed motion, delayed echoes, speed ramps, micro-loops and impact freezes.

VISUAL EFFECTS:
Layer sophisticated graphic treatments driven by the music:
- Chromatic aberration and RGB channel displacement
- Directional motion smears and multi-frame ghost trails
- Glitch propagation and digital frame tearing
- High-contrast monochrome flashes and selective color isolation
- Halftone textures, manga speed lines and graphic silhouettes
- Pixel sorting, scanline interference and datamosh-like distortions
- Grid warping, cell displacement and elastic boundary deformation
- Stroboscopic impact frames and negative-image flashes
- Temporal feedback loops and recursive motion echoes
- Brief typography fragments, abstract symbols and kinetic graphic overlays

RHYTHMIC EDITING:
Analyze the soundtrack's beats, accents, transitions and energy progression. Synchronize cell activity, temporal shifts, visual effects and grid transformations precisely to the music.

Use restrained motion during quieter passages, escalating into dense synchronized chaos during climaxes. On major impacts, trigger cascading temporal explosions across the grid, followed by sudden unified resets.

VISUAL COHERENCE:
Maintain the source footage's original characters, compositions and visual identity. The grid must remain structurally recognizable even during aggressive effects. Prioritize creative temporal manipulation over random glitch noise.

Make the result feel like an experimental motion-design masterpiece: dense, rhythmic, kinetic, visually intricate and deliberately choreographed.
