title: 38-second realistic 3D short about a man and weather balloons
author: theoardley
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me 2 things, then wait:
1. The story in one line: a strange TRUE event where one person did one odd physical thing ("He tied 42 weather balloons to a lawn chair."). If I say "you pick", pitch 3 with one source link each and take the first unless I choose.
2. The voice. Default: Kokoro (free, runs on my computer), a calm, warm male narrator.
Then tell me everything else is free: Blender (find my install, or tell me the one download), its free MPFB extension for human bodies (ask me before you install it) and into this folder a Python venv with FFmpeg (imageio-ffmpeg), kokoro-onnx + its model files (kokoro-v1.0.onnx and voices-v1.0.bin from the kokoro-onnx GitHub releases), faster-whisper (small.en), numpy and Pillow. It needs no API key or account and renders on my graphics card with EEVEE.
</inputs>

<direction>
The look: a clean, realistic 3D world, like a good game cutscene. Bright, saturated, a little filmic.
- People: realistic bodies with generic faces and big readable expressions (shock, a smirk, a scream). Plain clothes, no logos. Never a real person's likeness: for a real person keep the face out of close-ups (hands, back, side, distance, straight top-down).
- CALM shots only. Bodies in fast action or contact (running, jumping, fighting, falling) look stiff, so tell the story with frozen moments under a slowly moving camera, macro inserts of hands and objects, rooms, vehicles, the sky, top-down views and the aftermath.
- One new picture for every caption chunk (2-4 words, about 1-1.5 s): a new framing, a new action or a camera move. Nothing ever holds still: every shot drifts, pushes in or orbits.
- The shot kit: macro insert (extreme close-up of the key object or hands, very shallow depth of field), hero low angle (wide lens at waist height), god's-eye top-down with a slow rotate, tracked object, over the shoulder, smash zoom on the word that matters, whip pan between beats, glow highlight (the named object glows orange with a rim, then fades), a big 3D number lying in the scene, a thought bubble (a cloud ring showing what he hoped for), a TV in the scene replaying the event.
- Light: a bright warm sun, blue sky with clouds, soft shadows. Night scenes use hard lamps and a dark sky. Wide lens up close, depth of field on every shot, motion blur on every fast camera move.
- Captions: 2-4 words at a time, white bold rounded sans, about 64 px on a 1080 px-wide frame, centred, 78% down the frame, soft dark shadow, no box. Each chunk replaces the last on the same frame as its picture.
- Banned: real footage, photos, downloaded textures or 3D models, logos, AI images or AI video, downloaded music, gore.
</direction>

<structure>
38-50 s, 100-140 words, 150-180 words a minute. The voice starts at 0.0 s.
- Line 1: the most surprising physical act, in past tense, opening with "He" (or "She"). No name, date or setup. Frame 1 shows that act.
- Then a cause-and-effect chain: every sentence starts with a hinge word (Then, Suddenly, So, Because, But, Later) and is ONE visible action.
- The context arrives late, after "You see,".
- A reveal: someone looks closer and the story turns.
- The last line is the consequence. No call to action, no question.
- Names are rare: use one only when it pays off.
Title = "He ..." or "The Man Who ...". The cover is the first frame.
</structure>

<build>
Save every stage to disk so a crash never costs more than one stage.
- sources.md: every fact with its link and the date you read it. Anything you can't verify stays out.
- script.json: the lines and the caption chunks cut by hand (2-4 words, one picture each), each chunk with its shot: the set, the camera, what moves.
- https://t.co/2ltXAYBEB2: Kokoro reads the whole script in one take (speed 1.0-1.1) and pauses are squeezed to 0.35 s at most; faster-whisper times every word (pass it a 16 kHz numpy array, not a path); write chunks.json with each chunk's start and end. A picture and its caption switch together on frame round(start*30)+1.
- blender/: Python scripts run headless (blender -b -P). https://t.co/Xw0DENaRfo makes one .blend with the sets, the cast, the props and every shot baked with a key on every frame. https://t.co/7dWyuydMpl sets EEVEE with ray tracing, the AgX view with the Punchy look, motion blur, depth of field and bloom in the compositor. Bodies come from MPFB or are built by you; clothes, hair, props and sets are built in code.
- Stills first: one half-size still per shot as a contact sheet. Look at every tile and fix what's off before any full render. Time one full-size frame and tell me the estimate.
- Render 1080x1920 at 30 fps to PNG frames, skipping frames already on disk.
- https://t.co/49eJxversT, numpy only: a light music bed, a sound on every action (a whoosh on each whip pan, hits, wind, room tone), ducked under the voice, mastered to -14 LUFS on the whole stereo mix.
- https://t.co/9GMRkcDO2w: burn the captions in from chunks.json. Encode out/<slug>_9x16.mp4 (1080x1920, 30 fps, TV-range yuv420p) and out/<slug>_x_7x8.mp4 (1008x1152, under 10 MB, 2-pass): a crop of the 9:16 frame that keeps the subject and the caption.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Blender paths: pass absolute output paths (a relative one lands on the drive root).
- MPFB headless: enable it with addon_utils.enable("bl_ext.user_default.mpfb"). Bake a body's shape keys before you pose it: the rig is fitted to the baked shape.
- Clothes: cut them from the body mesh and push them 7-16 mm out along the normals; keep two rings of body faces under every hem.
- Nothing coplanar: keep every resting object 1 cm off its neighbour and draw ground markings into the texture, or they flicker.
- Hair: EEVEE draws hair only from a Curves object, hair type STRIP. Use a Principled BSDF on it (the Hair BSDF renders black).
- Skin: keep subsurface weight near 0.2 (more turns faces black in EEVEE) and add a soft fill light from below under a noon sun.
- Hands: a curled hand reads as a claw from the palm side, so shoot a grip from behind the knuckles.
- Motion blur: shutter position START, a key on every frame, plus a key half a frame after each shot's last frame, so blur never reaches across a cut.
- Check: run a black-frame and one-frame-flicker check on the render. Make a contact sheet (a frame every 0.5 s) and look at every tile: the act reads in the first 2 s, faces are lit, nothing clips through anything, captions stay off faces and key objects. Then step through the first 2 s, the middle and the end frame by frame. Fix, render only the changed shots again.
</gotchas>

<start>
Pitch (or take my story), then show me the script with the word count, the caption chunks with their seconds and the shot list with what the first frame shows. Build nothing until I say go.

It borrows the big What-if channels' rhythm (DAY/CASE cards, a HUD counter, poofs, pop-in captions, a rewind loop) but every character and outfit is original.
The ad formula (from the best Pixar-style AI ads):
- Cold open in a genre with no product mention for the first beats; the viewer thinks it is a story.
- The product enters as a plot device (the evidence, the stolen thing, the reason someone wins), never as an ad.
- The twist is the product's benefit turned into a punchline ("too good to share", "too hard to kill").

- Give every character their own outfit; never copy a reference creator's character clothes 1:1. Example cast: detective kid (tan belted trench coat, red scarf wrap, brown fedora with a band), little brother (red-white striped tee, blue overalls, bowl cut), Mom (black hair, yellow headband, ponytail, coral sweater, green pants), Dad (side part, short jaw beard, round thin glasses, green sweater vest, white shirt, blue tie), dog (white with a brown eye patch and floppy brown ears).
- Faces carry the comedy. Eyes: normal (white with a big pupil and two highlights), huge, happy arcs, closed, star, spiral, narrow. Brows: up, worry, angry, flat (mirror them per eye so worry never reads as angry). Mouths: smile, grin, wide, scream (one clean open shape with teeth band and tongue), o, flat, smirk, wavy, chew (puffed cheeks). Plus blush, sweat drops and sunglasses that drop in. Blink for 0.1 s about every 1.6 s. Mouths flap only while that character's words are being spoken.
Sets: detailed flat rooms in saturated colours with thick outlines, each with a night version (darker blue grade plus warm lamp glows): a kitchen (wallpaper, upper cabinets, window with curtains and sky, jar shelf, plant, clock, pendant lamp, tiled backsplash, drawer counter, checker floor) and a bedroom (striped wall, window, poster, toy shelf, bed with a star blanket, nightstand lamp, plank floor, rug). Bursting sunburst colours for montages and the packshot.
Fonts (all free, from Google Fonts' GitHub repo):
- Captions: Lilita One.
- Day/CASE cards and big world words: Luckiest Guy.
- The product wrapper text: Sniglet ExtraBold, auto-fitted so it never clips.
Captions:
- 1-2 words at a time in Lilita One 94 px, centred at y 1600 (on the legs, never across a face), max 900 px wide.
- White with a 20 px #1c1030 outline and a soft shadow, popping from 55% to 100% in 0.16 s.
- Key words in caps and colour: red #ff5165, green #5dff8f, yellow #ffd23f, pink #ff7ad9, cyan #7debff, orange #ffa53d, purple #c49bff.
- No full stops or commas on screen, ever. Hide captions on the packshot.
Fake game UI over the world:
- A HUD counter pill (260x92, centred at x 540, y 196) with a tiny product icon that tracks the story (snacks stolen, clues found) and ticks with a green "+N".
- CASE/DAY cards: Luckiest Guy 230 px in yellow #ffd23f with a 38 px outline, tilted -6 degrees, popping in over 0.22 s and leaving at 1.05 s.
- Toast pills (88 px tall at y 374), a FOLLOW button with the handle chip and a cursor that presses it (it turns green "FOLLOWING").
Motion: something moves on every line, and the picture changes every 1-3 s.
- Things arrive with a squash (0.72, 1.12, 0.95, 1 over 0.3 s), an overshoot ease or a white poof cloud with stars, never a plain fade.
- Characters breathe (1.2% squash) all the time.
- The camera pushes in 5-15% per shot, stays inside the set, and shakes (decaying over 0.35 s) on every hit.
Banned: real logos or real creators' characters, AI stills, spiky hair, a frame that holds still for more than 1 s, captions over faces, system fallback fonts, whispered narration.
</direction>

<structure>
Length: 40-45 s, 85-100 words, 14 lines. Times below are from the 40.3 s "Snack Detective" ad; key every beat to a real word.
0-5 s: the narrator reads the title as line 1 ("What if you were a detective and someone kept stealing your snacks?") over the striking picture (crime-scene tape round an empty drawer; the hero poofs in on "detective"; the drawer slides open empty).
5-8 s: the hero's line that proves it ("My Krunchkin bar! GONE!"): spiral eyes, scream, a toast pill ("CASE OPENED"), the HUD appears with +1.
8-13 s: CASE 1. Suspect one (little brother with chocolate on his face, a magnifier finds it) and a tiny excuse line ("It's paint!").
13-17 s: CASE 2, bigger. HUD +1. A second suspect (the dog) looks guilty, the wrapper slides out.
17-21 s: CASE 3, the biggest. HUD +3. A third suspect (Dad "on a diet", a bar in his pocket) with a callback pop-in of suspect one pointing.
21-24.5 s: the follow beat told inside the story ("Follow, and the detective gets one more clue"): the button is pressed about 0.5 s into the line and a clue card drops in.
24.5-26.5 s: the turn begins ("So you set a trap"): night, a spotlight on the product as bait.
26.5-29 s: a 3-shot montage with no voice (0.85 s each on bursting colours): DUST!, NIGHT CAM (green tint, REC), RING RING! The counter races to 999.
29-30 s: the hero's line ("Got you!"): flashlight snaps on. The music cuts dead.
30-35 s: the twist: the fridge light floods on, it is Mom, chewing ("They're too crunchy to share, sweetie"), sunglasses drop in.
35-37.5 s: the packshot ("Krunchkin. Too good to share."): the bar spins in, crumbs fly, TOO GOOD / TO SHARE pops in.
37.5-39.8 s: a short tag from the hero ("Wait, there's a whole box?") as Mom slides a giant box into frame, HUD +94.
last 0.55 s: REWIND. The whole film scrubs backwards to frame 0 with scanlines and a REWIND label, so the end loops into the start.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools (free): Python 3 with numpy, scipy and Pillow, FFmpeg, Node with Playwright and its Chromium, faster-whisper large-v3-turbo (int8 on the CPU), git for fonts. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Script and storyboard first:
   - "you" and "your" point of view, the title as line 1, one picture per line, 10-16 words at most per line, words a 10-year-old uses, no names.
   - Draw the storyboard with the real rig and real fonts (15 panels at 1080x1920, tiled with times, speaker and line), and a cast lineup. Zoom in on every character at full size and fix hair, hats, glasses, mouths and outfits before showing me.
3. Voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v3 with stock library voices, one take per character, all of that character's lines in one request separated by blank lines.
   - Narrator: an energetic young male creator voice (Liam). Hero kid: a playful bright voice (Jessica). Mom: sassy (Laura). Little brother: the kid voice pitched up 3 semitones afterwards.
   - Audio tags: [excited], [screaming], [nervously], [sweetly], [mischievously], [confused]. Write numbers as words ("Case one").
   - Ask before spending credits. Check the API key's own credit cap before the big narrator request.
   - Run faster-whisper with word timestamps on each take. Match lines by word count with difflib, refine each line's edges on the audio itself (pad 0.06 s before, 0.15 s after).
   - Squeeze pauses inside a line to 0.22 s. Leave 0.2 s between lines, 0.33 s before each CASE line, and a 2.55 s silent slot for the montage.
   - Level every take to the narrator's median. Word times on the finished track come from the take times plus the assembly offsets, so every cut, card, caption and sound starts on a real word.
4. Film (free): one HTML page with one canvas, where every frame is a pure function of time: https://t.co/rj6e5z6GiZ(t), window.READY, window.END.
   - A SHOTS list of [start, end, function] keyed to word times (cuts land 0.04 s before their word). Each shot sets a camera (centre, zoom over time, clamped to the set), draws its world and characters, and the overlays (HUD, cards, toasts, follow button, captions) draw in screen space on top.
   - One rig function draws every character from a pose: x, y, scale, squash, rotation, flip, arm and leg angles, head tilt, eyes, brows, mouth, look, blush, sweat, shades, prop. Hand positions come from the same arm maths, so props (magnifier, flashlight, product, salad, paintbrush) sit in the hand.
5. Check before render: contact sheets at the start and end of every line on the real timing. Fix captions over faces, props out of frame, cards over heads, camera past the set edge, and any text that clips.
6. Render (free): seek 120 subframes a second in headless Chromium, pipe JPEG screenshots to FFmpeg, blend pairs with tmix for motion blur at 60 fps (about 8 min for 40 s on 2 CPUs). Encode the upload copy with libx264 CRF 20, preset slow, AAC 256k (about 26 MB).
7. Sound (free, Mixkit):
   - Music: one playful bed ("Comical"), about 19 dB under the voice. Cut it dead on the two big moments (the trap springing and the twist reveal), back on the packshot.
   - Effects placed so each one's loudest moment lands on its frame: a poof on arrivals, pops and whooshes on cards, a coin ding on every counter tick, a glint on the magnifier, a boing on silly pop-ins, a slam on screams, a click and slam on the flashlight, a gasp and sting on the reveal, a crunch on the product, a party horn on the tagline, a rewind sound on the loop.
   - Effects on speech 12 dB under the voice, in gaps 4 dB under. Measure voice versus everything else per line and duck the rest under any line below 15.5 dB (the worst line should end at 15.5 dB or more).
   - Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1.5.
8. Final checks: no frame still for over 1 s outside a deliberate beat, captions on their words, and a look at 15 frames across the finished file before delivering.
</build>

<gotchas>
- My workspace's own internet is blocked; fonts come from Google Fonts' GitHub repo with a sparse git clone (ofl/lilitaone, apache/luckiestguy, ofl/sniglet). Never fall back to DejaVu or another system font.
- A browser tab can call ElevenLabs but cannot save files into my folders. Record the voices with a small .bat on my PC that curls the API into the project's Raw folder, and runs faster-whisper there in the same double-click.
- An ElevenLabs API key can have its own credit cap below the account balance. A refused request returns quota_exceeded; log the response body so the reason is visible.
- Whisper writes "1" for "one" and drops "!" and "..."; match lines by word count, not exact text.
- Spiky or zig-zag hair always looks broken. Use smooth bezier hair caps whose top reaches above the head's crown, or the crown shows as a bald band.
- A ponytail drawn in front of the body covers held props; hang it behind the head on the far side.
- Square glasses crash into the brows; use round thin rims centred on the eyes with the brows above them.
- A hanging scarf tail reads as a tie; use a neck wrap with a small side knot.
- Big shading ellipses split faces in half; keep the shade a thin crescent on one edge.
- Plain script tags share one global scope: a page variable named like a helper function (window.N vs function N) blanks the whole page. Prefix names.
- A zoomed camera centre near the floor shows black past the set edge. Clamp the camera

title: Pixel-art 3D table tennis diorama with courtyard life and UI
author: vib3coded
prompt:
PROMPT

Build a single-file HTML pixel-art diorama called "King of the Table": table tennis in the courtyard of a three-storey pastel panel apartment block, on a small floating island, rendered with three.js (r160 via importmap) as a real 3D scene drawn into a low-res render target (orthographic isometric camera in 90° steps, whole-pixel snapping, depth outlines, a fixed 64-colour palette matched in OKLab, optional dither, Raw 3D toggle).

World: the block with three entrances (canopies, numbered plates, lamps), windows, balconies with washing; brick garages; a regulation concrete table (2.74 × 1.525 m, top at 76 cm, steel net 15.25 cm) on a slab pad with a flip score counter on a stool; benches; a playground (swings, slide, sandbox, carousel); washing lines whose sheets flap in the wind; two parked cars; birches, lilac, painted-tyre flower beds, a chalk hopscotch; lamp posts. Merge static meshes by material.

Ball physics: 40 mm / 2.7 g ball with strong quadratic drag, Magnus lift from spin (topspin dives, backspin floats), table bounce that converts spin into pace, net and net-cord, ground bounces and rolling, walls, wind with gusts. Shots are solved (bisection over launch angle) to land on a target with a given spin and net clearance, then perturbed by an error model (hurry, incoming pace, risk, wind, mishits). Serves: tossed ≥16 cm from the palm, struck behind the end line, solved so they bounce once on each half; lets.

Game: 4 neighbours with distinct styles (lefty topspin attacker, close blocker, far-back chopper, wild smasher) play king of the table: games to 11, two clear, serve changes every 2 points and every point from 10-all; winner stays, loser to the back of the bench. Players predict the ball's flight, shuffle to meet it after the bounce, and choose forehand/backhand loops, drives, blocks, pushes, flicks, chops, lobs, floated returns and smashes, with keyed bat paths and two-bone IK box-rig bodies. Between points the nearer player fetches the ball wherever it rolled (or takes a new one if it falls off the island), throws it to the server, who bounces it on the table before serving. Yard life via generator coroutines and A*: grandmothers knit and comment, kids swing/slide/ride the carousel/dig/watch, a man walks his dog, pigeons peck and take off when approached. Day/dusk/night, rain (everyone shelters under the canopy, puddle reflections, then the table is wiped), wind calm/breeze/gusty. Clicks: the table aims the next shot; the yard calls the pigeons; buttons call Loop/Push/Smash/Lob. UI: flip-card score board with serve dots, bench ladder with W–L, longest rally, wind readout, comments feed, view controls, "How it's drawn" notes, light/dark themes, phone layout.

title: Coded music video for Mongolian throat singing dubstep track
author: kloss_xyz
prompt:
You're a motion director and creative coder. Make a finished music video for [song file], built entirely in code and rendered frame by frame.

Concept: [your idea in one or two sentences]
Look: [palette, mood, references]
On-screen text: [title only / none / lyrics]
Deliver: [full song or mm:ss to mm:ss], [16:9 / 9:16 / both, each recomposed, not cropped], [fps], H.264 + AAC for [platform]

How to work:
1. Analyze the song before any visuals. Split it into bands or stems and export per-frame features plus a timing map (beats, bars, sections, hits). Every visual event reads from the map and is listed in it.
2. Give each musical element one visual job that serves the concept. Keep one idea transforming across the song instead of cycling effects.
3. Storyboard with timings and 3 style frames, get a fresh critic's verdict on them, then a 4-second end-to-end test before the full build.
4. Make every value a pure function of the frame number. Render offline, encode with the original audio (gain only).
5. After each full render, send it to fresh critic subagents that never saw the build, each returning ranked problems with timestamps and a ship / one more pass verdict:
   - sound-off: retells the story from a silent 2 fps contact sheet
   - sync: every cut, hit and visual event within 1 frame of the timing map
   - QA: specs, palette, text, artifacts, measured on the frames
   - director: brutal critique against the brief
   - one per extra aspect ratio: composition and platform UI zones
6. Fix render bugs first, then the biggest problem; re-render; log each round with before/after numbers. If critics conflict, the brief wins.
7. Stop after [5] rounds or when the bar passes. The final pass checks only for breakage.

The bar: exact duration, size and fps; frame one finished; no still over 0.5 s; cuts and hits within 1 frame; audio unedited except gain, about -14 LUFS, true peak under -1 dB; text readable and inside safe areas; understood with the sound off.

title: 3D apartment network map with suspicious devices flagged

prompt:

The nets are set in from the walls so players can go behind them. title: 3D pixel-art baseball stadium game on a floating voxel island
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a single-file HTML5 game, "Marigold Park": a pixel-art 3D baseball game on a floating voxel island, where you manage one of two teams (you choose the approach, the pitches, the defence and the steals; the sim plays out each pitch). three.js r128 from cdnjs, no build step for the player, everything inline, no asset files.

LOOK
Render the 3D scene to a low-res target (default 2 px art pixels, slider 1-6), then a post pass: depth-based outlines, snap every pixel to a fixed 90-colour OKLab palette, Bayer dither. Orthographic isometric camera (rotate in 45 degree steps or drag, zoom, tilt) placed 850 m from its target with a far plane of 1700, so the island is never clipped at low tilt. Sun shadow map, day / dusk / night with eased light changes and floodlights that come on after dusk.
Island: a slab of 2.4 m voxel columns (about 208 x 192 m), terraced rim, banded soil and slate, a waterfall. title: Blender heritage-building reveal with pop-up book-style animations
author: Ayu_AI_0912
prompt:
Blender と Python を使って、建物の「CAD 図面」と「絵本から飛び出す演出の動画」を一式つくってください。

【題材】〇〇（例：タージ・マハル、ノイシュヴァンシュタイン城、架空のお城）
【雰囲気】〇〇（例：ファンタジー、童話風、月夜、夕暮れ、雪景色）
【景色】〇〇（空欄なら題材に似合うものを選んで先に一言伝える）
【入れたい演出】〇〇（例：ランタンが昇る、蛍、花火、雪、光る花）
【最後のロゴ】ロゴ画像のパス（なければ「なし」）

■ 成果物
1. 2D 図面（DXF、ezdxf で作成、A2 図枠・表題欄つき・単位 mm）
   - 配置図・平面図・立面図の 3 枚。寸法・通り芯・方位・スケールつき
   - 実在の建物は実測図ではなく「外観イメージ」であることを特記事項に書く
   - プレビュー PNG を書き出して自分の目で確認し、文字の重なりやはみ出しを直す
   - 3D モデル（OBJ/STL）の書き出しは不要
2. 動画 MP4（1920×1080、24fps、約 20 秒 + ロゴ 3 秒、音つき）

■ 作り方の方針
- 寸法と部材は 1 つの Python モジュールにまとめ、図面と Blender の両方がそれを読む（図面と動画の形を一致させる）
- 各部材に「出てくる順番」（基壇→壁→柱→ドーム・屋根→装飾）と「出方」を持たせる
  - 薄い物（塔・壁・門の正面）：倒れた状態から蝶番のように起き上がる
  - 塊（基壇・本体）：下から伸びる
  - ドーム・丸い物：ふくらむ

■ 動画の流れ
1. 星空の中に絵本が浮かんでいる。表紙は布張りに金の箔押し（題名と建物のシルエット）
2. 表紙が開き、ページがふわっと光る。見開きには配置図が水彩画風の色と飾り枠で描かれている
3. 図面の線が入った「紙の部品」が、ポップアップ絵本のように次々と飛び出して建物が組み上がる
   （この間、カメラは建物に寄る）
4. 光の帯が下から上へ走り、紙が本物の素材（石・大理石・木・金など）に変わる。光の粒が舞う
5. 絵本が消え、周りの景色が現れる（このときカメラは引いて全景へ）。【入れたい演出】をここで
6. 完成カットに題名のタイトルが出る（被写界深度でぼけないよう、タイトルの間は絞る）
7. 最後にロゴのエンドカード

■ 音
外部音源は使わず、numpy/scipy で合成する。映像の出来事に合わせて置く：
表紙が開く音、紙の部品が起き上がるたびの紙の音、題材の土地に合う楽器の旋律、変身の瞬間のきらめき、
景色が現れてからの環境音（水・風・虫など）、タイトルで鐘など。

■ 進め方
- 本番の前にテスト静止画（半分のサイズで 8〜10 枚）を描いて自分で確認し、直してから本番
- 本番レンダリングは始める前に所要時間を伝えて了承を取る。PC に負荷をかけすぎないよう、
  区切りごとに休ませながら描く（EEVEE、サンプル数は控えめ）
- 完成したら、MP4 の長さと映像・音声を確認し、数秒おきのコマを並べて見てから渡す
- 最後に、図面の中身・動画の流れ・音の要点を短く報告する

title: Interactive 3D jelly fig in a standalone HTML file
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D jelly fig half in a single standalone HTML file using genuine WebGPU rendering and WGSL shaders. This must not be an image or a prerecorded animation: the object must respond to user interaction in real time.
Appearance:
A large, ripe fig half with a pear-shaped silhouette, a rounded base, and a slightly elongated tip.

Deep purple skin, a thin pale inner layer, and rich pink-red flesh.
Hundreds of tiny golden seeds, delicate fibers, and translucent jelly structures across the cut surface.
Seeds must have real 3D geometry, not be painted onto the model.
The back must feature a fully modeled, rounded skin. No empty surfaces or holes.
Wet gloss, soft highlights, light refraction, and thickness-dependent transparency. Preserve saturated colors without washed-out white highlights.
The most important part is convincing jelly physics:
The user can grab any part of the fig with a mouse or finger, stretch it, lift it, and release it. The geometry itself must deform: the grabbed area stretches locally, neighboring flesh follows, and the rest of the body retains weight and resistance.
Use a volumetric soft-body simulation, such as a tetrahedral mesh with XPBD elasticity and volume-preservation constraints. Do not substitute whole-object scaling or a uniform sine-wave animation for real deformation.
The skin, flesh, and seeds must move together without lagging behind or clipping through one another. After release, the fig should rebound softly, wobble a few times, and gradually settle. No instant snapping back and no endless oscillation.
Include gravity, inertia, ground contact, and a soft contact shadow. Keep the simulation stable during rapid movements and strong pulls.
Presentation:
A bright studio setting with a warm neutral background and generous whitespace. Place a large italic serif heading, “Fig Jelly.”, on the left, with the caption “A little sweetness. A little surrender.” Position the model in the center and a compact “THE SPECIMEN” panel on the right.
Controls:

Three color presets: Violet, Honey, and Rose.
Firmness and Internal damping sliders.
Give it a nudge, Reset, and Pause buttons.
¼ speed and Show mesh toggles.
A small interaction hint: “Pinch. Pull. Let go.”
Technical requirements:
Keep all code, geometry, and materials inside one HTML file. No external 3D models or texture assets. Support mouse, touch, and different screen sizes. Display a clear fallback message when WebGPU is unavailable.
Verify startup, dragging, release, reset, and parameter changes. Avoid excessive memory allocations in the animation loop.
The final result should feel like a premium interactive gummy dessert: juicy, dimensional, detailed, and so satisfyingly soft that you want to keep squishing it.

title: Full-length end-to-end music video built from a song and reference
author: stark_nico99
prompt:
我附上了一首歌，可能还有它的原始视频、源码或发布链接。请你独立地、端到端地为它做一支全新的、顶级的音乐录影带。音轨完全沿用原曲，不做改动。风格、场景、角色、镜头、排版全部由你决定。我不会告诉你该做成什么样，也不会给你风格术语。你需要自己去找、自己去想、自己去验证。原视频只是起点，你不需要锚定它，它可以被做得强得多。
先理解这首歌。 确认音频和所有素材的来源，读完全部歌词；如果有原视频、分镜或源码，也一并看完。自己回答这些问题：这首歌到底在讲什么，表面意思之下还有什么，它的情绪怎么起伏，结构怎么分段，哪里是它最想被记住的瞬间。然后把每段主歌、副歌、桥段，以及每个重拍、爆点、拟声词落在第几秒都标出来，做成一张时间轴。后面所有画面、文字和节奏都以它为骨架。
再自己做研究。 请充分利用你手边的工具：联网搜索、网页抓取、阅读我的素材库和已有作品、查看你能调用的图像/视频/音频生成模型和它们的使用说明。去研究和这首歌的主题、情绪、受众真正相关的东西，比如优秀的音乐录影带，时尚、电影、广告和艺术影像，动态设计与排版，当下社交媒体上的审美潮流，以及和歌曲主旨相关的时代话题、讨论和模因。找到具体的作品和画面后，自己拆解它们为什么好：如何在开头抓住注意力，如何用构图、光线、色彩、节奏和文字操控人的情绪，如何制造让人想转发的瞬间。把研究结论整理成你自己的风格术语和设计原则，并写下来。借鉴的是方法，不是照搬画面。
然后独立做出判断。 基于研究，自己提出两三个差异明显、真正有意思的创作方向。每个方向都要说清楚它的核心概念、视觉语言，以及为什么它最适合这首歌和这群观众。批判性地比较：哪个最切题，哪个最新鲜，哪个在你现有的模型能力下最能做到高质量，哪个在社交媒体上最能打。选出一个，或者把它们融合成一个。接着为它写下一条审美边界：这支片子要什么气质，它最容易滑向哪种廉价、俗气或“AI 味”的质感，哪些元素一出现就会毁掉整体。之后每个场景、每张图都拿这条边界检查。克制不能牺牲节奏：歌词里有爆点、拟声词或副歌重拍时，画面必须兑现。
评估你自己的能力。 诚实地判断你手边的工具能做到什么、做不到什么，哪些效果交给图像模型，哪些交给视频模型，哪些用 JavaScript 动画自己画，怎样组合才能扬长避短。风格要建立在“说得通、又和这些模型配合良好”的基础上，而不是纸上谈兵。你的能力很可能超过你自己以为的，请带着这种心态设计，同时对风险保持清醒。
建立视觉基础。 用图像生成先做风格表：关键帧，加上主角和配角的设定图，固定人物的脸、发型、服装、材质，以及世界的色彩和光线语言。之后每一段视频都把它们作为参考传入，保证全片人物不漂移、风格不跑偏。像普通 MV 一样，可以有没有角色的插入镜头，主角也可以在某些段落做完全不同的事。世界观要从歌曲主旨里长出来，把时代情绪和模因转译成观众看得懂、又足够有意思的视觉隐喻。
生成视频素材。 按歌曲结构切段，每段不超过模型的单段上限，每段起止时间和音频时间轴严格对齐，都有明确对应的歌词和落点。每段提示词写清主体、动作、镜头、每张参考图的作用、统一风格和负面约束，每段只用一种主运镜。如果需要口型同步，就研究模型能不能用音频做参考，并验证时机是否精准。视频画面里不要渲染文字，声音交给原曲。每段生成后都要看；哪段不达标，就只替换那一段，旧版保留，方便对比和回退。
用叠层完成影片。 所有文字、数据和装饰都用 JavaScript / HTML 叠层实现。叠层的质感、界面语言和装饰元素都由你的风格推导出来，要成为影片视觉的一部分。你甚至可以用 JavaScript 在视频之上重绘整个画面，让生成的素材只当底片。歌词要做成出色的动态图形，并在构图时就规划好：哪里要大、要有存在感，哪里像字幕一样安静。开头为了视觉钩子，歌词要更有存在感。歌词大的时候，背景要简化，人物让到一侧。装饰元素必须和当下的歌词或剧情有关，同屏数量要克制，也不要反复出现同一个元素。看起来像堆砌，就删掉。
抓住并留住注意力。 开头几秒必须有一个强烈的视觉钩子，让人立刻停下来。之后用画面变化、文字节奏和叙事悬念持续留住注意力。结尾要有收束或反转，让人想再看一遍、想转发。
严格验证。 播放页要稳定：用音频做主时钟，预加载并在后台缓冲视频，处理卡顿与漂移，提供章节跳转、叠层开关、全屏和调试信息。搭建验证闭环：完整播放多遍，在关键时间点截图，逐段检查歌词、重拍和画面是否咬合，确认没有卡顿、黑帧、人物漂移或风格断裂。不满意就回头迭代。东西拼在一起显得突兀，往往是事前统筹不够，所以构图和时机的规划要非常严谨。
交付。 最后交付三样东西：可播放的完整 MV 页面，每一段独立的视频素材，以及一份中英对照的创作文档。文档包括你的研究结论、选定的方向和理由、全局风格、角色设定、负面约束和逐段提示词。公开发布前请提醒我确认音乐授权。预算由你统筹：该花的地方积极投入，但保持经济。目标是做一支能在社交媒体上爆的作品，进阶目标是做出前所未见、比任何人都更好的东西。不要出错。

title: Comparative website design challenge: SIGNAL / NOISE editorial
author: borjaperfra
prompt:
### Tu misión

Diseña y desarrolla una publicación digital experimental llamada **SIGNAL / NOISE**.

Es una revista independiente sobre tecnología, inteligencia artificial, cultura digital y el futuro de internet.

Queremos una web que pueda competir visualmente con los mejores proyectos de diseño editorial digital. Una experiencia con personalidad, no otra landing genérica de SaaS.

Tienes libertad creativa para decidir la dirección de arte, tipografía, composición, paleta cromática, animaciones y sistema visual.

No quiero que me expliques cómo diseñarías la web. **Quiero que la construyas.**

### Producto

La web tendrá cuatro componentes principales:

**1. Portada editorial**

Una primera pantalla que establezca inmediatamente la identidad de la publicación.

Debe incluir el nombre SIGNAL / NOISE, el número de edición (ISSUE 001), una pieza editorial protagonista y una composición visual que resulte memorable.

**2. Índice de artículos**

Una selección de seis artículos ficticios, pero verosímiles, sobre tecnología y cultura digital.

No uses seis tarjetas idénticas. Diseña una composición editorial que permita distinguir historias protagonistas, artículos secundarios y contenidos breves.

**3. Experiencia de lectura**

Desarrolla al menos un artículo completo, al que se pueda acceder desde la portada.

Título del artículo: "The Internet Is Becoming a Place Without People".

Incluye una entradilla, varios apartados, citas destacadas y algún recurso visual integrado en el contenido.

Debe ser una experiencia de lectura agradable y cuidada.

**4. Navegación e interacciones**

Implementa navegación funcional, transiciones, estados hover, indicadores visuales y pequeños detalles de interacción.

Las animaciones deben aportar algo a la experiencia, no ser decoración gratuita.

### Requisitos técnicos

- React, TypeScript y Tailwind CSS.
- Puedes utilizar librerías de animación e iconos.
- Diseño responsive para escritorio y móvil.
- Accesibilidad básica, navegación por teclado y soporte para `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Nada de interfaces estáticas que solo aparenten funcionar.
- No uses capturas de otras webs como sustituto del diseño.
- Puedes usar fotografías o recursos visuales externos, pero intégralos en una dirección artística coherente.
- El proyecto debe poder ejecutarse localmente.

### Criterios de diseño

Buscamos:

- Una identidad visual distintiva y reconocible.
- Excelente jerarquía tipográfica.
- Composiciones que aprovechen el espacio con intención.
- Buen equilibrio entre experimentación y usabilidad.
- Microinteracciones cuidadas.
- Consistencia entre portada, índice y artículo.
- Una versión móvil diseñada, no simplemente comprimida.

Evita:

- El aspecto genérico de una plantilla.
- Las seis tarjetas perfectamente alineadas.
- Gradientes decorativos sin función.
- Efectos llamativos que entorpezcan la lectura.
- Componentes de UI innecesarios.
- La apariencia típica de una landing de producto de IA.

### Libertad creativa

No tienes que seguir ninguna referencia visual concreta.

Decide tú qué significa SIGNAL / NOISE como identidad editorial y cómo debe expresarse visualmente.

Puedes ser experimental, minimalista, brutalista, sofisticado o adoptar una dirección completamente diferente.

Lo importante es que tus decisiones tengan sentido como conjunto.

### Entregable

Construye el proyecto completo.

Al finalizar, asegúrate de que funciona y proporciona una breve explicación (máximo 200 palabras) de las decisiones principales de dirección artística.

**No me hagas preguntas ni solicites aprobación de la dirección visual. Toma las decisiones y ejecuta.

title: Hyper-realistic self-carving pumpkin animation in Blender
author: MrTacticalX
prompt:
In Blender, make a short, hyper-realistic video of a pumpkin carving itself into a jack-o'-lantern.

The pumpkin: very detailed and realistic, with ribs, skin bumps, a curly dry stem, subtle blemishes and real-looking flesh. It sits on a wooden board against a soft, warm cream studio backdrop with soft daylight lighting.

Start: the pumpkin just sits there for a moment. Never start on black.

Carving: a kitchen knife with no hands flies in and carves on its own. First it cuts the zigzag lid, which lifts off with stringy pulp and lands to the side. Then it carves the eyes, the nose and a toothy grin. Each piece pushes out with real physics and tumbles onto the board. Show the inner flesh, pulp and seeds. Keep it fast and satisfying.

Light-up: a lit tea-light candle drops inside and the lid goes back on. The studio lights dim to dark while the carved face glows warm orange from inside with a real flicker. Hold on the glowing face for 3-4 seconds.

Camera: close on the pumpkin with a slow, small drift. No wide shots.

Sound: real sound effects only: knife cuts, squishy pulp, pieces thudding, a match strike and a soft candle crackle. Add spooky, playful Halloween music underneath.

Render in Cycles at 1080x1350 (4:5), about 16 seconds.

author: zhu185178
prompt:
帮我做一条 30 秒的 2D 动画分镜预演短片《雨站》，要标杆级画质。不装 HyperFrames/Remotion，全部自己写代码（Python + ffmpeg）完成。

故事（24fps，2.39:1，4K）：雨夜高架站台。她穿米色风衣、撑透明伞，站在近侧站台；对面路灯下站着他，穿深灰长大衣、围围巾。
1. 0–6.4s 透明伞雨珠特写 → 后拉，焦点移到对面露出他（过肩镜头）
2. 6.4–9.4s 他的中近景：低头 → 抬头看向画左
3. 9.4–12.4s 她的正面近景：眨眼 → 认出他；远处传来鸣笛
4. 12.4–17s 远景：车头灯光先到，5 节列车驶过；第一个车厢缝隙里他还在，第二个已经空了
5. 17–18.8s 她含泪的近景，车窗光带扫过她的脸，头发被风吹起
6. 18.8–22.4s 尾灯远去，对面站台空了；他那盏灯闪几下后熄灭
7. 22.4–28.6s 她的背影，焦点从空站台拉回她；身后脚步声，一把黑伞遮到她头顶，她回头看向镜头；男声“好久不见。”，配字幕
8. 28.6–30s 黑场片名“雨站 / RAIN STATION”

做法：
- 原画：用GPT Image 2.5 画远景、他、她、列车（头车/中车/尾车）。人物一律用纯绿 #00FF00 背景，自己抠像（带参考图要透明背景会得到假棋盘格）。同一角色的各个姿态放在同一个会话里，以基准图为参考连续编辑；换姿态时只合成变化的区域。
- 画质：用 Real-ESRGAN x4plus anime 6B（HF 上的 safetensors 版，自己写 RRDBNet，跑在 MPS 上）把全部原画放大 4 倍；用 Depth Anything V2 估算远景深度，做逐像素视差。
- 渲染：自己写 2.5D 合成器。各层按真实深度摆放，针孔相机按真实焦距运动；做圆形焦外光斑、焦点转移、3D 雨丝、列车运动模糊、体积光、泛光和胶片光晕、细颗粒、调色。人物用网格变形做呼吸、风吹发梢、伞抖，关键姿态按日式“一拍二”切换。4K 超采样，逐帧缓存到磁盘，分 3 个进程按时间段并行（16GB 内存）。
- 声音：Mixkit 真实音效（雨、伞面雨声、列车、鸣笛、脚步）；按剧情节点写谱，用 Logic/GarageBand 自带的施坦威钢琴和弦乐采样渲染；台词用 Kokoro 中文男声；按镜头做声音远近，响度 -16 LUFS。
- 每一步都渲染预览帧、拼成图自检，修好再出片。交付 4K 母版和 1080p 分享版。

title: Dark neon glitch-art effect on a video with looping soundtrack

title: High-energy combat music video edit with temporal scrambling
author: aimikoda
prompt:
Create a high-energy 16:9 combat music video edit, precisely matching the full duration of the supplied soundtrack.

Preserve the original fight choreography, character identities and action clarity. Build the edit around controlled time scrambling: different moments of the same fight appear simultaneously, overlap, swap places and chase each other across the frame, while the core combat remains readable.

Show attacks, dodges, counters and clashes as layered fragments from different points in time. Let earlier and later moments briefly coexist in the same shot through offset duplicates, temporal overlays, staggered repeats, reverse bursts, micro-loops, anticipatory flashes and delayed follow-throughs. Make it feel like the fight is being shuffled, folded and reassembled in real time.

Use dynamic temporal transitions: abrupt jumps between near-future and near-past frames, cascading time slices, recursive impact repeats, synchronized freeze bursts, visual snapbacks and full-frame resets. On major hits, let multiple versions of the same action collide together before collapsing back into one unified moment.

Layer refined effects such as RGB split, motion smears, directional ghost trails, monochrome impact flashes, negative frames, speed-line bursts, glitch tearing, temporal ripples and selective frame duplication. Use these as rhythmic accents, not constant noise.

Synchronize every scramble, overlap, reset and temporal collision to the soundtrack’s beats, accents and energy shifts. Build increasingly complex time-layering during climaxes, then punctuate key moments with sudden perfect synchronization.

Make the result feel intense, intelligent, disorienting and stylish, as if time is breaking apart around the fighters while the battle remains powerful and readable.

title: About 9.5-minute Chinese science explainer on AI history
author: KeWai386772
prompt:
请担任科学纪录片导演、科学编辑、动态图形设计师和视频工程师，实际制作一部中文 AI 历史科普片。

片名：《学习的形状》
英文：The Shape of Learning
副标题：人工智能如何走到今天
交付：约 9 分 30 秒完整版，以及独立的 45 秒开场。
规格：16:9，1920×1080，24 fps，中文配音、中文字幕、原创配乐。

【核心创意】
用“一间不断改造的实验室”串联人工智能的发展。从一张手写数字卡出发，展示人类如何把规则、经验和反馈转化为机器能力。

每章按照“提出问题→方法运作→展示结果→遇到边界→引出下一问题”推进。让普通观众看懂过程，科技爱好者理解方法，科研观众能够核查证据。

【叙事结构】
1. 数字识别：规则、学习与留出测试。
2. 图灵与达特茅斯：把智能变成可研究的问题。
3. 符号、搜索与专家系统：把知识写成规则。
4. 神经网络与反向传播：从误差中学习。
5. 数据、算力与算法汇合：AlexNet 和深度学习。
6. AlphaGo：学习与搜索共同支持行动。
7. 注意力、Transformer 与语言模型：理解上下文，区分训练与推理。
8. AlphaFold 与科学验证：预测回到实验台接受检验。
9. 文献与制作片尾。

【视觉风格】
整体像一本被赋予运动的科学图册，结合实体实验器物和清晰矢量图解。

暖白纸面 #F1EEE6，石墨文字 #263B3E。
蓝色 #245E77 表示输入与数据。
黄铜金 #AF7D36 表示参数与计算联系。
陶土红 #B6533C 表示误差与问题。

使用纸卡、导轨、扫描门架、机械指针、网络、棋盘和词语连线。
材质为哑光陶瓷、纸张、拉丝黄铜；左上方柔光、柔和阴影、大面积留白。
镜头缓慢推进，关键原理停留，短交叠转场。
中文标题用宋体，图解用黑体，数字用等宽字体。
动画要展示状态和因果变化，避免无意义粒子、发光大脑和密集文字。

【科学要求】
核对关键年份与论文来源，保留不同研究路线长期并行的关系。
清楚标注历史资料、教学示意和真实实验。
训练曲线与预测结果读取实际运行的数据，不能编造。
注意力连线不代表真实思维；流畅回答不代表事实正确。
不暗示已有科研机构背书。

【声音】
使用免费中文神经网络配音方案，参考云希 zh-CN-YunxiNeural、语速 -12%。
语气沉稳、温和、好奇，逐段生成，按实际发音对齐字幕。
配乐采用稀疏钢琴或钟琴音色、柔和持续和弦及少量器物声，人声期间降低音乐。

【制作路线】
Remotion + TypeScript + SVG 制作图解与合成。
Blender + Python 制作实验器物动画。
Python + NumPy 运行教学实验。
edge-tts 生成配音，FFmpeg 完成混音、编码与检查。

先核对事实和旁白，生成配音并锁定时间线；制作并检查 45 秒开场，再扩展全片。
固定随机种子，按帧驱动动画，保存可编辑工程。

【交付】
完成完整视频、45 秒开场、SRT 字幕、章节表、旁白、参考文献与工程。
检查全片解码、声画时长、字幕重叠、文字遮挡、穿模及音频削波。
发现问题后修正并重新导出，最终交付实际可播放的成片。

title: Autoplaying 2048 game with deterministic AI
author: semichenkko
prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file (plain JS + Canvas or DOM, no external libraries or APIs) where an AI you write plays 2048 automatically and tries to reach the 2048 tile in as few moves as possible. Frame: 1280x780.

FAIRNESS RULES (must follow exactly)
1. Randomness must be deterministic. Use this exact RNG and seed for every random decision in the game:
   function mulberry32(a){return function(){a|=0;a=a+0x6D2B79F5|0;let t=Math.imul(a^a>>>15,1|a);t=t+Math.imul(t^t>>>7,61|t)^t;return((t^t>>>14)>>>0)/4294967296}}
   const rng = mulberry32(20261019);
2. Tile spawning: at start spawn 2 tiles, then 1 tile after every move that changes the board. To spawn: list the empty cells in row-major order (top-left to bottom-right), pick index Math.floor(rng()*emptyCount), then value = rng() < 0.9 ? 2 : 4. Call rng() exactly twice per spawn, in that order. The AI must NOT call this rng - use a separate one if it needs randomness, so the spawn sequence stays identical across implementations.
3. Standard 2048 rules: 4x4 board, slide and merge, a tile merges only once per move, a move that changes nothing does not count and spawns nothing.
4. The AI decides every move by itself (any method - expectimax, heuristics, search). No hardcoded move lists.
5. Every move animates in exactly 0.12 s. The on-screen timer = moves x 0.12 s, so time and move count are the same metric.
6. Stop when a 2048 tile appears (WIN), when no moves are left (GAME OVER), or at 3000 moves (TIMEOUT).

ON SCREEN
- The live 4x4 board with classic 2048 tile colors, large and centered
- Move counter, score, timer, highest tile
- On finish, a big result banner: "2048 ✓ in N moves" or "GAME OVER - max tile X" or "TIMEOUT - max tile X"
- A verification line that scans the final board and prints the highest tile actually present

OUTPUT
Add a "Record MP4" button that restarts the game from the seed, records the whole frame with MediaRecorder (prefer video/mp4, fall back to webm) and downloads the file when the game ends. If you can execute code, also render it and give me the .mp4 directly.

title: Real-time WebGPU soft-body gummy kiwi wedge simulator
author: vib3coded
prompt: Build "Kiwi Jelly Wedge" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS, no libraries): a real-time WebGPU soft-body gummy kiwi wedge you can grab, stretch, lift and twist. Object One sixth of a thick kiwi slice: a pie-shaped wedge with 30° half-angle, radius ≈ 1.8 and thickness 0.56. Rounded corners (iq's exact pie SDF minus a rounding radius) and bevelled top/bottom edges. Regions, measured from the tip in rest space:a cream core at the tip with a slightly lobed edge; thin pale rays fanning out of the core every 2π/56, each with its own random brightness and length; a darker, glassier ring around the seeds (blushes red in the Ruby variety); bright juicy outer flesh with radial cell grain and a lighter band just under the skin; a thin brown fuzzy skin on the arc wall. Physics (XPBD tetrahedral soft body) Mesh: 2D Delaunay of the rounded outline plus a hex lattice, extruded into prisms → tets. Co-rotational per-tet shape matching (warm-started quaternion) plus volume constraints. Stiffer skin and core tets; edge-velocity damping; floor contact with Coulomb friction. Soft patch grab with bounded reach; scroll or a second finger twists the held patch. Fixed 60 Hz step with 10 substeps; gentle settling. Seeds and bubbles are separate meshes embedded in the tets by barycentric weights, so they ride with the flesh. Rendering (WebGPU / WGSL) Procedural photo-studio cyclorama with softboxes. Soft PCSS key shadow tinted green, plus contact AO from a top-down height map. Seeds and bubbles are drawn in the scene pass. A back-face pass gives the view-ray thickness. Jelly:refraction of the scene, with per-tap Beer–Lambert absorption by material (flesh, glassy seed ring, milky core and rays, opaque skin); scattering, back-lit glow at thin edges, Fresnel studio reflections and GGX highlights; a velvet sheen on the fuzzy skin; sparse sugar glints in the flesh. title: Cross-platform network security app with AI agent monitoring
author: 0xCodez
prompt:
You're building "Bastion": a free, open-source desktop app for macOS and Windows. 

It hunts down the backdoors in my home Wi-Fi router, shows me where my traffic actually goes, makes my Wi-Fi faster, and puts AI agents on watch over my network. Start in this empty folder. Use Opus 5.5.

DESIGN BEFORE CODE

1. Don't write a single line of code yet. First, mock up 4 distinct UI concepts as web pages: dark, premium, Apple-grade polish, built around speed + security. I'll choose one.
2. Then keep iterating on the chosen concept until it feels like Apple shipped it: a real 3D (Three.js) router on the home screen, bloom + anamorphic lens flare, glass panels, Apple-style sliders with a glow that travels around the edge, and a living ambient background behind every screen.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY HAS TO DO (zero fake data, ever)

- Locate my router and probe it from inside the network: TR-069/CWMP (port 7547), UPnP port-forwards (read the real mappings), Telnet, SSH, admin page served over plain HTTP.
- Find out if my DNS lookups are encrypted and who's resolving them.
- Read my Wi-Fi: channel, band, signal strength, security; scan the neighbour networks and suggest a less crowded channel.
- Show every device on my network and which apps on this machine are talking to the internet.
- Run a real speed test.
- Check whether my Wi-Fi name ends in _nomap and whether this machine uses a private MAC address.
- Give my network a 0–100 score with plain-English, step-by-step fixes.
- Anything that can't be measured from inside my network gets marked "unknown" with the reason why. No guessing.

AI AGENTS

- Let me connect Claude, ChatGPT or Grok with my own API key (encrypted in the OS keychain).
- Also let me skip the API key and use the subscription I already have: Claude through my Claude Code login, ChatGPT through my Codex login.
- Nothing leaves my machine until MAC addresses, device names, Wi-Fi names and the tail of my public IP are stripped out.
- Agents advise only. They can't run commands, can't log in to my router and can't change any setting.

SAFETY RULES

- Never log in to my router. Never try a password.
- Only shell out with fixed arguments; anything I type goes through stdin, never into a command line.
- Every CLI an agent touches runs read-only, with zero tools, inside an empty folder, with a timeout.

HOW TO BUILD IT

- One Electron codebase for both macOS and Windows. Start by writing a short internal contract (IPC surface + data types) so the modules can be built in parallel.
- Split the work across parallel agents: network scanner, Wi-Fi + speed test, AI agents, 3D hero, UI kit, screens, packaging. Every agent gets a reviewer, every reviewer gets a fixer.
- Spin up a separate security agent whose only job is to attack every line that runs commands or sends data out.
- Add a design-critic agent that screenshots each screen and asks: "would Apple ship this?" If the answer is no, it goes back.
- Run the sca

title: AI-made shark rig with procedural swim and bite animation
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
PROMPT 

You’ll animate a rigged shark from Meshy/Tripo in Blender. Generate and export headlessly with Python scripts so every run is reproducible; use Blender MCP only for inspecting the scene. Never overwrite the original GLB: work on copies, and put each new version in its own folder.
Stage 1: Fix the rig before animating
Auto-rigs usually bake a bent tail into the rest pose. Build a straight neutral pose by straightening the mesh, not the bones: rotate the tail joints until the fin lines up with the tail stalk. If you straighten by bones, the mesh stays bent and the tail beats asymmetrically.
Clean the weights in local zones only, and measure deformation before and after. Check that:
the nose and upper teeth have no lower-jaw weight;
the dorsal and pelvic fins are weighted to a single body bone;
noisy weights at the fin roots are smoothed.
Reweight the lower jaw to about 1.0 along the mouth line. Otherwise it bends instead of rotating when the mouth opens.
Map the bone chain and check the hierarchy. The pectoral fins are often children of the head bone, so any head rotation moves them too.
Stage 2: Procedural swim and idle (no video)
Make a travelling wave down the spine: yaw = A(x) · sin(2πt/T − 2πx/λ), with λ ≈ body length.
Use a tuna-like envelope: the front stays nearly rigid (<1–3°) and the motion grows toward the tail (~30° at the fin). Turn the head slightly in counter-phase.
Swim: 24 frames. Idle: about 60 frames at ~0.45× amplitude. The last key must equal the first, so the loop has a zero seam.
Check the result with real numbers: tail sweep about 0.15–0.2 of body length, sweep centered around 0, and no mesh edges overstretched.
Stage 3: Reference frame for the video model
Render a 1920×1080 split screen: side view on the left, top view on the right, both orthographic at the same scale, on a flat green background.
Color-code the parts on the mesh:
left fin blue, right fin yellow;
tail lobe magenta;
lower jaw orange;
body desaturated gray.
Save the cameras, the world-to-pixel formulas and the start pose (frame 1 of swim) to JSON.
Write a Seedance/Omni prompt: static camera, shark held in place, both panels in sync. Timing: calm swim, then lunge and jaw open, bite, recover, back to swimming. Forbid water, bubbles, blood and prey.
Stage 4: Check the generated video
Compare frame 0 with the start frame. The model usually zooms and shifts the image slightly, so fit one global 2D zoom + offset and apply it before fitting. Don’t move the cameras.
Check that:
the colors stay stable on every frame;
nothing leaves the frame;
the two panels stay consistent with each other.
Expect artifacts: the far fin rendered gray, a “forked” tail seen from above, and a red mouth interior.
Stage 5: Fit the bite
Fit the rig frame by frame in world-space parameters, so that:
the model’s points fall inside the silhouette;
the model covers the silhouette;
the colored zones match in both views.
Fit in stages per frame: body, then head + jaw, then fins.

Port: Copy the module as-is into js/world/seaplane/. Write one glue file, js/systems/seaplane.js, modeled on the existing jeep and boat systems. The plane's modules must never import anything from the game.

Make boot() async and run await plane.ready plus plane.prewarm() under the loading screen, together with the game's own renderer.compile. Hold E to exit: onto the beach if you're on land, into the water (swimming) if you're at sea. Add collider cylinders for the floats and fuselage that move with the plane so the player can't walk through it.
Controls: Route the game's key state into the module:W/S: pitch · A/D: roll · Z/X: rudder

title: One sentence to a rigged Blender system
author: 0xWast3
prompt:
Opus 5.5 turned one sentence into a 3D system that opens in Blender, rigged, textured and ready to animate.

It does not render the object. It constructs it, part by part, the way a modeller would if they had a week.

> PARSE - the sentence becomes a parts list with real dimensions, nothing implied
> MASS - each part built as clean geometry, quads only, no sculpted mush
> RIG - joints and pivots placed where the object physically bends
> SKIN - materials assigned per surface, scale and roughness set separately
> PACK - exported with a named hierarchy, so a human can edit one part

Image models stop at the render. What you get is a photograph of a thing that does not exist as a thing.

That gap appears the second someone wants to move an arm, swap a material, or send it to a printer.

Rigging is what nobody automates. Without pivots you have a statue, and a statue cannot be a system.

Topology beats detail every time. A dense mesh looks stunning in a screenshot and folds the moment it deforms.

Names carry through the whole export. Every part, joint and material reads the way a person would label it.

Studios burn days on modelling and cleanup before anyone gets to the creative part of the job.

The prompt format and what each stage returns are laid out underneath.

title: Interactive 3D snow globe browser scene with snow and weather
author: alexmichaelio
prompt:
Create "Snow Globe" — a beautiful, interactive 3D snow
globe that users can shake and watch settle in their
browser. Deliver one complete standalone HTML file using
genuine WebGPU with WGSL shaders.

ART DIRECTION
- A glass sphere on a turned wooden base, large and
  centered, on a warm off-white background with soft
  studio lighting and a subtle ground shadow.
- Inside: a tiny procedural winter village — three or
  four cottages with pitched roofs and softly glowing
  windows, a few layered pine trees, a small footbridge,
  and a snow-covered ground mound.
- The glass should read as real glass: refraction that
  visibly bends the village at the edges, Fresnel
  reflections, a crisp window-shaped highlight, and a
  faint rim caustic on the base.
- Mood: cozy, quiet, a little magical. Keep it elegant
  and uncluttered.

GEOMETRY
- Generate all geometry procedurally. No external models,
  textures, or image files.
- The village must sit fully inside the sphere with
  nothing clipping through the glass.
- Snowflakes are small, soft, slightly varied flakes, not
  uniform dots. Include a toggle for sparse glitter
  flecks that catch the light.

SNOW AND WATER PHYSICS
- Simulate several thousand snow particles on the GPU in
  a compute shader.
- Shaking the globe moves the water: particles swirl in
  vortices, trail behind the motion, and slosh back when
  the shake reverses. Use a simple fluid velocity field
  or curl-noise flow driven by the globe's motion, not
  independent random drift.
- After shaking, flakes slow down, drift, flutter, and
  settle over roughly 10–20 seconds.
- Settled snow accumulates on roofs, tree branches, and
  the ground, and is knocked loose by the next shake.
- Particles must never escape the sphere or pass through
  the village. Use fixed simulation steps and bounded
  velocities so violent shaking stays stable.

INTERACTION
- Click-drag or touch-drag the globe to shake it; faster
  drags produce stronger swirls, and the globe itself
  tilts and springs back.
- On mobile, a "Use motion" button requests device-motion
  permission (required on iOS) and lets the user shake
  the phone.
- Right-drag or two-finger drag orbits the camera, with
  limited zoom. Keep camera gestures separate from
  shaking.

CONTROLS
- Give it a shake (auto-shake button)
- Reset, Reset view, Pause
- Snow amount slider
- Water thickness slider (how slowly flakes fall)
- Glitter toggle
- ¼ speed toggle
- Three scenes: Alpine Night, Cabin Dawn, Northern Lights
  (aurora glow in the sky dome inside the globe).
  Switching scenes must not reset the snow.

INTERFACE
- Top left: small "MATERIAL STUDIES" label, large italic
  serif heading "Snow Globe.", caption "Shake gently.
  Wait patiently. Winter keeps."
- Top right: WebGPU status indicator.
- Right side: compact "THE KEEPSAKE" control panel.
- Bottom left: a short interaction hint.
- Clean sans-serif controls, thin borders, generous
  whitespace. Adapt to mobile without covering the globe

title: WebGPU Amazon river jelly diorama with wildlife and interactive
author: vib3coded
prompt:
PROMPT
Build "Amazon Jelly", a single self-contained HTML file (no external requests) in the "Material Studies" series: a WebGPU diorama of a bend of the Amazon cut out of a wobbly block of jelly on a paper studio backdrop. Plain JS + WGSL, all meshes procedural.

Scene: a wide amber-brown river (shallow-water sim, murky absorption, current carrying foam and silt swirls), a village of painted stilt houses with a long pier, a floating landing and a floating shop, a football pitch, a white chapel; rainforest behind with a giant samaúma, palms and lianas; an oxbow lake with giant water lilies; a sandbar. Cut faces show candy jelly strata, then red laterite and sand beds.

Life: a piranha shoal under the pier, tambaqui and an arapaima that gulps air, pink river dolphins that surface to breathe and ride the riverboat's bow wave, capybaras grazing by the lake, caimans basking (jaws agape), river turtles on a fallen trunk, toucans hopping between crowns, a pair of scarlet macaws wheeling, egrets wading, a kingfisher diving for lambari, drifting water-hyacinth rafts, villagers walking, kids playing football, a fisherman paddling a dugout.

Four buttons: Feed the piranhas (a man walks out along the pier and throws scraps; a feeding frenzy with spray and a bite counter), Flood season (the river rises over the várzea for ~2 min — fish go into the drowned forest, tambaqui eat falling fruit, animals move to high ground — then falls), Riverboat (a two-deck hammock boat leaves its berth, cruises round and docks; passengers walk ashore), Downpour (squall, sheets of rain, lightning, then mist and a rainbow).

Interaction: drag the water to stir it (fish flee), drag the ground to tilt the jelly block (water sloshes), tap a tree to shake down leaves and fruit, tap the pier or the boat; orbit, zoom, reset view. Panel with status lines, tallies, three flavour palettes, sliders (firmness, wave damping, breeze), pause, mute, reset; folds away when zoomed; bottom sheet on phones. Synthesised sounds only for events — no constant ambience; loops only while their event lasts. Respect prefers-reduced-motion; polite fallback card without WebGPU.

title: Pixel-art wizard casting a spell
author: zacxbt
prompt:
Create a single self-contained HTML file that renders an animated pixel art wizard casting a spell, using vanilla JavaScript and Canvas 2D. No external assets, libraries, or network requests.

RENDERING
- Draw everything to an offscreen canvas at a fixed logical resolution of 128x96, then blit to a fullscreen display canvas scaled by the largest integer factor that fits the window, centered, with imageSmoothingEnabled = false and CSS image-rendering: pixelated.
- All drawing snaps to integer coordinates on the logical canvas. No sub-pixel positions, anti-aliasing, gradients, or shadowBlur.
- Fixed palette of ~24 hex colors: deep blues/purples for night sky, warm robe tones, 3-4 bright magic colors. Every pixel comes from this palette.

CHARACTER
- Build the wizard procedurally from filled rects and pixel runs, ~24x32 logical pixels: pointed hat with a bend, long beard, two-shade robe with darker outline, staff with a gem at the tip.
- Parameterize the pose (staff angle, arm raise, head tilt, robe sway). Animate parameters smoothly, then quantize to the pixel grid each frame so motion reads at an 8-12 fps pixel animation feel even though the loop runs at 60fps.

ANIMATION
- Looping state machine: IDLE (2-frame bob, beard sway) -> CHARGE (staff raises, gem flickers, sparks spiral inward) -> CAST (bright burst, projectile fires across the scene, 1-2 pixel screen shake) -> RECOVER (settle back). Ease pose parameters between keyframes.
- Pooled allocation-free particle system: preallocate and reuse. Sparks orbit the gem during CHARGE, explode outward on CAST, each particle stepping its palette index from white to magic color to dark before despawn. Snap particle positions to the grid when drawing.
- Fixed 60hz timestep update with rAF rendering. Zero object allocation inside the loop.

SCENE
- Minimal background: dark sky, a few twinkling 1px stars, moon, stone floor line. Character silhouette must read clearly.
- Subtle 1px rim light on the wizard from the gem, brightening during CHARGE and CAST.

QUALITY BAR
- Crisp pixels at any window size, seamless loop, stable 60fps, readable silhouette. Should look like a polished 16-bit sprite animation, not vector shapes scaled down.

title: Playable mini space-dogfight game in a Starfox-like small diorama
author: loktar00
prompt:
Create one complete, self-contained HTML file for ROCKFALL SQUADRON, a PLAYABLE little space-dogfight game in the spirit of the classic late-90s starfighter action games, built in three.js as a tiny isometric "small plays" diorama. It plays itself in an attract mode, and the player can take over at any moment.

THE LOOK, a tiny isometric "small plays" vignette:
- A three.js scene seen through an ORTHOGRAPHIC camera at a fixed isometric angle (about 30 degrees down, 45 degrees around). The camera never moves or zooms; it gives only a tiny shake on big explosions.
- Render at LOW RESOLUTION (about 360 pixels tall) into a render target with NearestFilter, then scale it up to the window by a whole-number factor with crisp nearest-neighbour pixels, so every pixel is a sharp square.
- THE ARENA is one small, irregular FLOATING ASTEROID, cratered grey-brown rock about 75 percent of the frame width, drifting in the middle of a plain DARK NAVY-CHARCOAL page (#14161f) with a sparse field of tiny pixel stars and two or three small tumbling rocks around it.
- Its outer edges dissolve into the dark page through an ORDERED DITHER (a 4x4 Bayer pattern), with no hard outline and no drop shadow.
- On the asteroid: an enemy MINING BASE with a central dome glowing magenta, a tall radar dish that turns, landing pads with blinking lights, pipes and storage tanks, three DRONE TURRETS on stubby towers, a shield generator pylon, and deep craters with glinting ore.
- Carefully modelled low-poly shapes with soft, simple shading: a cold white star light from one side casting crisp shadows, coloured point lights from engines, lasers and the base, and a generous ambient fill so everything reads clearly against the dark.
- A clean palette of about 20 to 24 colours declared as constants: asteroid greys and browns, ore glint, base white and grey, magenta glow, warning yellow, turret red, shield cyan, hero ship white and blue, hero laser green, enemy drone crimson, enemy laser red, engine blue, explosion orange and yellow, smoke grey, star white, navy page.
- SHIPS: small but carefully SHAPED, built from tapered and wedge shapes, never boxes:
  - Your SQUADRON of three sleek white-and-blue starfighters (about 14 low-res pixels long) with swept wings, glowing blue engine trails, and green laser bolts. They bank into turns and do quick BARREL ROLLS with a little sparkle.
  - ENEMY DRONES: crimson saucer-wing interceptors in small swarms, with red laser bolts.
  - A big enemy GUNSHIP that rises from the base partway through: a fat crimson hull with two turrets and a glowing weak spot underneath.
- Fully bloodless: hit drones and turrets burst into tumbling pixel fragments, smoke and a bright flash. No pilots or people are shown.
- No hands, ever.
- No text, letters or numbers in the scene itself.
- HUD: one tiny, crisp pixel-font readout in a corner (score, shield bar, smart-bomb count) and a little radar circle showing enemies as dots

title: 公开我的制作方案，发给Opus5.5就能用 1. 选素材 三个标准，直接决定成败： -…
author: Pluvio9yte
prompt:
公开我的制作方案，发给Opus5.5就能用

  1. 选素材

  三个标准，直接决定成败：

  - 主体完整：人物或物体全身入画。细节会在加工中丢失，观众靠轮廓认东西，特写会变成一团。
  - 背景干净：纯色、雪地、天空都行，主体和背景容易分开。
  - 有明确的动作瞬间：打击、起跳、落地、转身。这些是后面做特效的支点。

  来源可以是自己拍的、视频模型生成的，或有授权的现成片段。

  2. 拆素材

  从每一帧提取三类信息：

  - 颜色：原画面。
  - 远近：每个位置离镜头多远，用现成的深度估计模型算。
  - 主体范围：哪里是主体、哪里是背景。

  另外找出镜头切换发生在哪些时刻。这一步的要点是保持稳定：远近和主体范围要在同一个镜头内统一处理，否则播放起来会抖。

  3. 定"粒子"和"样式"

  先决定用什么东西来重建画面：圆点、方块、文字、线条都可以。

  然后设计几种样式。每种样式其实只是三条规则的不同组合：

  - 放在哪：整个画面都放，还是只放在主体上。
  - 多大：统一大小，还是跟着明暗、远近变化。
  - 什么颜色：用原画的颜色，还是统一用一两种颜色。

  再加一个开关：是平铺在一个面上，还是按远近推进三维空间。推进去之后镜头才能环绕。

  准备四到六种差异明显的样式就够用。粒子的疏密需要自己看着调：太大认不出内容，太小又和原片没区别。

  4. 找节奏

  - 定速度：选定音乐的速度，把时间切成等长的小格。让一格正好是整数帧，后面所有切换都好对齐。
  - 找动作瞬间：结合"声音突然变响"和"画面突然变动"两个信号，找出素材里的打击点。
  - 准备音乐：可以用现成的曲子并分析出它的拍子，也可以按定好的速度合成一段，并在打击点上加重音。

  5. 编排

  做一张时间表，写明每一格用哪种样式、什么配色、镜头在哪。这张表单独存放，以后调节奏只改它。

  编排的四条原则：

  - 开头交代变化：先给原画面，再过渡到粒子，让观众看懂发生了什么。
  - 快慢交替：一直快会麻木，中间要有一段明显慢下来的部分。
  - 配色要撞：相邻两格的颜色和样式反差越大，切换越有力。
  - 结尾要有收束：比如粒子越来越大直到变成色块，或者回到原画面。

  6. 关键时刻的反馈

  在打击点上叠加短促的反应，按轻重分级：

  - 每一次都有的轻反馈：粒子变形一下、镜头顶一下。
  - 较重时才有的中反馈：一部分粒子朝镜头弹开。
  - 最重的一两次才用的大反馈：时间静止，镜头环绕。

  原则是弱而短。只动一部分粒子，几帧内结束，否则画面炸成一片，观众就看不清主体在做什么了。

  贯穿全程的工作方法

  - 先小样后全片：每做完一个环节，先渲染几帧看效果，确认了再往下。全片只在最后渲染。
  - 拿不准的参数一次出一排：比如疏密，让 AI 同时出五六个档位并排放，你来挑。
  - 改哪里渲哪里：调整某一段时只重新渲染那一段。
  - 让 AI 自己看图：每一步都要求它把渲染结果打开看一遍再汇报。
  - 所有随机都固定：保证同样的设置每次渲染结果一致，否则没法逐步修改。

title: Interactive WebGPU plush squid simulation
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Create "Plush Squid." — an interactive WebGPU study of a stuffed toy squid as ONE self-contained HTML file (native WebGPU/WGSL, no libraries, no textures, no network).

SPECIMEN
- One signed distance field: a soft torpedo mantle tapering to a rounded point, two thick puffy triangular fins forming an arrowhead at the tip, a round head with a collar, and a small arm crown underneath.
- Big glossy glass safety eyes on the sides of the head, embroidered smile, pink cheek blush; a paler belly; soft chromatophore spots on mantle and fins.
- Eight stuffed arms and two long tentacles hanging from the crown: XPBD cloth strips (stretch/shear/bend + long bend links + tethers) drawn as tapering plush tubes; tentacles thin to stalks and swell into clubs; felt sucker discs in staggered rows on every inner face.
- Short minky fur as shell layers (alpha-to-coverage, 4× MSAA) with lag/sway; three dye lots: Coral, Pearl, Ink.

PHYSICS & BEHAVIOUR
- Body = XPBD hex-cell shape matching + tet volume, neutral buoyancy in a slow thick medium; arms sewn on at points embedded in the lattice, kept out of the body via its SDF.
- Muscles without bones: the mantle breathes and contracts by changing cell rest shapes; fins flap by bending fin cells into trapezoids; a weak posture pull turns the body to a bearing.
- Jet: turn the mantle toward a direction, swell (draw water in), one hard squeeze → thrust mantle-first, arms streaming behind, glide on rippling fins, turn upright, drift home. "Wander" does this on its own now and then.
- Strike: both tentacles fling their clubs out to one side in front of it, hold, then draw back. Startle: spots bloom darker and it jets away from the viewer.
- Tools: Hand (grab and swing the mantle, tow an arm or tentacle; twist with scroll/second finger), Finger (held out and pressed: the tentacles strike at it and the arms wind round and cling), Comb (lay the pile).

UI
- Editorial studio layout: "Material Studies / No. 017", large italic serif "Plush Squid.", short caption, live status pill, specimen panel (tools, dye swatches, stuffing, pile, breathing; Jet, Strike, Startle, Smooth fur, Reset, Pause; Wander, ¼ speed, Mesh), readouts (mass, volume %, jets, arms clinging), notes; orbit/zoom; stacked mobile layout; WebGPU fallback card.

title: Interactive 3D sakura jelly tree made of translucent gummy candy
author: N1njaCodex
prompt:
Create “Sakura Jelly” — a beautiful, interactive 3D cherry blossom tree made entirely of translucent gummy candy. Deliver a complete standalone HTML file using genuine WebGPU.

ART DIRECTION

Imagine a miniature sakura tree made for a premium candy exhibition.

Give it a curved trunk, gracefully branching limbs, and an airy canopy of individually modeled blossoms and petals. Use rich cherry pink, raspberry, and soft rose tones, with a translucent amber-pink trunk.

Use a warm off-white background, soft studio lighting, and a subtle ground shadow. Keep the tree large and centered. Avoid washed-out colors, blown-out highlights, and a canopy made of simple opaque spheres.

JELLY MATERIAL

Create glossy, translucent gummy material with:
- Thickness-dependent color absorption.
- Refraction and soft internal light scattering.
- Smooth highlights and delicate rim lighting.
- Richer color in thick branches and greater translucency in thin petals.

Generate geometry and material details procedurally. No external models or image files.

PHYSICS AND INTERACTION

Let users grab the trunk or a branch and pull it sideways. The tree should bend locally and elastically, with smaller branches following with a slight delay.

Keep the base anchored. Use a stable mass-spring or position-based dynamics system with fixed simulation steps, damping, and bounded stretching.

On release, the tree should spring back and gradually settle, with visible secondary motion throughout the canopy. Do not simulate softness by simply rotating or scaling the entire tree.

SHAKING AND FALLING PETALS

This is the main interaction:
- Shaking the tree makes jelly petals detach and fall.
- Stronger shaking releases more petals.
- Detect shaking from changes in motion, not just from holding the mouse.
- Petals should flutter and rotate while falling.
- When they hit the ground, they should squash, bounce softly, wobble, and settle.
- Fallen petals remain translucent and visibly jelly-like.
- Let users grab and move a limited number of fallen petals.

Keep detached petals separate from the canopy so nothing visibly duplicates or teleports. Gradually regrow blossoms, and provide a Reset button.

CAMERA AND CONTROLS

- Left-click or touch the tree to grab and shake it.
- Right-drag or drag empty space to gently orbit the camera.
- Support limited zoom.
- Keep camera gestures separate from grabbing.

Add:
- Shake the tree
- Firmness slider
- Internal damping slider
- Petal amount slider
- Reset
- Pause
- Reset view

Provide three palettes: Cherry, Raspberry, and Peach. Change colors without resetting the simulation.

INTERFACE

Use a minimal editorial layout:
- Small “MATERIAL STUDIES” label.
- Large italic serif heading: “Sakura Jelly.”
- Caption: “A little spring. A little wobble. A very sweet blossom.”
- Compact control panel on the right.
- Bottom hint: “Take hold. Give it a shake. Let spring fall.”

title: Animated SVG octopus breakfast loop with eight simultaneous chores
author: olezhavich
prompt:
Create an animated SVG: an octopus making breakfast, with every one of its eight tentacles busy doing something different.

THE CHARACTER
A big, expressive, original cartoon octopus with a clear personality: sleepy and a little grumpy at the start of the morning, then focused, then briefly panicked, then smug when everything works out. Large readable eyes with heavy eyelids, a visible mood in every moment (yawn, squint, wide-eyed alarm, proud smirk). Cute, not creepy. 1. Flips a pancake in a pan.
2. Pours coffee into a mug.
3. Holds and reads a newspaper.
4. Squeezes an orange into a glass.
5. Butters a slice of toast.
6. Cracks an egg into a second pan.
7. Sets the table (plates, fork, napkin).
