title: First-Person 3D Procedural Arms and Dynamic Grip Rigging in Three.js
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
TASK: Build production-grade first-person arms ("Hands 2.0") for a Three.js browser game, then fix them until every pose actually holds the object it should hold. Do the whole thing yourself with scripts, from generating the model to the in-game checks. I already did this once. Below is what works and the traps I fell into, so you don't repeat them.

━━━ PART 1 — THE MODEL (Blender + MPFB2, fully scripted) ━━━

1. Don't patch AI-generated "statue" arms (Meshy etc.). Chaotic topology with no edge loops at the joints and fingers baked into a pose will crease at every bend. Without clavicle and twist bones the wrist twists like a candy wrapper. Gluing separate generated parts together only adds seams to the same bad mesh. Start over with a real humanoid generator.

2. Use Blender (headless: `blender --background --python tools/hands/*.py`) + MPFB2 (MakeHuman, CC0) and its official asset packs. Put every step in a script so it can be rebuilt:
   - build_body.py: macro params (male, ~30 y/o, wiry and lean: muscle ~0.66, weight ~0.3) plus local arm targets.
   - build_arms.py: game skeleton with clavicle → shoulder → upperarm01/02 → lowerarm01/02 (twist bones!) → wrist → metacarpals → 3 phalanges per finger. Keep skin only from the elbow down and apply subdiv 1. Make the sleeve a separate mesh on the same bones, with real geometry for the rolled cuff. Accessories (watch, bracelet) are parented to forearm/wrist bones; watch hands are bones too.
   - build_tex.py: UVs, then bake veins, tendons and knuckles into geometry and normals. Author every detail in bone-local 3D space so it survives re-UVs, then bake in Cycles.
   - https://t.co/3ocKmFbTLm → pack script → hands_v2.glb. Budget ~25–40k tris for both arms incl. sleeves (they're huge on screen), 1–2 skin materials + sleeve + accessories. Textures 2048² on High, 1024² on Low, plus a tiling micro-normal for pores.
   - Generate a full body with pants, boots and the same shirt, and save it as a .blend for a future "player body" stage. Don't put it in the game yet.

3. Look: tanned back of hand and forearm, paler palm and inner side. Scars, calluses, short nails with natural cuticles. Flannel sleeves rolled just below the elbow, with a visible inside-out lining on the roll. Tactical watch on the left wrist, cord bracelet on the right.

4. Check skin weights on stress poses before you export: fist, pinch, spread fingers, 90° supination. Fix weights in a script, not by hand.

5. HARD STOP #1: render review shots in Blender (neutral light and warm daylight): front, back, palms, fist, pinch, cylinder grip, spread fingers, sleeve close-up, two plaid colour variants. Wait for my verbal OK. Iterate. Don't integrate anything into the game until I say yes.

6. glTF only gives you standard material slots, so use them as carriers. Example: MR = (R AO, G roughness, B subsurface thickness), emissive = masks (R hair, G dirt accumulation order), clearcoatNormal = pore tile. Document the mapping and read it back in the runtime.

━━━ PART 2 — SHADERS (MeshStandard/Physical + onBeforeCompile) ━━━

- Skin: wrap lighting, back-lit translucency in thin areas (fingers, webbing, knuckles go red against the sun), pore detail normal, micro-sheen, tan gradient by mask.
- Hair: 4 fur shells in ONE instanced draw, only on hairy triangles, visible on the silhouette against the sun. Disabled on Low.
- Dynamic state:
  · wet = max(world wetness, rain when not under a roof), with two layers of droplets. The sleeve goes darker when wet.
  · dirt builds up from game events (gather, pickup, log, fish_land, climb_out…), fingers and palms first through the mask, and washes off in water or rain.
- Arm lighting mirrors the world: shade under roofs, lamp light, lightning.
- Precompile every arm shader behind the loading screen. https://t.co/nXMh9v1zBi.programs.length must not grow during gameplay.
- Budget: the arm overlay may cost at most ~0.3 ms more GPU than before on High. Measure with a timer query before and after, not by feel.

━━━ PART 3 — THE ARM SYSTEM (data, not code) ━━━

Goal: a new item or action (axe, bow, paddle, steering wheel) should be a data entry plus a clip, never new logic.

1. Rig wrapper: bone map, wrist twist spread over the twist bones (e.g. 0.3 / 0.8 on lowerarm01/02). No candy-wrapper wrists.
2. Two-bone IK (shoulder–elbow–wrist) with pole vectors (elbows down and out) and joint limits.
3. grips.js: for each item, per hand: `at / axis / back / r / diag / gap / slide / fingers / thumb` in item space. One hand owns the item, the other IKs to its socket.
4. Fingers are always a joint table `[[mcp, pip, dip, spread, twist] × 5]` (absolute bend) and blend between poses. Autogrip closes the fingers until they touch the handle.
5. Animation layers, in this order: base pose → clip keyframes → IK → procedural (breath, bob, mouse-turn inertia, sway, recoil, fatigue tremor) → additive reactions. Smooth transitions between states.
6. Clips: JSON keyframes in code, plus importing .glb animations (with empty hand_R/hand_L) for future Blender-made actions. Clip events (strike frame, bow release) go onto the effects bus.
7. In-game pose editor (Shift+H, game keeps running, cursor free): sliders for item offset and rotation, sockets, every finger joint, elbow pole, shoulders, layer speeds. Show changes live. "Copy" puts JSON on the clipboard to paste into grips.js. I need to be able to tune a grip without Blender.
8. Keep the old public API as a facade (hands.anim, reach, lampInHand…) so fishing, boat, lamp, weapons, sleep and the seaplane don't need deep rewrites.
9. Port EVERY existing action: rifle (stance, ADS, fire, reload with mag, dry fire), knife (2 strikes), stone throw, fishing rod (cast, fight, reel, fish in hand), carried log, lamp, reach and pickup, plant gathering, inspect, crate, swimming (breaststroke and crawl), boat tiller, hands down while sleeping, hidden arms in vehicles. Each one must be at least as good as before. Delete the old arm code only after everything is ported (keep a backup).
10. HARD STOP #2: in-game screenshots for my approval (idle, rifle, rod, log, lamp at night, wet after swimming, dirty after firewood, under a roof and in full sun).

━━━ PART 4 — THE FIX PASS (bake this in from day one) ━━━

The first version shipped with these bugs. Every one of them came from old poses written for "stump" arms with no shoulder.

ROOT CAUSE: a real arm has a fixed length (shoulder→wrist ≈ 0.48 m in view space). Old poses put wrists at targets the arm can't reach. The solver then "cheated": it pushed the clavicle out (up to 0.32 m) and clamped the wrist rotation. The hand ended up somewhere else, while finger curls were cached for the ideal hand position, so the fingers squeezed thin air.
  - Rifle, left hand: handguard 0.516 m away with a 0.479 m arm → shoulder pushed out ~0.3 m and the fist still sat 3.8 cm below the handguard.
  - Rifle, right hand: wrist rotation clamped by ~21°, palm not seated on the grip.

FIXES, as SYSTEM features:
1. Shoulder stance as data: per item/pose, `stance: { L:[x,y,z], R:[x,y,z] }` with smooth blending, and the elbow pole moves with the shoulder. Rifle: left shoulder forward and in, right shoulder slightly back (a real shooter's torso rotation). The left elbow stays slightly bent and the clavicle doesn't stretch.
2. Elbow auto-swivel: give each forearm a pronation range (e.g. R −100°…+95°, 0 = thumb up). If the requested pole would over-twist the forearm or bend the wrist past its limit, rotate the elbow around the shoulder–wrist line to the nearest valid angle. The old poses were silently over-twisted (+101° on the rifle, +80° on the knife).
3. Grip by the REAL handle shape. A cylinder radius is wrong: the knife handle was a 2.6 × 4.2 cm oval, not Ø2.5 cm, so the knuckles sank 2–6 mm into it.
   - Handle = elliptical cylinder with end caps (`sec` [along back, across], `span`, `inset`).
   - measureSection(item, socket): take the cross-section automatically by slicing the item mesh around `at` along `axis`.
   - CPU-skin the hand (SkinnedMesh.getVertexPosition, palm and phalanx vertices with weights) and test real skin vertices, not phalanx tips.
   - gripFit, cached and computed at startup: first push the palm out until it leaves the handle. Then close each finger with all joints together until first contact, and after that only the joints past the touching phalanx. If the start pose already intersects, open it up.
   - Fingertip targets: `fingers: {1: {to:[x,y,z]}}` puts the index pad on the trigger.
4. Validator: hands.check(pose) and hands.checkAll(). Run every scenario × both hands + the live rod pose, print a console table, and show it live in the Shift+H editor with a "Check all poses" button. RED if wrist miss > 0.5 cm, rotation clamp > 3°, shoulder push > 0.5 cm, twist over the limit > 3°, or any skin vertex deeper than 1.5 mm inside the handle. Don't call the work done until it's all green (mine ended at 122/122).

DATA FIXES that came from my screenshots:
- Rifle: left hand on the WOODEN handguard, not the metal in front of it. Handguard runs diagonally across the palm, thumb along the left side, forearm coming in from the lower-left corner. Right hand fully on the pistol grip using the grip's real rake (axis (0, 0.95, −0.32), not a guessed 40°), index on the trigger. On reload the hand leads and the mag rides in the hand, and the shoulder dips to follow it. Check sprint, recoil, dry fire, and steering a boat while holding the rifle.
- Log: nobody carries a 44 × 7 cm log with two arms like a crate. One hand, an ordinary hammer grip like a bottle: knuckles up, thumb on top, held about a third from the back end, log pointing forward and up from the thumb side, riding in the fist. The throw is a one-handed wind-up and lunge. The left hand stays free, so the lamp stays in it.
- Swimming: fingers together and slightly cupped (no fan), hands in the bottom third of the frame. Crawl recovery comes in from the side, palm facing out. The sleeve never covers the middle of the screen and the palm never faces the camera.
- Fix every pose the validator flags: stone wind-up and throw, aim, lamp, lamp lowered, climbing, reach.

━━━ RULES ━━━
- Backup before each stage. Measure, don't guess: write every claim down as a number (cm, °, ms, tris, programs).
- No performance regression: grip fit is cached per socket, and the validator only runs in the editor or dev builds.
- Write down what's still unfinished honestly in the report (e.g. "right hand mostly below the frame on the rifle", "pinky sometimes curls without contact").
- DONE = I approved the renders and the screenshots, bends are clean on every grip, fingers wrap handles with zero penetrations, wet and dirt work, every old action works on the new system, a new item is one grips.js entry + one clip, and FPS is unchanged.

title: Jelly Dice: soft-body gummy dice
author: SpacyApps
prompt:
Build "Jelly Dice": a single self-contained HTML file (all JS/CSS inline, no build step) with translucent gummy-candy dice that behave like real soft bodies. Render with raw WebGPU (WGSL shaders, no three.js). If WebGPU is unavailable, show a clean fallback card that explains why.

PHYSICS (the heart of it; it must feel like real jelly, not a rigid die with a wobble shader)
- Each die is a rounded cube simulated as a tetrahedral lattice with XPBD: co-rotational shape matching (per cell and per tet) for elasticity, tet volume constraints so it is nearly incompressible, and hard strain limits so it can never stretch without bound. Inverted elements must always recover.
- Floor contact with static and kinetic friction, plus a raised rim around the plate. Die–die contact against each other's rounded box, with friction.
- Separate rigid motion from deformation: rotational resistance on the floor, internal damping that only damps the wobble, never the rigid motion.
- Sleep when calm: settled dice must never jitter. Wake neighbours when an awake die comes close.
- Heavy landings soak up the rebound, so a dropped die squashes and settles instead of bouncing like rubber.

INTERACTION
- Drag a die to stretch it. The grab is compliant and progressive: a gentle pull stretches the jelly while its base clings to the plate, and a firm pull lifts and moves it. Cap the force, and allow no launches or wild spin on release.

- Soft shadows whose penumbra grows with distance; the shadows are tinted with the candy colour and lighter, because the candy is translucent. Contact occlusion from a top-down height map.
- Smooth normals from the deformation Jacobian (cofactor) on the GPU via a compute pass. Upload only node positions per frame.
- Six candy colours: Emerald, Amethyst, Amber, Sapphire, Raspberry, Lime. Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, MSAA, dither.

title: Interactive mangrove island diorama with synced fireflies
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a single-file interactive WebGL diorama called "Mangrove Lights" (Three.js r160 via import map, OrbitControls, no external models or textures, English UI). A mangrove island sits inside a rounded rectangular block of water, about 10×10 units and 1.7 deep, on a cream plinth, over a transparent canvas with a soft contact shadow.

Island: a procedural heightfield with a dry forest floor at the back, shallow mud flats, creeks, and an open inlet at the front corner. Mangrove fringes stand in about 0.5 of water along both glass walls that face the camera, so the stilt roots show above the water and through the glass. The terrain's side walls are a layered mud cross-section with root fibres. Mud below the high-tide line stays dark, wet and glossy.

Trees (about 140): each has a short trunk; 8–11 arching prop roots built as CatmullRom tube geometry that reach into the mud; hanging aerial roots; and a dense crown of displaced icosphere blobs with per-instance AO and dark glossy greens. Bark is algae- and barnacle-stained below the high-tide line. Add pencil-root pneumatophores on the flats, a fisherman's hut on stilts with a lit window and lamp plus a boardwalk, a canoe that bobs on the waves, wading egrets, an egret flying by day, and schools of silver fish that swim between the roots and flee the cursor.

Water: refraction, Beer–Lambert absorption from real thickness, Fresnel sky, screen-space reflections, sun glints, and almost no shore foam. A 256² GPU wave-equation ripple sim responds to the cursor and clicks. Low mist layers part around the cursor.

Fireflies: about 1600 Kuramoto oscillators around the crowns, coupled to a local spatial-hash mean field plus the global field, with a position-dependent phase offset so the synchronized flash sweeps across the forest as a wave. Use an asymmetric flash curve and additive point sprites drawn after the water, with a manual depth test. Mirrored copies show reflections on the water. Two point lights pulse with the average glow. The cursor randomizes the phase of nearby fireflies and pushes them away; a click scatters a wider area; they drift home and resync.

Lighting: day/night palettes with moonlight, a warm hut lamp, ACES tone mapping and tilt-shift.

UI: brand "bakau°"; headline "A forest that blinks in time."; dock buttons Reset, Night/Day, High/Low tide, Tune and Fullscreen; a settings panel (time, fireflies, pull to sync, mist, water color, tide, waves, ripples, clarity, light azimuth, tilt-shift); a live sync % and clock; a "How it's made" note. The page theme turns dark at night. Include adaptive DPR, a low-detail mode for touch devices, reduced-motion support and a WebGL2 fallback.

title: Interactive jelly watermelon slice with cuttable gummy spiders

SIMULATION
- A thick triangular watermelon slice (rounded rind arc, rounded corners) as an XPBD tetrahedral soft body: co-rotational per-tet shape matching with warm-started quaternions, volume constraints, edge damping, gravity, floor collision with friction.

title: Three.js island scene for a survival game project
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
PROMT 5 

Stage 18 — Island 2 as a real playable zone

Goal: the low, hazy islands on the far left of the starting view stop being cheap backdrop geometry and become a real second island you can reach by motorboat, moor at, and walk around on. It should read as the edge of a large swampy mainland: a low mangrove shoreline, a river mouth facing island 1, and a swamp river leading inland into jungle. This stage is only the foundation. River water, jungle and the wooden boat come in later stages.

1. Location and terrain
- Find how the distant islands are built now and replace them with island 2 in the same spot, about 380 m from the boat pier, so crossing at full throttle takes 1–2 minutes. Keep one of the old far islands as scenery.
- Give island 2 its own heightfield module (separate from island 1's grid and with its own seeded RNG, so island 1's placement never shifts). Build the coastline mask, run an exact distance transform, then add noise: a muddy shore 0.2–0.6 m high, a gentle rise inland to about 4 m, and hills/karst in the west up to about 25 m where the river "comes from".
- Carve the river system into the terrain now: Catmull-Rom splines for a main channel, a branch, a backwater and two creeks, each with width and depth tables along its length (about 20 m between sand spits at the mouth, a wider estuary, about 7 m in the hills). Add floodplains with small ponds, and a shallow muddy delta in front of the mouth. River water level is flat (sea level), so one reflection plane stays correct.
- Bake the data grids later stages will need: height, real distance to water, calm-water gradient, sand, channel proximity (for planting) and coast. Add CPU and GLSL accessors so getHeight, getShoreDist, the water shader, the underwater composite, the ripple sim and rain all understand island 2.

2. Level-of-detail zones
- Two zones, island 1 and island 2. Only the zone the player is in gets the full detail set: layered ground, grass, undergrowth, LOD trees, shadows, planar reflection. The other zone gets a cheap far mesh plus tree impostors, faded by aerial perspective.
- Switch smoothly with hysteresis. Build detailed 80 m terrain chunks nearest-first in time-budgeted slices (no frame over about 30 ms) while the player is still at sea, dither them in over the far mesh, and dispose of everything when you leave. When looking from island 2 back at island 1, hide small objects by screen size.
- Shadow cascades, water sim windows, caustics and reflections must follow the player to island 2. Check float32 precision at x ≈ −900 for shimmering or jitter.

3. Sea between the islands
- Rework the soft world boundary so a corridor to island 2 is open while the rest of the sea still pushes you back. Shape the seabed as deep water rising to a muddy shallow at the mouth.
- Near island 2, fade out waves, swell, surf and foam, and shift the water colour from turquoise to murky green-brown with no visible seam. From island 1, island 2 should read as a hazy silhouette w

  5. 離陸機が滑走 → 機首上げ → 上昇。B滑走路には着陸機が進入、空に飛行機雲

title: Side-by-side boar animation refinement comparison in Blender
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
Use Blender MCP to refine an existing rigged boar animation against a side-view video reference (144 frames at 24 fps, 6 seconds).

First inspect the scene, rig, rest pose, bone hierarchy, mesh weights, and existing animation. Create a verified backup before making changes.

Set up a synchronized side-by-side comparison in Blender: reference on the left, model on the right, with matching frame numbers. Review all 144 frames and match the visible motion as closely as the model’s proportions allow. Explicitly identify any poses inferred because of occlusion or missing depth information.

Animate complete leg chains from the shoulders and hips, with appropriate body movement and weight transfer. Preserve bone lengths. Match footfall timing, hoof placement and orientation, swing height, stride length, and joint bending. Avoid excessive bending of supporting legs, ground penetration, foot sliding, and unnatural hoof tilt.

Validate the front and hind legs separately before smoothing. Previous attempts improved the front legs but left the hind legs with short strides, insufficient swing flexion, and trajectories poorly positioned relative to the pelvis. Smoothing preserved these errors instead of correcting them.

Once the gait is correct, improve continuity without changing footfall timing or ground contact. Check interpolated and subframe poses using the deformed hoof mesh, not only bone positions. Treat numerical smoothness and contact checks as supporting evidence; also inspect the rendered motion.

If working from v4, preserve the approved front legs, torso, head, and tail animation, and modify only the hind-leg chains. Use the reference to determine hind-leg timing; do not assume a fixed offset from the front legs.

Deliver the updated .blend file and synchronized comparison video. Briefly report what changed, what failed and how it was fixed, what was verified, and any remaining mismatch. Do not claim an exact 1:1 match unless the comparison supports it.

title: AI motion graphics about kanji and their structural components
author: haiz_ai
prompt:
Use Claude Code to drive the After Effects project I have open. Write JSX, run it in AE (AfterFX.exe -r on Windows, osascript on Mac), render with aerender, then pull key frames with ffmpeg and check them yourself before moving on.
First check that AE, Python, ffmpeg and a heavy Japanese gothic + mincho font are available. If anything is missing, tell me how to install it (free Google Fonts like Dela Gothic One are fine).
</setup>

<rules>
- 144 BPM (1 beat = 10 frames at 24 fps). Every cut lands on a beat.
- One strong colour pair per screen: 群青 #1F4BFF / 濃紺 #0B1F4D & 山吹 #FFC627 / 生成 #F3F1EC & 墨 #1C1A1A / 臙脂 #7A0E2E & 桃 #FFB3A8 / 深緑 #1F4F2A & 萌黄 #C6E23A / 朱 #FF6A1F
- Motion comes in fast and holds briefly.
- No explanatory text in the video.
</rules>

<idea>
Treat kanji as architecture: things built from parts that can be taken apart and rebuilt.
Let one shot's last shape become the next shot's first shape, so the whole piece feels like one continuous thought.
Give it an arc: an opening, a build-up, a peak, one quiet moment, and an ending that loops back to the start.
</idea>

<ingredients>
Pick a few of these and decide the order yourself. You don't have to use them all, and you can add your own.
- Kanji built from plain bars, changing into other kanji
- Kanji large enough to touch the frame edges, cropped like a poster, but keep about two-thirds of each character on screen so it still reads
- Traditional Japanese patterns (立涌, 青海波, 麻の葉 …)
- Calligraphy: stroke counts, stroke order
- Genkō yōshi (manuscript paper), vertical writing
- Split-flap departure boards, the twelve zodiac signs
</ingredients>

<sound>
Synthesise everything (no audio files) in the Japanese in scale: hyoshigi, taiko, bells, whooshes. Place sounds at the same frame numbers as the cuts. Leave one stretch where the beat drops out.
</sound>

<constraints>
- Patterns from shape-layer properties and repeaters, never drawn by hand. Animate on normal keyframes so I can retime things.
- Put all colours on one controller, and give me controls for the main movements.
- Use matchName, not display names (works in Japanese or English AE). Render with aerender's default template. Wrap scripts in try/catch.
- Shape layers start at comp centre; set anchor/position to [0,0] when plotting in comp coordinates. Text caps at ~1296 px, so scale up beyond that. Check every character exists in the chosen font.

title: Browser 3D spider simulator with IK and teardown
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build an interactive 3D field simulator of a robotic spider that runs in the browser: a single HTML file on three.js 0.170 (loaded via an importmap from https://t.co/lj8MfmK18g). Use no external models; generate all geometry in code.

CHARACTER
Saltus SX-8: an eight-legged survey robot styled after a jumping spider, made by the fictional company Saltus Field Robotics.
- Cephalothorax built from thick ellipsoid shell patches with bevels, rivets and seams: 6 hinged carapace plates plus a top cap with a lidar puck.
- Two large principal eyes: 3-stage telescoping barrels, a 9-blade iris, a glowing sensor and lime rings; plus 6 small auxiliary eyes.
- Chelicerae with titanium fangs, a needle core sampler, and pedipalps that keep moving.
- Abdomen made of plates with "SX-8" markings and lime chevrons; the rear petals open to reveal the silk spool, the battery stack and a 3-nozzle spinneret.
- 8 legs: coxa, femur, knee, tibia, metatarsus, tarsus with claws; joint drives and 2 hydraulic rams per leg that actually track their joints.
- Every part is a separate movable piece for an exploded (teardown) view.

STYLE
Graphite + titanium + acid lime (#C6F23C) on a cool light-grey studio background. PBR materials (clearcoat on the shell), RoomEnvironment, soft shadows, GTAO (exclude the background and the floor from the AO pass), NeutralToneMapping, a soft contact shadow under the spider. On the floor: thin measurement rings and a dot grid.

ANIMATION
- Leg IK (3 links, knees up), alternating-tetrapod gait with no foot sliding.
- Poses: hanging on the silk line, leap, raised front legs, exploded.
- A deterministic 30 s timeline (stateAt(t)) that drives pose, assemblies, camera and telemetry:
  rappel down → touchdown → walk → crouch and leap → open optics → carapace → leg L2 (links separate horizontally) → abdomen → fangs → full teardown on a turntable → reassembly → ascend on the silk line.
- A dedicated camera angle for each scene with smooth blends; legs must not block the assembly being inspected.

HUD (HTML/CSS/SVG over the canvas)
Fonts: Space Grotesk + IBM Plex Mono.
- Top bar: logo, title, hydraulic load meter, sim ID, runtime, status, operator.
- Left: Hydraulics (pressure with a 3 s graph, foot force), Power, per-leg load for all 8 legs.
- Right: attitude indicator, assembly buttons (HERO / OPTICS / CARAPACE / LEG L2 / SPINNERET / FANGS), display toggles (LABELS / EXPLODED / SILK / TURNTABLE), subsystem status chips.
- Bottom: operation log with a scrubbable timeline and play/pause; a lime operating-mode badge.
- Callouts anchored to 3D points, set in columns at the viewport edges on a light backing, never overlapping.
- Every number is driven by the simulation.

CONTROLS
Any button switches to manual mode with smooth transitions. OrbitControls for a free camera; double-click returns to the auto camera. Keys: Space, 1–6, E / L / S / T / C, arrow keys.

TECHNICAL
Adaptive quality on weak devices, mobile layout, prefers-reduced-motion, safe-area

title: Interactive pixel-art cyberpunk window wallpaper you can smash
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file (no libraries, no external assets, works offline) called "Neon Window": an interactive pixel-art live wallpaper where the viewer can smash a window.

TECH
- Plain JavaScript. Canvas 2D for all pixel art, raw WebGL (one custom GLSL fragment shader) for the glass, Web Audio API for all sound (fully synthesized, no audio files).
- Draw the world at a low resolution of 480×270 and scale it up to cover the viewport, keeping crisp square pixels. On narrow or portrait screens, keep the window in view. Cap devicePixelRatio at 2. Target 60 fps.

SCENE — OUTSIDE (rainy cyberpunk Tokyo at night, seen through the window)
- Smoggy purple-magenta sky with a hazy pink moon; distant skyscraper silhouettes with tiny lit windows and blinking red beacons.
- A large holographic koi swimming slowly across the sky, projected by a beam from a tower (cyan/pink, scanlines, occasional glitch).
- An animated billboard on a tower cycling through three screens with glitch transitions; a monorail train passing every ~20 s; a small flying car with a light trail now and then.
- A street of five buildings: a ramen shop (indigo noren curtains, red paper lanterns, diners in silhouette), a convenience store (bright interior), an izakaya (lattice doors, a big red lantern with 酒, string lights on the roof), a karaoke bar (pink and purple windows), and a bar (vending machines, a graffiti-covered shutter, a fire escape). Add AC units, cables and rooftop water tanks.
- Neon signs drawn with a hand-made bitmap pixel font: vertical katakana ラーメン, ホテル, カラオケ and horizontal BAR, OPEN, 24H, all with glow. Signs flicker occasionally; one is "broken" and flickers often.
- A wet road with mirrored, rippling reflections; pedestrians with colorful umbrellas walking both ways; cars with headlight beams and light streaks on the asphalt; steam from a manhole and roof vents; slanted rain streaks with small splashes.

SCENE — ROOM (cozy, warm, Japanese)
- A dark wooden window frame and a plank wall, warmly lit by a hanging red paper lantern (chochin) that flickers softly.
- A hanging scroll with an ink-wash mountain painting, a small framed Mt. Fuji print, and a shelf with a daruma, a succulent and books.
- A desk with: a bonsai whose foliage overlaps the bottom of the window, an open book, a digital clock showing the real local time, a steaming cup of instant noodles, and a sleeping black cat. Clicking the cat makes it open its eyes and play a synthesized "meow".
- Pink, violet and cyan neon light spilling onto the desk from outside.

GLASS (WebGL shader)
- Seen through the glass, the street is slightly hazy and soft, with condensation fog near the bottom and a blurred warm reflection of the lantern.
- Raindrops on the glass: many small drops plus larger ones that grow, slide down in jerky bursts, leave trails and absorb small drops. Render them as a normal map that refracts the scene (an inverted lens image) with a darker rim and a specular highlight.

title: 15-second anime-style game PV of ruined city transforming into
author: mi7_crypto
prompt:
## 制作仕様
- 尺：15秒
- アスペクト比：16:9
- 動画モード：multimodal
- 最終出力：世界観を一貫させた、終末世界を描く1本のゲームPV
## 全体方針
`灰都開花` の世界が、起動に失敗したシステムの内部から再構築されていく。人物や既存IPのキャラクターは登場させず、崩壊した未来都市そのものを主人公として描く。@ Image1 を唯一の画風基準とし、純黒、純白、少量のニュートラルグレー、高彩度の侵食マゼンタ、ごく少量の再起動シアンという配色を維持する。マゼンタは環境表現、水平走査光、データ亀裂、FUIの強調、場面転換に使用する。シアンは再起動信号のみに限定し、1フレーム内の占有率を5％未満、映像全体の平均を3％未満に抑える。硬質なコミック調の線、網点、黒ベタ、平面的な色面から始まり、走査光とスライス再構成を通じて、奥行きと重量感を備えたAAAゲームCGへ連続的に変化させる。未来都市、花の都市、サイバー森林は別世界として切り替えず、同じ建築物と地形が変形していく連続空間として見せる。エンディングに表示する正確な文字は `灰都開花` と `滅びのあとで、世界は咲く。`。
## 参考素材との対応
- @ Image1：唯一のスタイル／シーン基準。崩壊した未来都市、データ亀裂、幾何学的な花とサイバー森林、硬質な線、無彩色と侵食マゼンタ、限定的なシアン、情報量を抑えた大きな色面、コミック表現から立体的なレイヤー表現へ移行する視覚言語を提供する。正確な開始フレームや終了フレームとして固定せず、映像全体のビジュアルを統一するために使用する。
- 9分割プレビューは動画の参照素材として渡さない。承認済み絵コンテに沿った構図、動作の段階、ショットサイズ、つながりのみを、以下のタイムラインへ反映する。
## サウンド
モデルが生成する同期サウンドを使用する。低い電源ハム音から始まり、起動エラー、デジタルな途切れ、紙とガラスが裂ける音、鋭い走査音、断片が吸着する音、都市の低域が加速する音、花を思わせる倍音、サイバー樹木の共鳴へと連続的に発展させる。13.2秒で全帯域を一瞬吸い込み、タイトルの再構成と同時に深い衝撃音を鳴らす。最後は短いデジタル残響と安定した電源音だけを残す。無関係な声、歌、ナレーションは入れない。
## 絵コンテ順序の制約
冒頭は、ほぼ暗闇に近い中央のクローズアップから始める。FUIの崩壊は平面的に見せ、斜めに走る亀裂を次のコミックパネルの枠へつなげる。コミック世界は、斜めに重なった3層のミディアムショットから、水平断片が浮遊するワイドショットへ展開する。細いシアンの信号を画面奥の固定軸とし、断片をその軸へ再結合させながらCG空間へ移行する。未来都市では、一点透視の地表を高速で前進する。花の都市では一瞬だけカメラを高く上げ、広角で全景を見せる。白い霧をサイバー森林の奥行きへつなげ、森林ではローアングルで枝の間を抜けながら中央の信号へ収束する。最後は暗く左右対称のタイトル画面で締める。
## メインタイムライン
### 論理ショット1｜0.00–2.20秒｜起動失敗
完全な黒から開始する。画面中央で細い白い起動カーソルが点滅し、カメラが画面奥へごく浅く前進する。小さな `BOOT SEQUENCE` が現れ、白い起動ログが縦方向に増殖する。0.7秒から侵食マゼンタの水平走査線が左から右へ走り、ログの一部を欠損させながら `BOOT FAILED` の断片へ崩していく。FUIレイヤーは異なるZ深度で前後にずれ、データ亀裂のマスクが文字と黒い背景を同時に割る。低い電源ハム、リレー音、途切れるエラー音、走査音を重ねる。ショットの終わりに、亀裂の白い隙間から斜めのコミックパネルを露出させる。
### 論理ショット2｜2.20–6.80秒｜コミック世界の崩壊とCG再構成
カメラは亀裂を通り抜け、崩壊した未来都市、瓦礫の大通り、浮遊建築を描いた写実寄りのコミックパネル3層へ進入する。パネルは斜めに配置し、前景の網点、黒ベタ、枠の断片をそれぞれ異なる速度で動かして、3Dレイヤーを前後に動かすような視差を作る。4.4秒からマゼンタの走査光が全レイヤーを貫き、建築物、空、瓦礫を細い水平スライスへ分解する。断片はZ軸方向の手前と奥へ引き離され、走査光が通過した部分から、線画が重量感と空気遠近法を備えたAAAゲームCGへ変化していく。黒いデータ亀裂が遮蔽ワイプのように画面を噛み切り、断片は細いシアンの固定軸へ吸着して再結合する。紙が擦れる音、ガラスが割れる音、鋭いスキャン音、金属的な吸着音、重い低音の衝撃を重ねる。最後は、完全に再構成された都市空間へ抜ける。
### 論理ショット3｜6.80–9.30秒｜未来都市の実体化
地表すれすれの一点透視で、巨大な未来都市を高速前進する。濡れた路面、前景の瓦礫、中景の建築物、遠方の環状メガストラクチャー、薄いFUIレイヤーがそれぞれ異なる速度で後方へ流れ、強い奥行きを生み出す。配色は無彩色と侵食マゼンタのまま維持し、多色ネオンにはしない。建築物の輪郭が一瞬だけコミック調の線へ戻り、すぐにCGへ復帰する。低域を加速させ、都市の残響と遠くで構造物が崩壊する音を広げる。路面のデータ亀裂からマゼンタの幾何学的な花が芽吹き、カメラの進行方向へ広がっていく。
### 論理ショット4｜9.30–13.20秒｜花の都市からサイバー森林へ
前進を止めることなく、建物と街路を水平断片へ分解し、それらを花弁状の橋、結晶の花塔、巨大な花の都市へ再構成する。カメラを短く上昇させ、広角で全景を見せる。遠方にある小さなシアンの信号だけで、正常系への復帰を示す。花弁の影が画面を覆い、その輪郭が黒い樹幹と枝へ変形する。白い霧、マゼンタの回路状の葉、前景の枝、中景のFUI、遠景の信号をそれぞれ独立した3Dレイヤーとして前後に動かし、枝の間を高速ですり抜ける。硬質なデータ音の中に短い倍音が広がり、電子的な木々の共鳴と風切り音へ変化する。13.2秒

title: Procedural winter steam locomotive scene with smoke, snow, and
author: SamirJunaid
prompt:
Create a complete, single-file HTML application using Three.js and custom GLSL shaders that renders a dynamic, procedural 3D winter scene of a vintage black steam locomotive speeding through a snow-covered pine forest at golden hour. Do not use any external 3D models or texture files; generate all geometry, materials, and particle systems entirely via code.
1. The Locomotive Geometry & Materials:
Construct a detailed classic steam locomotive positioned on a diagonal railway track, viewed from a dynamic low-angle three-quarter front perspective. Include a cylindrical boiler with metallic bands, a front smokestack, steam domes, a cab at the back, a detailed front snowplow (cowcatcher) with red trim, and a bright glowing warm-white headlight on the nose with a volumetric light cone effect. Build a complex wheel assembly featuring large red spoked driving wheels, smaller leading/trailing wheels, and animated metallic connecting rods and pistons that mechanically rotate and reciprocate in sync with the train's forward speed. Apply PBR materials (MeshStandardMaterial / MeshPhysicalMaterial) using dark weathered matte black steel with subtle roughness variations, metallic sheen, and frost accumulation along the edges.
2. Animations & Particle Systems (Smoke, Steam & Snow):
Create a continuous movement illusion where the train stays centered while the railway tracks (wooden sleepers and steel rails), snow terrain, and pine trees scroll seamlessly backward. Implement three distinct GPU-accelerated particle systems:
Heavy Exhaust Smoke: Dense, billowing white and grey volumetric smoke puffs erupting from the top smokestack, drifting backward and expanding with turbulence.
Piston Steam: Fast, pressurized bursts of white mist shooting sideways from the lower wheel cylinders and undercarriage.
Plowed Snow: Dynamic snow powder and ice chunks spraying outward and upward from the front snowplow as it cuts through deep snowdrifts on the tracks.
3. Environment & Lighting:
Generate an infinite procedural winter landscape with rolling snowbanks along the tracks and dense clusters of snow-laden pine trees in the background. Set up dramatic cinematic lighting: a warm, low-hanging golden-hour sun positioned in the background behind the trees, casting long shadows, god rays (volumetric crepuscular rays), and warm rim lighting across the dark metallic train and billowing smoke, contrasted against cool blue ambient snow shadows.

title: 16-bit style pixel-art wizard spell short film with synced chip
author: gkxspace
prompt:
你是一位像素动画师兼游戏手感（game feel）设计师，也会写芯片音乐。你用代码做出的东西，要像 16-bit 时代一流工作室手绘的角色动画，而不是缩小的矢量图。   </role> <inputs>   以下是默认值，直接开工，不用问我：   - 片名：《第 99 次施法》   - 画幅：1920×1080，60fps，时长正好 16 小节（140 BPM，约 27.43 秒），结尾无缝衔接开头   - 逻辑分辨率：192×108，整数 10 倍放大（竖屏版改为 108×192 → 1080×1920）   - 声音：代码合成的芯片音乐和音效   </inputs> <story>   一个老巫师在夜里的山崖上练一个总是失败的法术。三次尝试，一次比一次认真，最后一次成功点亮了山下整座沉睡的村庄。   140 BPM，一拍约 0.429 秒，一小节约 1.714 秒。   - 第 1–2 小节 待机：巫师轻晃，胡子摆动，星星闪烁。镜头极慢地推近。   - 第 3–5 小节 第一次：蓄力 → 宝石亮了一下 → "噗"地冒出一缕灰烟，帽子被吹歪。音乐停半拍，留出喜剧停顿。   - 第 6–8 小节 第二次：更用力 → 飞弹射出 → 在空中掉头飞回来 → 打掉自己的帽子。停 1 拍，巫师眨两次眼。   - 第 9–10 小节 准备第三次：捡起帽子戴正，深呼吸（身体 1 像素起伏两次），音乐收得只剩三角波低音。   - 第 11–13 小节 第三次：长蓄力，火花螺旋聚拢，越转越快；第 13 小节最后一拍前全场静音 0.3 秒。   - 第 14 小节正拍 施法：hit-stop 冻结 5 帧，全屏白闪 1 帧，飞弹划过夜空落向山下。   - 第 15–16 小节 村庄的窗户从近到远依次亮起（错相，每扇窗间隔 2–4 帧），音乐全奏。巫师满意地捋胡子，帽子又滑下来挡住眼睛，然后回到待机姿势。   - 循环：render(16 小节的时长) 与 render(0) 逐像素一致，成片只包含 [0, 总时长) 内的帧。   </story> <direction>   像素纪律   - 所有内容画在 192×108 的离屏画布上，再按整数倍放大；imageSmoothingEnabled = false，CSS image-rendering: pixelated。   - 所有坐标对齐整数格。禁止亚像素、抗锯齿、shadowBlur、线性渐变；需要过渡时用 4×4 Bayer 抖动。   - 固定调色板不超过 24 色，先输出色板：夜空深蓝紫 4 阶、长袍暖色 4 阶、肤色 3 阶、魔法色 3–4 个，石头和村庄若干。画面上每个像素都必须来自色板。   - 角色约 22×30 个逻辑像素，用选择性描边（sel-out，受光一侧的描边用较浅的颜色）。光照靠切换色板色阶表现，不叠半透明。
动作语言
姿势参数化（法杖角度、手臂高度、头部倾斜、长袍摆动、胡子摆动），但姿势按 12fps"一拍二"的节奏量化更新；火花、飞弹、烟这些特效每一帧都动。

每个动作都走完：预备 → 动作 → 冲击 → 余震 → 回稳。法杖快速挥动时插 1–2 帧拖影帧（smear frame），不用运动模糊。
冲击感：命中瞬间 hit-stop 冻结 3–5 帧；屏幕按整数像素震动，幅度 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 衰减；宝石白闪 1 帧。
挤压拉伸控制在 1–2 像素以内：在像素动画里，1 像素已经是很大的变化。
错相：身体先动，胡子和帽尖晚 2–3 帧跟上，长袍下摆再晚 2 帧。
喜剧靠停顿：失败后的静止和眨眼要给够时间，不要用特效把停顿填满。
场景与光
三层视差：星空（几乎不动）、远山、近处的石崖和巫师。镜头漂移时各层速度不同，位移都取整。

宝石是动态光源：蓄力时，巫师面向宝石的一侧加 1 像素轮廓光，越亮色阶越高。成功那一刻，整个画面的色板短暂整体提亮一阶，再回落。

禁止

<sound>   - 只用四个通道，模仿 8-bit 主机：方波 1 弹旋律；方波 2 弹和声或琶音（占空比在 12.5%、25%、50% 之间切换）；三角波弹低音；噪声通道打鼓。方波用带限合成（PolyBLEP 或加法合成），避免刺耳的混叠。   - 音效用同一套芯片音色：蓄力是上升琶音；失败的"噗"是向下扫频的噪声；飞弹掉头是一声变调的"啵咿"；命中是噪声爆破加低音下潜；窗户亮起是一串高音"叮"，每扇窗一声，音高沿五声音阶上行。   - 喜剧停顿时，音乐真的停下来；hit-stop 的 5 帧里，只留一条拉长的噪声尾巴。   - BPM 已知，节拍网格直接用公式算。所有关键动作落在拍上，预备动作可以提前 2–3 帧。   </sound> <engineering>   确定性渲染（违反任何一条都算失败）   - 页面暴露 window.render(t)，t 单位为秒，画面只由 t 计算。不用 requestAnimationFrame、setTimeout、https://t.co/Lwkwc6MyZu()、https://t.co/FDvnvYDWAb()、CSS transition/animation 驱动画面。   - 随机数一律用带固定种子的 PRNG（如 mulberry32）；帧与帧之间不保存状态。   - 粒子（火花、烟、飞弹拖尾）用种子预先生成每个粒子的出生时间、初速度和寿命，位置由 t 解析计算后取整。   - 角色和场景全部程序化生成，不用任何图片；渲染时不联网。
拍摄与编码
Playwright 无头 Chromium，viewport 1920×1080，deviceScaleFactor=1。
逐帧调用 render(t) → 截图 → 通过管道直接喂给 ffmpeg，不在磁盘上堆几千张 PNG。
视频 H.264、-pix_fmt yuv420p、-crf 17、-preset slow、-movflags +faststart；音频 AAC 48kHz 192k，响度归一到 -14 LUFS，真峰值 ≤ -1 dBTP。 </engineering>
<qc>   - 像素网格检查：随机抽 10 帧，先最近邻缩小 10 倍再放大 10 倍，必须与原帧逐像素相同（证明没有亚像素和抗锯齿）。   - 色板检查：随机抽 10 帧统计用到的颜色，必须全部属于色板。   - 循环检查：render(总时长) 与 render(0) 逐像素一致；音频首尾做 10ms 交叉淡化，循环播放时不爆音。   - 抽帧拼图：每 0.5 秒一张。按这几项各打 1–10 分：剪影可读性、喜剧节奏（停顿够不够）、打击感、动作完整度（有没有直接滑过去的动作）、声画同步、像素纯度。把最严重的 3 个问题修掉再重渲，直到每项 ≥ 8。   </qc> <start>   自主模式，中途不要停下来问我。先输出色板图和 3 张关键帧

title: Interactive three.js espresso machine teardown with detachable parts

title: Animated short in the spirit of Hedgehog in the Fog
author: superalesha
prompt:
make an animated short that felt like Hedgehog in the Fog. I didn’t want to copy Yuri Norstein’s film, so we went with a new story.

It runs for 6.5 minutes. All 9363 frames are drawn by JavaScript code written by Opus. No video or image generation models, just canvas.

It follows a little mouse in a red scarf. Her grandfather, an old mole, is out fishing when fog rolls over the lake. She goes looking for him with a walnut-shell lantern and a sleeping firefly inside. They have a secret knock to help them find each other: short, short, long. It means "I’m here".

Norstein used paper cutouts on layers of glass, filmed frame by frame. I wanted some of that paper texture to come through in code. So the scenes use different styles: torn-paper collage, chalk on black paper, tissue paper underwater. There’s even sand on a light table and a pop-up book.

Opus wrote the music too. It found Steinway piano samples in my Logic library and used Python to compose the score around the rhythm of that knock.

title: Real-time pixel-art badminton diorama with physics, UI, and park
author: N1njaCodex
prompt: Build a real-time 3D pixel-art diorama "Sunday Net": one-on-one grass volleyball in a city park on a floating island (three.js 0.160, orthographic isometric camera with quarter-turns, low-res render target, depth outlines, 64-colour OKLab palette, hard shadow map, day/dusk/night). Park: 8×5 m grass court taped in white, worn sand patches at the serving spots, net top 2.30 m on two blue steel poles with guy ropes, white tapes and red-white antennae over the sidelines; a duck pond with stone bank, reeds, bulrushes, lily pads and a willow, its water rendered as a screen-space planar reflection (mirrored scene pass) with glints and expanding ripple rings; gravel paths with cast-iron lamp posts and benches, a yellow kvass barrel cart with parasol and seller, a picnic on a checked cloth, a striped players' blanket with bag and bottles, lindens, a bicycle, a round flower bed, a low clipped hedge round the edge. Ball physics: 21 cm, 270 g, quadratic drag, Magnus force for topspin jump serves, knuckling wobble for float serves, grass bounce and roll, net/tape collisions (rolls over or drops back), crossing outside the antennae is out, floats and drifts on the pond. Shot solver: for each launch angle bisect the speed to reach a target at a given height (ground across the net, or set height on one's own side), choose the angle by touch (pass/set apex, fastest spike that clears the tape, softest cut), iterate the aim against the wind as the player reads it, add skill/hurry noise and shanks. Rules: one player per side may touch the ball three times running — pass to self, set to self near the net, approach-jump-attack (spike, cut shot, deep shot) or a free ball over; rally scoring to 15 (or 21), win by two, winner of the rally serves, winner of the set stays on, four friends rotate from the blanket. AI predicts the flight and picks a contact family (forearm pass, side digs, overhead set, spike with jump height, dive), reads the attacker's position on defence, leaves balls going out (sometimes wrongly). Box-rig players with IK: platform pass, hands over the forehead, arm-swing jump spike, dive and push-up, toss and float/jump serve. Retrieval: pick up off the grass, wade into the pond knee-deep (ducks paddle away), spare ball from the bag. Mallard ducks that dabble and come to crumbs from a grandmother on the bench; a man walking a dog along the paths; a waiting player buys a mug of kvass. Fireflies by the pond, moths at the lamps, butterflies over the flowers; wind calm/breeze/gusty. UI: flip scoreboard (set, rally, ball speed), three-touch indicator, attack-call buttons (spike/cut/deep/jump serve), set-length switch, players ladder, feed of remarks, wind readout, view controls; clicks aim the next attack or throw bread to the ducks.

Watermelon wedge (half-disc slab): red flesh with dark teardrop seeds, a pale rind band, a green striped skin. 2. title: 8-bar 3D motion design film of a website
author: kloss_xyz
prompt:
Make an 8-bar 3D motion design film of my website: 1920x1080, 30 fps, Blender Cycles on GPU, headless, built entirely from code, in this folder.

INPUTS
SITE: [path to your site's repo, or its live URL]
HERO: [a .glb, 3 to 4 views of your character, or "the site's logo mark"]
AUDIO: [a WAV you own or licensed, with a clear drop, or "synth"]
LINE: [the one sentence the film proves]

STORY
Bar 1, hook: the site fills the frame, flat, and something alive inside it moves within 2 seconds. No title card.
Bar 2, premise: the hero breaks out of the page and the page splits into its sections as floating slabs.
Bar 3, drop: the first landing hits the music's drop.
Bars 3 to 5, proof: each landing switches one real section on. A landing that changes nothing gets cut.
Bar 6, breadth: every section lit in one frame.
Bar 7, thesis: the slabs fly back into one page.
Bar 8, close: a clean poster frame. Make the last frame match the first so it loops.

TRUTH
- Real pixels only. Capture each section of the running site with headless Chrome. Replace every clock the page uses (the performance timer, requestAnimationFrame, setTimeout and CSS animations) with a stepper so every frame is reproducible. Measure every target from the DOM.
- Never draw a screen, logo, number or claim that is not on the site. Cut empty sections.
- The look comes from the site: color, type, radius and easing tokens (from the code, or computed styles for a live URL), written into a style guide with the source of each. Anything not on the site is marked as a film choice.
- Banned: dark chrome, iridescent porcelain, a centered title over a gradient, fade-in on everything, particles that mean nothing.

TIMING
- One Python timeline file is the only clock: every event in beats at the track's tempo, with a check that fails on gaps. Capture, Blender and sound all read its JSON.

title: Tutorial-style animated explainer about making animations with Opus
author: king1818888
prompt:
请帮我上网研究大家怎么用 Claude Opus 5.5 制作动画，整理成一套清楚的操作流程，再用这套流程亲手做一部「如何用 Opus 5.5 做动画」的教学动画。

第一阶段：资料收集

1. 搜寻范围：YouTube 教学影片（可读字幕或说明栏）、X/Twitter、Reddit（r/ClaudeAI 等）、个人部落格、Medium、GitHub 范例专案，以及 Anthropic 官方文件。
2. 关键字用中英文都搜，例如：「Claude Opus 5.5 animation」「Claude 做动画」「Claude Remotion」「Claude Manim」「Claude SVG animation」「Claude HTML animation prompt」「Claude artifact animation」。
3. 以最近三月内的资料为主，至少参考 【10】 个以上不同来源。
4. 每个来源记下：作者、网址、用的工具或技术、他们的提示词写法、遇到的问题和解法。

第二阶段：整理分析

1. 先分类大家的做法。我不确定是用动画工具还是写程式码，请帮我厘清，可能包括：
 程式码类：HTML/CSS/JS、SVG、Canvas、GSAP、Three.js、Remotion（React 影片）、Manim（Python 数学动画）、Motion Canvas 等
 工具搭配类：Claude 写脚本或分镜，再交给其他动画或影片工具
2. 比较各做法的难易度、适合对象、成品效果和优缺点，做成表格。
3. 归纳出一套「新手也能照做」的标准流程，例如：构想 → 写脚本/分镜 → 下提示词 → 生成程式码 → 预览修改 → 汇出影片。每一步都附上实际可用的提示词范例。

第三阶段：制作教学动画

1. 内容：用动画呈现第二阶段整理出的流程，让没有经验的人看完就知道怎么开始。
2. 长度：约 【2-4】 分钟，分成 【5–7】 个段落（开场 → 各步骤 → 小技巧 → 结尾总结）。
3. 风格由你决定，以清楚易懂为最高原则。可以是扁平插画、资讯图表或简约动态文字，配色统一、画面不要太杂。
4. 语言：画面文字用简体中文，专有名词保留英文。
5. 制作方式：请采用你研究后认为最适合的方法，最好就是教学里介绍的方法，让这部动画本身也是示范。
6. 动画要能自动播放，也要有暂停、上一段、下一段的控制。

第四阶段：交付内容

1. 一份研究报告，包含来源列表（附连结）、做法比较表和标准流程。
2. 分镜脚本：每一段的画面描述、文字、秒数。
3. 成品动画：可直接播放的网页版。如果做得到，也请附上 MP4 或汇出影片的方法。
4. 完整原始码和使用说明，让我之后能自己修改。

注意事项

如果某些资讯查不到或不确定，请直接说明，不要编造。
开始制作动画前，先把第二阶段的流程和分镜给我确认。

title: Meteor Time-Freeze Cinematic Sequence Prompt Orchestrated by Opus 5.5
author: MadMax_Series
prompt:
[Identity Lock | Woman]

[Identity Lock | Man]

[First Frame]
24mm low-angle wide shot looking down street; quiet night street, shop lights, streetlamps, dark sky; top-right sky glows bright orange-white.

[Timeline / SHOT 1]
0.0–4.0s | 24mm low wide upward tilt: 0.0–1.5s sky lights up brighter than day, cast shadows swing rapidly; 1.5–3.0s pedestrians gaze up as massive burning meteor streaks across top-right sky towards horizon; 3.0–4.0s meteor glare reflects on cafe door glass, creating first match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 3]

[Timeline / SHOT 4]
15.0–19.0s | Match cut from flying glass, 50mm eye-level profile, both in street center: 15.0–17.0s reaching out, he drops both coffees, liquid spills, glass whirls, dust wall 20m away, wind pulls hair; 17.0s time abruptly freezes completely; 17.0–19.0s absolute standstill except she slowly blinks, creating fourth match cut.

[Timeline / SHOT 5]

[Timeline / SHOT 6]

[Physics]

title: Procedural jelly kitten knight in a grassy field
author: vib3coded
prompt:
Build "Knight Kitten": a single self-contained HTML file, native WebGPU, fully procedural (no models, no textures, no libraries).

The scene: a tiny jelly kitten knight sitting in a grassy field.
- The kitten wears a little suit of armour and a bow.
- It holds a sword far too big for it, and a cape is sewn to its back.
- The kitten, the armour, the bow and the sword are all one signed distance field filled with a single lattice, so no part can come loose. Material regions are painted in rest space: jelly, armour, blade, grip, guard and pommel, bow.
- Candy-bright glossy eyes; tabby stripes and a cream muzzle, chest and toes inside the jelly.

Physics (XPBD):
- The body is a soft lattice: co-rotational shape matching on hexahedral cells plus tetrahedral volume constraints, a fixed 60 Hz step with substeps, edge damping and sleeping.
- The armour is firmer than the jelly.
- The sword is steel that bends: overlapping shape-matching clusters along it, with the hilt held in the kitten's grip in the torso's best-fit frame.
- The seat keeps its footing on the grass and the toy rights itself after a wobble.
- A drag stretches the kitten. "Lift" mode picks the whole kitten up so it dangles and jiggles, then lands and finds its footing again.
- The cape is an XPBD cloth (stretch, shear and bend constraints from a flat pattern) sewn to points embedded in the lattice.
  - Spheres riding the body keep the cape off it, and it rests on the grass.
  - Per-triangle aerodynamic wind acts on it.
  - The cape can be grabbed; a hard pull tugs the kitten along.

Rendering:
- The jelly is a refractive volume: front depth plus the nearest back face, absorption by thickness, a glowing deep colour, gloss and the environment refracted through it.
- The kitten is skinned on the GPU from the lattice nodes and their deformation gradients.
- The sun shadow map also stores the coloured light the jelly lets through; a top-down height map gives contact shading under the kitten.
- An instanced grass field around it sways in the same wind formula as the physics.

Weather presets, each with its own sun, sky and wind:
- Mist (soft hazy light);
- Wind (gusts that lean on the toy and blow the cape);
- Rain (falling streaks and splashes on the ground);
- Storm (dark sky, heavy rain, lightning flashes).

Make all four look unmistakably different.

Interaction:
- Drag the kitten to stretch it; drag the background to orbit; zoom.
- Grab the cape.
- A Lift toggle to carry the kitten.

UI:
- A minimal glassy UI: weather buttons (keys 1–4), jelly palettes Honey, Rose and Icy blue, Softness and Wind sliders, Pause (Space) and Reset (R).
- Responsive on phones; adaptive quality.
- NaN-safe WGSL: clamp every pow and smoothstep input and clamp the HDR result, so no black specks appear on real GPUs.

title: 60-second anime-style short film from a weekend photo diary
author: henloitsjoyce
prompt:
Make me a ~60-second, 16:9, 1080p short film from my attached photos and videos, using only the Hedra MCP. Cost doesn't matter.

STORY: Order the media by capture time and tell it as one day from morning to night, seen by the person holding the camera. Invent small in-between moments and about 7 short spoken lines, so it plays like a movie, not a slideshow.

LOOK: For each story beat, make one 16:9 keyframe with GPT Image 2 (high). Write each prompt as a single widescreen frame from a 1990s-2000s Studio Ghibli feature film, scanned from a 35mm print: hand-painted watercolor-and-gouache backgrounds, flat cel paint with one shadow tone and thin outlines, muted slightly faded colors, soft grain. Use wide shots, with the person small in a big painted landscape. Ban: glossy, bloom, sparkles, lens flare, over-saturation, close-up portraits, text. Make the first finished keyframe the style anchor, and pass it as the second reference on every other keyframe. Show me all the keyframes as a contact sheet before animating.

MOTION: Animate with Seedance 2.5 at 1080p. Clip N starts on keyframe N and ends on keyframe N+1, so the whole film is one continuous camera journey with no cuts, fades or wipes. In video prompts, describe the style instead of naming the studio (naming it trips moderation). Sound: natural ambience only (footsteps, wind, rustling, crowds). No music, and no instruments or music-like sounds that would fight the score.

SCORE: One continuous 60-second live-recorded chamber waltz from ElevenLabs Music: upright piano, solo violin, accordion, mandolin, harp, small strings, flute, cello. Give it a timed arc (piano intro, playful middle, sweeping climax, tender close) ending on a soft held chord. Acoustic only, no MIDI feel, no vocals. It must never cut between scenes. Compose it in the style of Chopin.

VOICE: Clone my voice from the attached recording. Voice the lines with ElevenLabs v3 at stability 0.5 and speed about 1.05, using light, playful tags such as [happy, lighthearted], [delighted], [giggles], [laughs] and [whispers], never [wistful] or [sighs]. Make 2-3 takes per line and put them on a listening page so I can pick.

FINISH: Assemble with ffmpeg: 0.25 s crossfades; the score continuous under everything and ducked under the voice; scene sounds normalized per clip and sitting about 5 dB under the music; a gentle fade out. Burn in soft white film-style captions (Lato, a subtle halo, short fades) timed to the speech. Save a captioned and a clean version to my Movies folder. Check a contact sheet of stills at every caption before you call it done.

title: 10-second sailboat glide under Golden Gate Bridge at golden hour
author: LukeTsiaras
prompt:
Write code that renders a 10-second MP4 of a sailboat gliding under the Golden Gate Bridge at golden hour. Every frame must be generated programmatically.

Make it feel real: obsess over light, water, sail, wake, haze, and sky until every detail holds up to close inspection. Shoot it as one continuous, smoothly orbiting camera move with no cuts. Let the light, pacing, and sound carry a feeling without explaining it.

Use only publicly available open-source tools: no connectors, skills, or private resources. No speech; music and sound design are encouraged.

Review your work before delivering, then report how long it took and estimate the cost from tokens used, showing your math. Don't let the report change how you work.

title: Glitch title animation with scan lines and RGB split
author: aimikoda
prompt:
Build a glitch title effect in code (Python/ffmpeg). [16:9, 1920x1080, 30fps, 10 s, with sound]

Text: "[WORD]", [white], [font name], dark drop shadow underneath.
Loop (x4): letters flash one at a time in their own slots within the word (2 frames each) →
full word appears with a slight jitter and occasional glitches → disappears by [glitching apart].

Background: dark base with bright, saturated, broken vertical scan lines and downward-dripping streaks;
dark areas stay as black silhouettes. Generate it from the attached images. Mix in striped ring/polygon scenes.
Hard cut every 2–4 frames, never repeating.
On top: horizontal slice shifts, RGB split, light grain. Colors: [red + cyan].

Story (optional): [short summary] — each loop is one chapter; colors, images and the exit effect match it.
Deliver: MP4 + script.

title: Explorable desert oasis tree village in Three.js
author: cryptomanavan
prompt:
Build this concept image as a AAA-quality, fully explorable Three.js/WebGPU world. Use the image as the primary art-direction reference.

Create a large, seamless desert oasis tree village centered around a crystal-clear turquoise lagoon. Ancient massive trees grow directly from rocky islands and shoreline areas, with believable roots, trunks, branches, dense foliage, vines, and vegetation. Integrate handcrafted tree homes naturally into the trees: wooden rooms, balconies, spiral/tree stairs, rope bridges, suspended walkways, lanterns, railings, docks, lookout platforms, thatched roofs, linen shade canopies, hanging baskets, and small gathering spaces.

The environment should feel physically plausible rather than theme-park-like. Tree architecture must appear structurally attached to trunks and branches. Bridges should sag naturally. Wood, bark, rope, stone, fabric, sand, vegetation, and water need high-resolution PBR materials with realistic roughness, normal variation, imperfections, weathering, and contact detail.

Make the lagoon a centerpiece: transparent tropical water, believable depth gradient, refraction, reflections, underwater visibility, caustics, shoreline wetness, gentle ripples, shallow sand, submerged rocks, and small waterfalls feeding the lagoon. Surround it with pale desert sand, rocky cliffs, palms and sparse oasis vegetation fading into a huge arid landscape.

Include multiple distinct tree houses based on the reference: large primary tree house, medium nest-style house, small perch, multi-level canopy house, and a house/platform extending over the water. Connect them into one coherent village using elevated bridges, ground trails, docks, and shoreline paths.

Lighting: cinematic late-afternoon/golden-hour daylight, physically based sky and atmosphere, soft volumetric haze, long natural shadows, subtle reflected turquoise light from the lagoon, warm lantern interiors, excellent exposure and tone mapping. No fantasy glow except believable lantern lighting.

Player should spawn near the lagoon at human eye height and freely explore in first person with smooth walking, sprinting, jumping, stairs, bridges, platforms, buildings, docks, shoreline, shallow water, and swimming. Use realistic collision and movement. Make distant views equally convincing from elevated tree houses.

Prioritize AAA visual fidelity + 60 FPS-class optimization: LODs, instancing, frustum/occlusion strategies, texture compression, baked/static lighting where appropriate, efficient foliage, pooled effects, sensible shadow distances, aggressive asset preloading, and no first-interaction hitching.

No sound/audio yet. No gameplay objectives or HUD clutter. The goal is a beautiful, photorealistic, peaceful world that feels like a real place someone could spend hours exploring.

title: Interactive plush frog toy with grooming mechanics
author: N1njaCodex
prompt: Build "Plush Frog" — Material Studies No. 011.  One self-contained HTML file, raw WebGPU/WGSL, no libraries, with a clean fallback card when WebGPU is missing. All labels in English.  SHAPE. An original plush frog (not a copy of any existing toy) as a signed distance field: a soft bean of a body, two eye bumps smooth-unioned on top, haunches folded at the sides, stubby front feet, flattened where it sits on the table. Skin = surface nets of the SDF (one Newton step, gradient normals).  SEWN-ON PARTS, all embedded in the simulation lattice so they ride along with every squeeze: – two glass safety eyes: near-black beads with a dark amber ring round the pupil and mirror-bright gloss; they stay rigid (follow the polar rotation of the averaged deformation gradient, never squash); – an embroidered smile: a round thread tube laid along a curve projected onto the face; – a felt lily-pad beret with a notch, draped over one eye bump (its height settled at build time so the underside just clears the skin), with five cupped felt petals and a wool-knot heart.  PHYSICS. XPBD on the CPU, 60 Hz, 6 substeps. Hex lattice in the body's principal frame, boundary nodes snapped to the surface, barycentric embedding of every render vertex. Co-rotational shape matching per 8-node cell (warm-started rotation, strain stiffening), soft tet volume constraints (the stuffing compresses a little, unlike jelly), a firmer fabric shell. Edge damping, deformation damping relative to rigid motion, rolling resistance, sleeping. Floor with Coulomb friction.  FUR. Shell fur: the skin drawn ~40 times as instanced shells, outermost first. Strands are jittered points in rest-space cubes (~0.8 mm spacing); each shell keeps the fragments within a tapered cone around each point, so thickness and length vary naturally; per-strand tilt and crimp, a vertex-level wave; alpha-to-coverage under 4× MSAA. Rest-space regions: cream belly patch, pink dyed cheeks, a groove for the smile, a back seam, stitched toe lines, pile pressed flat under the felt cap.  FUR MOTION. Laid-down pile stands lower.  SHADING. Wrapped diffuse through the pile, darker toward the roots, two Kajiya–Kay lobes, a velvet term (pile seen against its lie looks darker and denser, with it, it shines), a soft halo in the outermost wisps, a per-vertex soft key shadow on the shells. Procedural photo studio, PCSS floor shadow plus contact AO from a top-down height map, felt with fibre fuzz and sheen, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping. title: 15-second motion graphics video introducing overseas dramas
author: hAru_mAki_ch
prompt:
# ROLE

あなたは世界トップクラスのモーションデザイナー兼クリエイティブコーダーです。

ユーザーから与えられたテーマや指示を解釈し、その世界観を最大限に拡張した、ダイナミックで洗練された **15秒のモーショングラフィックス動画** を制作してください。

単なる説明動画ではありません。

Behance / OFFF / Awwwards / モーションデザインスタジオのショーリールに掲載できるレベルを目指し、

「この15秒だけで、この人のモーションデザイン能力が伝わる」

と思わせる作品にしてください。

---

# USER INPUT

以下のユーザー指示を、動画全体のテーマ・世界観・コピー・モーション表現へ変換してください。

```text
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}
```

ユーザーの指示が短くても、そのテーマから

- 世界観
- ストーリー
- キーワード
- 色
- タイポグラフィ
- 図形
- データ表現
- カメラワーク
- サウンド

を補完し、15秒の映像として成立させてください。

ユーザーが具体的なデザインを指定している場合は、その指定を最優先します。

---

# CREATIVE DIRECTION

動画は「履歴書用ショーリールのベスト15秒」のつもりで制作してください。

安全で無難なデザインに逃げず、

- 大胆なタイポグラフィ
- 高速なトランジション
- スケール変化
- 奥行き
- パララックス
- グリッド
- ライン
- UI
- データビジュアライゼーション
- パーティクル
- 3D空間
- カメラ移動
- モーションブラー
- 強弱のある静と動

などを組み合わせます。

ただし、すべてを同時に使う必要はありません。

テーマに最も合う表現を選択し、

**情報量は多いが、視線誘導は明快**

な映像にしてください。

テンプレート感のある企業PVではなく、デザイナーが意図を持って演出した作品にします。

---

# STORY STRUCTURE

15秒の中に明確な起承転結を作ります。

目安：

## 0–3秒：HOOK

最初の1秒以内に視線を奪ってください。

巨大なタイポ、急激なズーム、強い図形変化、3D空間への突入など、

「何が始まった？」

と思わせる導入にします。

## 3–7秒：DEVELOPMENT

ユーザーのテーマを視覚言語へ展開します。

文字、図形、ライン、データ、UI、アイコン、空間などを使って世界観を構築してください。

## 7–11秒：ESCALATION

映像密度とエネルギーを最大化します。

それまで登場した要素を再利用・再構成し、

カメラ移動、パーティクル、3D、グラフ、モーションブラーなどでクライマックスへ向かいます。

## 11–15秒：PAYOFF

映像を一度整理し、

最も伝えたいメッセージ、タイトル、コンセプトを強く表示します。

最後の1〜2秒は静止画として切り出しても成立する、美しいエンドフレームにしてください。

---

# MOTION PRINCIPLES

すべての動きには意図を持たせてください。

単純な fadeIn / fadeOut の連続は禁止です。

基本的に以下を活用してください。

- overshoot
- anticipation
- follow-through
- stagger
- spring
- easing
- scale transition
- masking
- clipping
- motion blur
- parallax
- camera movement
- rhythmic cuts

重要な動きは音楽の拍と同期させます。

「速い → 止まる → 爆発する」

「密集 → 解放」

「2D → 3D」

など、モーションにコントラストを作ってください。

---

# TECHNICAL STACK

映像は **Remotion** で実装してください。

使用技術：

- Node.js
- Remotion 4
- React 19
- TypeScript
- CSS
- SVG
- Canvas
- CSS 3D
- @remotion/motion-blur

必要に応じてGoogle Fontsを使用して構いません。

---

# ANIMATION ARCHITECTURE

Adobe After Effectsのように大量の手動キーフレームを打つ設計ではなく、

**現在のフレーム番号を入力として、映像の状態を数式で決める**

というRemotionらしい設計にしてください。

例えば、

```ts
const frame = useCurrentFrame();
const {fps} = useVideoConfig();
```

を基準として、

- position
- scale
- rotation
- opacity
- blur
- perspective
- color
- camera position
- particle position

などを計算します。

可能な限り、

- interpolate()
- spring()
- easing
- 数学関数
- deterministic random

を使ってください。

---

# RENDERING METHOD

表現によって描画方式を使い分けてください。

## Typography / UI

CSS transform

- translate
- scale
- rotate
- skew
- clip-path
- filter
- perspective

## Lines / Graphs / Diagrams

SVG

- path
- strokeDasharray
- strokeDashoffset
- mask
- clipPath

などを使います。

## 3D

可能なものはCSS 3Dで構築します。

- perspective
- translateZ
- rotateX
- rotateY
- transform-style: preserve-3d

を利用し、

トンネル、カード空間、タイポグラフィ空間などを制作できます。

## Particles

大量のパーティクルはDOM要素を大量生成せず、

Canvasを使って描画してください。

数百〜数千個の粒子でも安定してレンダリングできる構造にします。

---

# AUDIO

可能であれば外部音源素材を使わず、Node.jsで音を生成してください。

追加の音声生成npmパッケージに依存しない構成を優先します。

Node.js標準機能でPCM/WAVを書き出してください。

例えば、

- Kick
- Hi-hat
- Click
- Impact
- Rise
- Noise
- Sub bass
- UI beep

The scene is a floating island. title: 20-second satisfying physics short of balls multiplying inside a
author: treyscalez
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: the machine (default: Crusher; others: Sweeper Arm, Laser Blades, Rotating Frame, Multiplier Zones, Split Rings), how many new balls one hit ball becomes (default 8), the length (default 20 seconds), and whether I have my own sound effects (if not, synthesize them in numpy).
</inputs>

<direction>
An oddly satisfying physics short at 1080x1920, 30fps, drawn entirely in code with Python, pymunk and OpenCV, every shape anti-aliased with cv2.LINE_AA at sub-pixel shift 4.
Space: pure black #000000, no gradient, no stars. The arena is a white ring, radius 438px, 5px stroke, centred at 540,960.
The machine: brushed steel #8E9198 with a darker edge #5C5F66 and a 2px highlight line #B9BCC2 along its top, 6-7px rounded corners, three small dark bolts per plate and a thin orange pad #E9A23B on every face that touches balls. For the Crusher: a 16px steel rail from each jaw's outer side to the screen edge with a rounded end cap, and two C-shaped jaws "[ ]" facing each other, each a 42x312 back plate with top and bottom arms 118px long and 33px thick pointing inward. No rail between the jaws.
Balls: flat solid circles with no outline or shading, radius 9px, the first ball 17px. Each wave is a new color in this order: orange #FF8A1F, indigo #4B2BFF, green #3BFF3B, pink #FF2D7A, cyan #22C3F5, yellow #FFF000, purple #A01EFF, mint #1FF58A, red #FF3B1F. Old colors stay, so the ring marbles into a mix.
Draw order: ring, rail, balls, squashed balls, machine on top.
Finish: one white flash at 55% fading over 5 frames on the finale, nothing else.
Banned: text, captions, counters or watermarks on screen (except zone labels on Multiplier Zones), camera moves, gradients, glow on balls, gravity pulling down, balls spawning inside the machine, AI images or AI video, NexusBox Lab's logo or name.
</direction>

<structure>
20 seconds, the machine never stops moving and every crush is bigger than the last.
One orange ball sitting still left of centre at 400,955, jaws open (0s) → the jaws start closing at 0.2s with an ease-in cubic slam over 0.5s, the ball gets swept in and squashed, pinch at 0.7s, 8 indigo balls shoot out both sides → jaws ease back open over 1.2s and rest → every 2.4s the same clamp: pinches at 3.1, 5.5, 7.9, 10.3, 12.7 and 15.1s, each crushing whatever drifted into the jaws and turning every crushed ball into exactly 8 of the next color, so the waves grow 8 → 8 → 16 → 32 → 88 → 264 → 880 and the ring fills up (0.7-15.1s) → on the last close the ring itself gets pulled in and shrinks into a white capsule squeezed between the jaws (17.0s) → pinch: capsule vanishes, white flash, deep boom, the red wave of 2,000+ balls bursts out and every ball blasts off screen at 600-1100px/s (17.5s) → the empty jaws clamp once more on black at 19.9s so the last frame flows into the first.
For any other machine, keep the same shape: one lonely ball, the first hit before 1s, a hit every 2-2.5s with each wave a new color and 8x bigger, the ring fills, the machine destroys the ring at about 87% of the length, everything explodes off screen, the empty machine keeps moving into a seamless loop. Sweeper Arm: a 12-tooth gear with a 150-degree curved arm sweeping round, pinning balls against the ring. Laser Blades: 5 neon cyan blades spinning from a hub, slicing balls in two. Rotating Frame: a spinning square frame that squeezes shut every 2.4s, on two X rails. Multiplier Zones: an octagon with gates labelled x20, x5, BIG, SMALL and a skull, with normal gravity. Split Rings: four corner ramps tipping colored piles into four stacked rings with rotating gaps.
</structure>

<build>
1. One Python script. Every number in a CONFIG block at the top, a fixed random seed (default 4) I can change with an environment variable, raw frames piped straight into ffmpeg.
2. Physics: pymunk with zero gravity, 10 substeps per frame, 12 iterations, space.damping 1.0 so balls never slow down, ball elasticity 0.95, machine 0.6, wall 1.0, friction 0, speed clamped at 1100px/s. A gentle spring pull toward the centre (2.0 x distance per second squared) keeps balls drifting back into the machine. Switch it off when the ring breaks.
3. The ring wall is 160 static segments just outside radius 438. Every moving machine part is a KINEMATIC body: every substep set its position AND its velocity from the next substep's target, or balls tunnel through and don't get shoved.
4. The crush: once the jaws' arms overlap, the box is sealed. Balls inside leave the physics and are drawn squashed, keeping their x as a fraction of the gap and narrowing into ellipses. At the pinch they all count as crushed.
5. The multiply rule: spawn EXACTLY crushed x 8 new balls, no rounding, no fixed totals, safety cap 4000. Stream them out over 9 frames just outside the jaws, worked out from where the jaws are when each ball appears, flying away at 250-520px/s fanned over 110 degrees. Print one line per pinch: "pinch N: crushed X -> spawned Y (x8), total Z".
6. Sound: one effect per event kind (jaw whir rising 120 to 380Hz through each close, metal clunk on each pinch, a burst of 14 tiny pops 22ms apart on each spawn, a deep 1.6s boom on the finale), each peak-aligned to its frame. If I gave you my own sound effects, use them instead. Normalize the mix to -1.5dB peak and mux it with ffmpeg.
7. Encode with libx264 at CRF 17, yuv420p, preset veryfast, AAC 192k.
</build>

<gotchas>
With damping below 1.0, balls lose their energy and settle in the gaps above, below and behind the jaws, so nothing gets crushed and the waves die out. Without the centre pull the same thing happens: test it and you'll see crushes of 1, 0, 0, 0. Spawn positions must follow the jaws as they open, or the finale wave gets stuck inside the jaws. If fewer than 1 ball is crushed in each of the first 3 pinches, try another seed or raise the pull. If the cap gets hit before the finale, lower the pull. Run the physics once with rendering switched off, show me the crush log and a contact sheet of every pinch before the full render.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me the inputs, run the physics and show me the crush log with the wave sizes it gives, then build and render the video.

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: twoclipping
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word), a 4-word tagline, the 3-step story of what it does, a launch date and domain, a royalty-free song with a clear drop, 4 vertical talking-to-camera clips and 12 portrait photos. If I skip any, use the defaults: "castr", "ugc ads, cast by ai", write a brief → scan 1,000 creators → cast 4, Mixkit "Cat Walk" (129.6 BPM, drop at 29.7s), free Pexels clips and portraits, and transparent stickers from Pixabay (serum, mic, megaphone, vintage camera, spotlight, lips).
</inputs>

<direction>
A 25 second square launch trailer, 1440x1440 at 60fps, loud poster style. Cobalt #2B3BFF, ink #0E0F1F, cream #F6E4C6, pink #FF7DC7, tangerine #FF5A1F. Archivo 900 extra-condensed for names, expanded for headlines, Geist and Geist Mono for labels. Op-art sunburst, scrolling waves, film grain. Real media only: the clips play inside the design, and the stickers get a white die-cut border and a soft shadow.
Motion rules: the camera never stops (a slow 1.03-1.07 push on every scene), nothing pops in (letters rise through a mask line one by one), nothing snaps to the beat (patterns rotate continuously), swaps are carousel glides of about 0.55s, colour changes fade over about 0.35s, stickers ease in and then keep a slow sway. No full stops after the wordmark or any headline.
Banned: beat-snapped rotations, pop-in slams, white flashes, crossfades between scenes, hard cuts, templates.
</direction>

<structure>
54 beats. The song starts 8 beats before its drop.
Beats 0-8: a cobalt sunburst turns around a breathing cream disc. The wordmark types in with a gliding caret and the tagline pill rises. The disc floods the frame into the drop.
Beat 8, the drop: the cream becomes the face of a 3D box and "ONE BRIEF" rises letter by letter. The camera pulls back to the box floating on waves. On beat 12 it turns to "1,000 CREATORS" (stacked, with outlined echoes), on beat 14 to "ZERO DMs".
Beats 16-22: a whip to a dark desk. A tangerine "BRIEF #042" ticket types its rows (product, vibe, cast, due), stickers drift on, a polaroid of a real clip drops onto the corner, and a "NOW CASTING" stamp presses down on beat 20.
Beats 22-34: the casting stage. A crowd of black and white portraits in an arc, a 3D stage block, and the creators gliding through like a carousel. Each plays live in a big disc in black and white, with their name in pink on the stage, their followers, and a MATCH % that counts up. One beat later a "CAST ✓" stamp lands and the clip fades to colour. A counter rolls 1/4 to 4/4.
Beats 34-39: pink floods out of the last disc. The disc morphs into a phone screen (the clip keeps playing) and fans into 4 phones playing all 4 creators, with views counting up. "4 ADS" and "BY FRIDAY" rise.
Beats 39-44, the music's break: the pink floor drops away and a cream "JOIN THE WAITLIST" ticket glides down onto the sunburst. On the pickup its stub tears off.
Beats 44-54: the ticket body morphs into a poster arch. The wordmark rises in, then the tagline, then an info bar slides up in 3 blocks (date, numbers, domain) and a ticker runs round the frame edge. Then it all folds back into the opening disc, so the last frame is the first.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Every frame is a pure function of time inside seek(t).
2. A beat map in beats, B = 60/BPM, with the song placed so its drop lands on beat 8.
3. The 3D box is an orthographic projection: each face is a 1440px offscreen canvas drawn with an affine transform and shaded by its normal.
4. Cut the clips to 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg, draw frame floor(t*30), and do the black and white with ctx.filter.
5. Trim the sticker PNGs and add the die-cut border by dilating their alpha.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event (a shutter on every cast, whooshes on the glides, key clicks on the typing), each placed by its measured peak. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 8 motion-blur subframes. Scan for single-frame pops, then compare its motion against a reference video (hard jumps per second, share of still frames).
</build>

<gotchas>
A pattern that rotates one notch per beat reads as stutter: rotate it continuously, and pick each ring's speed so it lands on the same pattern at the last frame. 4 subframes ghost on fast whips, so use 8. A layer whose background is a huge flood circle still covers the screen after sliding down one frame height, so switch it to a full-frame rect once it has flooded. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's. The disc must morph inside the same camera transform as the scene it leaves, or it jumps.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, box, brief, casting, phones, poster) before you render.
</start>

title: 3D character rebuilt from a turnaround sheet with animations
author: bonsaixbt
prompt:
Delete the "learn Blender first" step. Claude Opus 5.5 rebuilt my mascot in 3D straight from his character sheet, skeleton and animations included

No Blender, no 3D artist, no rigging tutorial. Just one PNG with four views of a guy who has a bonsai growing out of his TV head

I expected a rough blocky mannequin that only sort of looked like him. Instead Claude read the sheet the way a modeler reads a turnaround, front, side and back, and carried over every detail it could see, right down to the pixel bonsai on the hoodie and the green heels on the sneakers

The trick is that a chunky stylized character isn't really "3D art" to Claude, it's geometry it can describe in Three.js, so the whole hero ends up as one readable file you can open and change

Here's how it works:

> Claude uses the front, side and back views as the blueprint for proportions, so the head, hoodie and baggy cargo pants keep the same silhouette as the drawing
> it builds the model from rounded blocks and voxels: a TV head with a pixel screen face that blinks, a 354-voxel bonsai, the hoodie, the cargo pants and the sneakers
> it rigs him with 18 real bones from the hips up to the head, plus one extra bone for the tree, so the bonsai sways and lags behind every time he moves
> it writes five animations by hand (idle, walk, run, jump and wave) and blends between them, so switching from a run into a jump doesn't snap
> it drops him into a small paper-style level where WASD walks, Shift runs, Space jumps and E makes him wave

You can use the same approach for a brand mascot on your landing page, a hero for a weekend game jam, an animated avatar for your videos, or a quick prototype before you pay anyone for production 3D

title: Pixel-art 3D floating-island funfair with a physics roller coaster
author: 0kncn
prompt:
Make a pixel-art 3D diorama of a funfair on a floating island, the same series and engine as my other pixel dioramas (three.js, orthographic isometric camera turned in quarter steps, small render target with no anti-aliasing snapped to whole pixels, depth-based outlines, a fixed 64-colour palette matched in OKLab, hard sun shadows, day/dusk/night, rain with puddles). Call it “Lift Hill”.

The fair: a wooden roller coaster with a chain lift hill, a turning first drop, camelback hills and a banked turnaround, built on a white timber lattice of bents, ledgers and diagonal braces that reaches down to the grass; a station with a striped roof, a numbered sign and a switchback queue. Around it: a Ferris wheel whose gondolas hang free, a chair-swing ride, a carousel with bobbing horses, a bumper-car arena under a spark grid, a cotton-candy stall, a popcorn stall, a balloon seller, an information booth, a photo booth, a bulb-lit entrance arch, lamp posts, benches, round trees and conifers, and a fence along the edge of the island.

Real coaster physics: the train runs on a spline sampled by arc length. Each step it feels gravity from the slope under every car, rolling friction and air drag; the chain grabs it on the lift and its anti-rollback dogs hold it there; trims, brakes and station tyres slow it and park it. The track is banked from its real curvature and the speed a dry run predicts. Riders feel the actual vertical and lateral g from the speed, the curvature and gravity: they lift their arms and float off their seats in airtime and lean into the turns. Offer three layouts (Classic out-and-back, Twister with a helix, Hyper with airtime hills) and a lift-height slider. If the lift is too low the train does not crest a later hill, rolls back, gets stranded in the valley and is towed over by maintenance. Show speed, height, vertical and lateral g, the energy head against the next hill and a prediction for the chosen lift height.

Other physics: Ferris gondolas are pendulums driven by the wheel’s acceleration, so they swing when it starts and stops; the chair-swing seats find their angle from the spin (tan θ = ω²r / g) with lag; bumper cars are rigid discs that collide with impulses, bounce off the walls and spin, with sparks.

Life: visitors walk the paths, queue for the coaster in the switchback, board in order, ride with their own shirt colours and walk off at the exit; parents walk with children; a child sometimes gets lost, the PA asks the grown-up to come to the information booth, the parent goes there and then to the child; umbrellas come out in the rain. Bulbs along the track and the rides light up and chase at night, lamp posts light the paths, and fireworks go off. Tap the ground to let a balloon go, tap at night for a firework, tap the station to dispatch. English UI; must work on phones.

prompt:

At the end the kraken's head rises from the water behind the island, with a glowing yellow eye and a slit pupil, as lightning strikes.
