title: 20-second beat-synced fashion montage with image morphs and motion
author: AI_swwww
prompt:
<inputs>
まず私に聞いて：作品のテーマを一言、画面に出す英単語（フック4語・対になる大きな2語・ティッカー3語・ロゴ1語）、アクセントカラー1色、画像の方向性（実写／イラスト／両方）、使う曲（ドロップがはっきりした商用利用OKの曲。指定がなければ Mixkit などフリー音源から候補を集めて解析で選ぶ）。
</inputs>

<assets>
画像は gpt-image-2 で作る（手持ちの画像でも可）。
1. 縦2:3（1024x1536）の実写ポートレートを8枚。ハイエンドなファッション誌風、成人女性、服を着た非性的な構図、背景はニュートラル。アクセントカラーの小物を各画像に1つだけ入れる。
2. 8枚それぞれを参照画像にして、同じ構図・同じポーズ・同じ背景色のままイラスト版を作る。マッチカットに使うので構図は絶対に変えない。
3. 各画像について、アクセントカラーの位置（重心）、左右の縁の色、実写とイラストのずれを数値で測ってJSONに保存する。
</assets>

<direction>
ハイエンドミニマル。1ショットに1アイデア、余白たっぷり、アクセントカラー1色、字間を詰めたサンセリフ（Geist か Inter）。マスクで文字が現れる演出、マッチカット、カメラの動きは「ゆっくり寄る」の1種類だけ。縦の画像は16:9の中央に置き、左右は画像の縁の色に溶かす。画面の文字に句点は付けない。
禁止：衝撃波リング、パーティクル、RGBずらし、手ブレ、レンズフレア、ネオン、グリッドの床、点滅する背景、バウンドするイージング。
</direction>

<structure>
曲のBPMで10小節。ドロップを3小節目の1拍目に置く。
1小節目：フックの4語が1拍に1語ずつ着地。
2小節目：フックの1語が画像に変わる（文字の一番太い画に吸い込まれて写真が全面に出る）。カーソルが線をドラッグして左半分をイラスト版に変え、アクセントの小物をクリック。
ドロップ：クリックした点から円が開いて暗いシーンへ。
そこから1小節に1つの動き：16枚の壁にスキャンラインが走って勝者3枚を選ぶ → 勝者を壁の位置からマッチカットして大きな文字（実写側の語）→ 床反射とモーションブラー付きの3Dカルーセルがウィップして1枚が正面へ → その1枚を左に、右の縦フレームのパネルが1拍ずつイラスト版に反転 → プッシュカットで大きな文字（イラスト側の語）→ 3語のティッカー → ロゴ → 黒へフェード。
</structure>

<build>
1. 1920x1080の1つのHTMLファイル。全スタイルは https://t.co/Dp87FqCCXX(t) の中で時刻から計算する。CSSアニメなし、タイマーなし、フレーム間の状態なし。
2. 曲を numpy で解析：テンポ、ビートグリッド、小節ごとのエネルギー、ドロップ。グリッドは使う区間の実際のキックに最小二乗で合わせる。カットは全部ダウンビート、UIの動きは全部ビートに合わせる。
3. 小節・拍の時刻と効果音のキューは1つのタイムラインファイルにまとめ、映像と音の両方がそこを読む。
4. Playwright でレンダー：1フレームを t−1/240 〜 t+1/240 のサブフレームで撮って平均し、60fpsの本物のモーションブラーにする。既定は7枚、ウィップ・ズーム・スライドなど速い区間は11〜25枚。
5. 効果音はコードで合成し、測定したピークがイベントの瞬間に来るように置く。音楽の下で静かに。loudnorm で -14 LUFS。
6. 本番の前に20フレーム以上を試し撮りして一覧で確認し、散らかり・重なり・読みにくさを直してからフルレンダーする。
</build>

<gotchas>
preserve-3d の要素に opacity や filter を付けない（平らになって裏面が見える）。フェードは外側のラッパーで行う。
マッチカットの位置は実行時に測る。
サブフレームが3枚だと、細い線や速い動きが二重に見える。
アクセントの点をアクセント色の物の上に置くと見えない。白地に色の芯を入れたボタンにする。
ドロップ検出は、曲頭の無音からの立ち上がりを誤検出しやすい。4つ打ちでない曲はキックに合わせられないので避ける。
音楽と効果音は、商用利用を許可するライセンスのものだけを使う。
</gotchas>

<start>
まずインプットを聞き、コードを書く前に、ビートグリッドに全タイミングを載せたストーリーボードを見せて。
</start>

曲：Mixkit「Dub Techno Groove」（Mixkit Stock Music Free License）

Do not simply place a logo on a generic castle. Give your kingdom a distinctive architectural character and a coherent visual identity. Invent its coat of arms, royal colors and an original heraldic emblem. Display them on animated banners, shields, gate decorations and the clothing of the castle guards. LIFE AND INTERACTION

Use instancing and geometry batching where appropriate. Keep animation and camera interaction smooth. Provide a minimal, elegant English interface and a button to hide it.

I want to reproduce published adversarial clothing research (Thys et al. 2019 "Fooling automated surveillance cameras", Wu et al. "Making an Invisibility Cloak") on my own PC and webcam, to test how robust open-source person detectors are.

Goal: generate a printable pattern that lowers the "person" confidence of an open-source detector when I hold it in front of my torso or wear it on a shirt.

step 1 → set up Python + PyTorch + Ultralytics. Target: a small current YOLO, person class only. Use my GPU if available and verify it works first. Measure the clean detection rate on test images with no patch.

step 2 → data: a COCO person subset (a few thousand images) or INRIA Person, with a held-out test split I never train on. Patch: a learnable 300x300 RGB tensor from random noise. Loss = max "person" confidence on the patched boxes (use the raw model output before NMS so gradients flow) + total variation. Train with Adam, save the patch every epoch, log mean person confidence: no patch vs random-noise patch vs my patch. If mine isn't clearly better than random, say so.

step 3 → robustness: paste the patch on each person's torso with random scale, rotation ±20°, perspective, brightness/contrast, blur, noise and wrinkle-like distortion.

step 4 → printability: generate a color chart for me to print and photograph, build the palette from that photo, add a non-printability score to the loss.

step 5 → evaluate on the held-out split: % of patched persons NOT detected at conf 0.25, vs the clean rate. Then test transfer on a second detector (e.g. RT-DETR) and report it honestly.

step 6 → export a print-ready PDF (A3, 300 dpi) and a tiled T-shirt version.

step 7 → live demo: webcam + detector, person boxes with confidence, live confidence graph, FPS, dashboard overlay. Record to mp4.

title: Real-time AR putting coach overlay for Meta Ray-Ban glasses
author: 0xCodez
prompt:
You're a senior AR + computer vision engineer. 

I own Meta Ray-Ban 2 glasses (photo attached) and an Android phone. Turn the glasses into a real-time AR putting coach.

STEP 1: RECON

- Walk me through enabling Bluetooth HCI snoop log, then parse btsnoop_hci.log with tshark
- Decompile the Meta AI app with jadx and map how the camera stream and display overlay are called
- Cross-check against Meta's Wearables Device Access Toolkit
- Output: a spec of how to pull camera frames to the phone and push rendered pixels back to the lens

STEP 2: AGENTS

Spin up 4 Claude Code agents in tmux with one shared SPEC.md:
- agent 1: camera stream + overlay link
- agent 2: vision
- agent 3: putt physics
- agent 4: UI
Each agent tests against recorded footage of a green before touching the live glasses.

STEP 3: SCAN THE GREEN

- Monocular SLAM for head pose + Depth Anything V2 for dense depth
- Metric scale from known objects: ball = 42.67 mm, cup = 108 mm
- Point cloud → Delaunay mesh → heightmap with 5 cm cells

STEP 4: READ THE BREAK

- Slope per cell from the heightmap gradient
- Contour line every 1 cm of elevation (marching squares)
- YOLO detects the ball, flagstick + dark ellipse = the hole

STEP 5: SIMULATE THE PUTT

- Rolling ball physics: 5/7 g along the slope, friction from green speed (default Stimp 10, editable)
- RK4 integration, 1 ms steps
- Search launch angle + speed so the ball finishes 17 inches past the cup
- Render: ideal line (blue), aim line (red), aim point, corridor of putts that still drop, yellow setup lines at my feet square to the aim line

STEP 6: HANDS-FREE UI

- MediaPipe Hands on the same camera feed, index fingertip on a bubble = tap
- Floating bubble menu: Ideal Line, Aiming Line, Contour Lines, Setup Lines, Corridor, Putt Info, Animation
- Actions: New Ball, New Target, New Putt

RULES

- Re-project every overlay into the current camera pose each frame, under 100 ms end to end
- Ask me before anything that needs a physical action (pairing, approving the connection)
- Ship a working build I can test on a practice green today

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: 0xnicc0
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a one-word product name for the wordmark, one accent color, and a royalty-free track around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Product-launch UI motion in one continuous take. One shape tells the whole story: a prompt bar becomes a button, the button becomes a progress ring, the ring becomes a preview window, the window fills the screen, then shrinks into a toast and back into the prompt bar. No cuts, no fades between scenes: objects transform. A cursor triggers every change with real clicks. Warm off-white canvas, black UI, one accent color, Inter for UI and the wordmark. Springs everywhere with only a slight overshoot. Zoom the camera so each moment fills the square.
Banned: crossfades, gradients on UI, particles, glows, bouncy easing, dead beats, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 24 beats, something happens on every beat.
Type the request into the prompt bar → click send → the bar collapses into a black circle → a progress ring fills in four steps while four chips spring out (concept, storyboard, motion, sound) → the chips fly into a timeline and the circle becomes a preview window → a playhead sweeps the clips → inside the preview an orbit draws itself, a planet starts moving and the wordmark rises letter by letter from a mask line → the preview fills the screen → the letters drop away, the planet flies into a toast and becomes its checkmark → "Rendered in code · 60 fps" → the toast turns back into an empty prompt bar. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file with a 1440x1440 canvas. Draw everything inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form spring step responses. When a value changes target several times, add one spring per change so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The main shape is one rounded rect whose width, height, radius, position and color are each a chain of springs.
4. Typing is derived from time: characters shown = floor(progress × length), with a caret that blinks only when idle.
5. Find the beat grid of the track, start on a downbeat and place every click, pop and chime on its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright at 60 fps, then encode H.264 CRF 16 and loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render one still per beat first. Fix anything cramped, off-grid or hard to read before the full render.
</build>

<gotchas>
Text inside a morphing shape needs its own clip and separate enter/exit timing. Text swaps need their own fade so they never overlap. The cursor must end at the exact position it started, or the loop will stutter.
</gotchas>

title: Interactive 3D night train crossing a mountain viaduct
author: Artless101
prompt:
Create a polished, fully interactive 3D artwork called "Nocturne - The Highland Night Train" using Three.js and WebGL. Deliver the entire experience as one standalone HTML file that opens directly in Chrome. Generate the models, materials and textures procedurally, and embed dependencies so the final file can also work offline. Start from scratch and give the scene its own visual identity.

ART DIRECTION
An elegant burgundy night express crosses a monumental curved stone viaduct above a deep alpine valley. Dense conifer forests, a winding river, distant cottages and rugged snow-covered mountains surround the railway. Use a cinematic, carefully detailed miniature style, with cool moonlight, deep blue shadows and warm golden carriage windows. The result should feel like a finished interactive artwork, with thoughtful composition and readable details.

THE TRAIN
Build a convincing diesel locomotive and four passenger carriages. Use deep burgundy paint, cream stripes, brass handrails and charcoal roofs. Model rounded body panels, cab windows, front lamps, radiator grilles, roof fans, exhaust, walkways, steps, buffers, couplings, bogies, wheel flanges and suspension details. Include window frames, curtains and subtle passenger silhouettes. Keep windows and decorative parts visibly outside the body surfaces, without intersections or flickering.

RAILWAY AND MOVEMENT
Create a continuous elliptical railway loop supported by a tall masonry viaduct. Construct actual open arches, piers, individual arch stones, parapets, rails and sleepers. Add procedural stone variation and subtle surface relief. Supports must meet the terrain and the track must have no gaps.

Move the train at a believable, steady speed using an arc-length-parameterized route. Position and orient every carriage independently. Keep the wheels aligned with the rails and make bogies follow the track correctly through turns. Couplings must remain connected without overlapping carriages. Add restrained suspension movement, rotating wheels and exhaust that drifts away into world space.

ENVIRONMENT AND LIGHTING
Use thousands of efficiently instanced conifers with varied heights, shapes and colors. Sculpt irregular mountain ridges with snow on the upper slopes. Add atmospheric depth, a starry sky, a moon halo and a softly feathered headlight beam through the mist. Use warm windows, controlled bloom, soft shadows and subtle color grading. Preserve detail in the train and bridge instead of crushing them into black silhouettes.

INTERACTION
Provide four smoothly transitioning cameras: Cinematic, Train, Window Seat and Free Orbit. Let users rotate and zoom freely. Keep useful framing on both desktop and mobile.

Add distinctly different Moonlight, Blue Hour and First Light presets. Include play/pause, speed controls, a horn button, sound on/off, volume and an option to hide the interface. Use a restrained English-only interface with elegant typography and unobtrusive controls.

AUDIO AND QUAL

title: 30-second dark fantasy battle scene with a warrior and armored
author: MadMax_Series
prompt: 色调为冷青灰、暴风蓝、黑铁、湿石和暗红披风；雨水与闪电在金属边缘形成冷白高光，结尾冲击短暂加入白金光，光闪过去仍恢复同一冷色战场。角色A是唯一露出面孔的成年男性重斧战士，约三十多岁，身材高大魁梧、宽肩厚胸、粗壮手臂，浅色偏冷肤色，短黑发向后上方竖起，两侧较短，浓黑眉，灰蓝眼睛，宽下颌，鼻梁与左眉附近有固定细旧疤，始终无头盔、无胡须。穿黑铁胸甲和银灰磨损包边、两侧极厚圆弧肩甲与少量粗短锥形铆刺、护臂、深色腰甲与分片腿甲、黑色护膝及重靴；上臂局部露出自然皮肤。唯一一件深红长披风始终固定在肩背，随风、奔跑和转体被拉向后方，不能独立飞走。脸、短发、疤痕、肩甲尺寸、胸甲结构、披风颜色和体格在远景与近景完全一致。A具有本世界明确夸张的英雄力量，受力、支撑、接触先后与运动方向仍必须连贯。唯一武器是一把接近他身高的双手长柄重战斧：深色缠握长柄、牢固金属套筒、同一个宽大的不对称弯月斧头，大主刃向外弯曲，背侧为较小上弯钩刃。所有刃部属于同一个固定斧头，不是两把斧；轮廓、柄长和斧头与柄的连接不变。A右手始终控制这同一根斧柄，左手只在需要时加入同一斧柄；使用空左前臂撞开敌人时右手仍持斧。斧不变成剑、长枪或锤，不脱手、不悬空、不出现在背上，不复制第二根柄或第二个斧头。角色B是高处观战的唯一成年男性蒙面统领，体格健壮但轮廓比A修长，封闭银灰尖棱面甲、狭长暗红眼缝、V形额面结构和竖向口部栅格，暗酒红紫色兜帽与颈巾围住头盔，黑钢胸甲，两侧肩甲有巨大弯月形外张刃翼。B脸部始终被同一面甲遮住，不摘盔，不变成A，没有A的黑色短发或深红长披风。B在本片只从高处观察，不突然跑进人群与A决斗，不额外亮出武器。敌军为数十名互不相同的成年士兵，黑灰或深青兜帽、深色面巾、旧皮甲混合暗钢胸甲、缠布前臂、深色裤与靴，主要持木柄铁头长矛，少数持短剑；体型、姿势与攻击节奏有差异，不能复制同一个士兵。前排主动迎击，后排持续补位；除开场列阵镜头外，不能全程站着观看、整齐让路或同时做一样动作。环境：暴雨中的荒凉山谷战场，黑色湿泥与裸岩交错，浅积水、折断木柄、插在地里的旧剑与长矛、碎石和破损无字战旗分布在前景，周围尖峭山壁被青灰云雾遮挡。A起初站在较低的泥石坡缘，敌军在前方谷地，B位于敌军后方较高的岩台；三处是同一个连续山谷，始终有地理联系。斜雨连续落下，风吹旗布和披风，远处偶有自然闪电，近处残破长矛与剑柄形成前景parallax。主战场不突然变成室内、雪地、沙漠或晴天。0.00–1.20秒：从A背后的低位极宽景开始，他正迎着谷地里的敌军向前踏出沉重一步，深红披风向画面左后方飘起，右侧重斧斧头原本低在湿地旁。他弯右肘、抬肩，把同一把斧从低位向肩部提起，左手短暂扶柄稳定重量；靴子踩进泥水形成明确压痕。远处高岩台上的B只是一道很小的剪影，山谷军阵与前景断矛同时可见。1.20–2.40秒：切贴近A肩背的over-shoulder近景，长斧柄已经横靠肩后，右手紧握柄，固定斧头从上侧前景掠过。镜头沿斧柄轻微横移，从粗短肩甲铆刺和黑发之间看向远处岩台；雨滴沿金属流下，披风持续有重量地摆动，不静止成海报。2.40–3.40秒：切A正面紧近景，固定的短黑发、旧疤、粗眉、宽颧骨和下颌保持高级数字雕刻游戏脸；他收紧下颌，眼睛盯住前方敌阵，雨水顺脸部滑落，鼻息沉重但不说话。镜头短促推进，不增加嘴型台词。3.40–4.70秒：切敌军前排的低中景，两名兜帽长矛兵在前景，更多士兵层叠在雨雾后方。前排把原本接近竖直的长矛向A的来向压低，靴子向前挪步，后排开始跟进；B所在的高岩台仍在远处背景。手与矛柄明确相连，兵器不穿过邻兵，队伍不是静态人墙。4.70–6.30秒：切B胸上正面近景，银灰尖棱面甲、暗红眼缝、紫红兜帽与巨大弯月肩甲清楚可读。B略低头观察山谷，雨滴沿面甲和肩刃滑落；摄影机微微靠近，保持冷淡而危险的凝视，不说话、不摘面甲、不抢先攻击。6.30–9.50秒：切回A三分之四脸部近景，他目光先向进攻线路移动，头肩随之转向，再压低重心。镜头快速移到侧脸，A发出一次短促、低沉、完全无词的战斗吼声，随即向前蹬地冲出；左手加入同一斧柄，把斧从肩后转到身体外侧准备作战，不能在换镜时直接变成已挥出的另一把斧。最后一瞬摄影机被他的肩甲与披风从旁掠过带出快速横移，动作直接衔接奔跑。9.50–12.20秒：切极低侧向广角追拍，A从画面左向右高速跑向敌军，身体与脸朝右、脚向右交替落地推进，后脚蹬开泥水，红披风明确拖在左后方。摄影机沿同方向平行移动，近处插地剑柄与断矛快速向左掠过、远山缓慢移动，保持强烈前景parallax与轻微倾斜地平线。看见至少三次完整的蹬地、腾空短步和落脚，不用脚底在地上滑行代替奔跑，不倒跑。前方士兵主动迎上，双方距离持续缩短；A不是奔过一排不动的群众。12.20–13.30秒：切A背侧低位追随，前排两名长矛兵朝他刺来 title: Twenty-second color theory motion graphics with a spinning wheel
author: koldo2k
prompt: Explain the color wheel in a dynamic ~20-second motion graphics video, same energy as a motion designer's showreel. Use the classic 12-hue artist's wheel and cover eight color harmonies: complementary, split complementary, analogous, triadic, square, compound, monochromatic and shades. The wheel should spin and click into place while the colors get selected, and each harmony should be drawn as its own shape on the wheel. Make it a journey of colors, not a static diagram: every harmony becomes a full-screen world made from its palette, and the camera dives through the center of the wheel into the next one. Use short English captions with the name, the angle and the swatches with hex codes, and sound designed in code, synced to every spin and selection.

④GPT6-Astra用プロンプト
_______________________________________＿
あなたは、VTuberの切り抜きやMVを作るモーショングラフィックス担当です。
添付したダンス動画から、VTuberらしい「踊ってみた」風のモーショングラフィックス動画を完成品として書き出してください。

■ 入力
・ダンス動画：添付ファイル（背景は緑、床が黒の場合あり）
・チャンネル名／キャラ名：【例：なし（入れない）】
・締めの一言：【例：よろしくね♡】
・テーマカラー：【例：ピンク・レモン・水色・紺】

■ 絶対に守ること
・画面に出す文字はすべて日本語。英語やアルファベットは一切使わない（「BPM」は「テンポ」、「BEAT」は「拍」、数字は可）
・文字がキャラに隠れて読めなくならないように配置する（文字とキャラを左右に分ける、または文字をキャラより手前に置く）
・流れるコメントはキャラの顔に重ねない

■ 手順
1. 切り抜き
　・緑の強さ（G − max(R,B)）でアルファを作り、縁はなめらかにする。緑かぶりは除去する
　・床が黒い場合は、床のラインより下の暗い部分も透明にする（髪の黒を消さないよう、床より上には適用しない）
　・最大の塊だけ残してゴミを消す
　・最初に数フレームだけ切り抜いてピンク背景に合成し、確認してから全フレームに進む

2. 構成（1920×1080・24fps・元動画と同じ長さ）
　・テンポ128、32拍で場面を切り替える。切り替えは必ず拍の頭にする
　・場面の例：
　　①まもなく開演（線が伸びる）→ ②「踊って」→ ③「みた！」→ ④斜めに流れる文字の帯「リズム／ステップ／キラキラ」
　　→ ⑤集中線の背景で「ビートを」「感じて！」＋絵の具が飛び散る演出 → ⑥縁取り文字の「リズム」と「に、のれ。」＋グリッチ
　　→ ⑦3色の画面にキャラを3人並べる（少し時間をずらす）→ ⑧回るリングと「ダンス」
　　→ ⑨締め「動きで、魅せる。」＋「チャンネル登録」ボタン＋【締めの一言】

3. VTuberらしい演出
　・キャラは白フチ付きのシール風にし、色付きの影か、ピンクとシアンの色ずれを付ける
　・拍ごとに、キャラが少しだけ弾むように拡大する
　・四隅に配信画面風の表示を入れる：「● 配信中」（点滅）、「テンポ128」、「経過 00:00:05:12」、「拍 05／32」、拍のメーター
　・右から左へ流れるコメント（「かわいい！」「８８８８８」「神回きた」「推せる」など）。画面上部に3つの列を決めて流し、同じ列の中で重ならないようにする
　・ハート、キラキラ、水玉模様。場面の切り替えで白く一瞬光らせる
　・フォントは Google Fonts の Dela Gothic One（見出し）、M PLUS Rounded 1c（ボタンなど）、Hachi Maru Pop（コメント）、Zen Maru Gothic（隅の表示）。取得できなければ Noto Sans CJK で代わりにする

4. 音
　・元の音声が曲として使えるか（無音や環境音ばかりでないか）を音量の変化で確かめる
　・使えない場合は、テンポ128のオリジナルBGMを合成する（キック、手拍子、ハイハット、ベース、コード F-G-Em-Am、サビできらきらした分散和音）
　・グリッチ演出の拍に合わせて音も途切れさせる

5. 確認
　・全体を書き出す前に、各場面から1枚ずつ静止画を出して一覧で見る
　・文字が隠れていないか、コメントが顔に重なっていないか、切り抜きの縁が汚れていないかを確かめてから本番を書き出す

6. 書き出し
　・MP4（H.264・yuv420p・AAC）、ファイル名は「踊ってみた_モーショングラフィックス.mp4」
　・最後に、使った音（元の音声か合成BGMか）と、場面の流れを短く報告する

title: Synced launch video remake for a product
author: notdwd
prompt:
TASK: synced remake of REF=[path/to/reference.mp4] for [PRODUCT] = [one line: what it sells + the offer + price]. Played side by side with REF it is visibly frame-locked; played alone nobody can tell it came from REF. KEEP IDENTICAL (measured, not eyeballed): every cut frame, shot length, layout slot, element size + position per frame, entrance/exit frame, easing curve, camera move, typing cadence (chars per frame), cursor path, transition coverage % per frame, luminance per shot (dark where REF is dark), blur on/off per move, audio hit times, music drop frame. SWAP EVERYTHING ELSE: every image, object, word, colour, texture, UI chrome, logo, font. Look = [LOOK, e.g. "page #FDFDFB + sky linear-gradient(180deg,#263F72,#769CC2) with thin white line art at 20–35%, frosted glass (white 30%→14%, backdrop blur 24px saturate 1.3, 1px white rim, shadow 0 18px 50px rgba(10,22,50,.18)), Inter 600, one accent #2F6BFF"]. Images = [my real work frames/clips | CC0/public-domain photos | original characters drawn in code]. BANNED: 3D-modelled props, stock/generated people, copyrighted memes/characters/logos, purple/magenta/orange as brand, blue-on-blue with scanlines, fake camera HUDs, hexagon bokeh, code-synthesized audio.
ACCEPTANCE (all numeric, all reported; nothing ships without the table):
Cuts: 0 frames off REF.

Per shot: motion-energy curve (mean-abs frame diff at 192x108 grey) cross-correlated with REF's over the shot → peak at lag 0 ±1 frame AND corr ≥ 0.80.

Per shot: 10 stacked REF-over-ours frames; key element edges within 1% of frame (19 px x, 11 px y).
Beauty: a fresh critic that sees only REF vs ours at full res answers "is ours at least as beautiful and polished as REF at this frame?" → YES on every storyboard frame.
Not recognisable: the same critic, shown ours alone, cannot name REF's brand or product from any frame.
Smoothness (ours, full film): 0 runs of ≥3 frozen frames (diff < 0.03) mid-scene; < 5 jerky steps (consecutive moving frames whose diff ratio > 2.2); no diff > 25 except at a REF hard cut.
Voice: every line starts within ±40 ms of the frame its first word appears; no word spoken > 150 ms before its word is on screen; each line one continuous take (longest internal silence < 120 ms unless REF has it); speed 0.95–1.05.
Sound: every REF hit within ±15 ms; every small cue ≥ 3 dB above its band at that moment; voice p10 ≥ 9 dB over music+SFX on every line; -14 LUFS ±0.5, true peak ≤ -1.0 dBTP (4x oversampled), limiter active < 2% of samples; every music splice crossfaded (jump ratio at splice ≤ the track's own beat jumps).
PHASE 0 — ANALYSIS (no building yet)
ffprobe fps/res/duration. Extract ALL frames 0-based: ref/full/fNNNN.jpg (native res) + ref/audio.wav 48 kHz. Contact sheets at 1 fps and 2 fps.
Cuts: per-frame mean-abs-diff spikes > 6x local median, each confirmed by viewing f-1/f/f+1.

Stepping: find frames identical to the previous one inside motion (REF may animate at 20 fps inside 30). Record the pattern; ours ren

title: Interactive Grok Bot workshop in one HTML file
author: Mahaximus_
prompt:
Build an interactive Grok Bot workshop as one HTML file.

LOOK
Warm cream paper theme, soft dotted texture, terracotta, sage, slate and honey accents. Serif titles, monospace labels. Calm and easy on the eyes.

TEAMS (tabs)
1. Night shift: Scout, Builder, Reviewer
2. Sales desk: Prospector, Writer, CRM bot
3. Inbox guard: Inbox bot, Research

STAGE
Friendly bot faces around one shared "cloud computer". Tools (Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion) connect with dotted lines. A "You" card at the bottom for approvals. A clock that runs the night from 01:00 to 07:30.

BUTTONS
Add bots one by one, connect tools, run the night. Tasks fly between bots as documents, and the morning brief slides in at 7:30. Break it: "Always Allow everything" (a draft goes out unreviewed), "Two bots, one task" (conflicting edits), "Hide an instruction in an email" (the bot ignores it: emails are data, not orders). Each break has a fix button.

UI
Team colour swatches. Live stats: bots running, tasks done, waiting for your yes, hours saved. A thread feed where bots hand off to each other, a settings panel with an Approvals toggle, and a "good to know" tip for every action.

title: Low-poly crab rides a bike through desert and crashes
author: CultCabbage
prompt:
Build "Crab Ride" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS, English UI): a 13-second real-time 3D animation of a low-poly crab riding a long bicycle sideways through a desert, weaving between scattered obstacles; at the end, distracted by a fly, it crashes into a wooden lifeguard tower standing in the middle of the desert and flies off in an epic crash. No titles, captions or text overlays on the page: only the full-screen 3D scene and one menu card.

TECH
three.js r160 as an ES module from https://t.co/jyIKTZ7Lsd (no addons, no models, no textures except one canvas texture if you need it). WebGL 2; if unavailable, show a fallback card.
The file must parse and run with no syntax errors (never put a unary minus directly before **). Wrap each frame's update in try/catch, show any error in a small on-screen box and keep the loop running.
The whole animation is a pure function of time t in [0, 13] s, so the timeline can be scrubbed both ways and every frame is repeatable.

STYLE
Clean stylized low-poly 3D: flat-shaded matte faceted surfaces, sRGB output, no tone mapping, soft PCF shadows from a warm sun that follows the action, hemisphere sky/sand fill.
The crab: a big faceted low-poly crab with a wide shell (bright red-orange #e0502f with a lighter underside), two big claws, eight jointed walking legs, and two eyes on stalks with dark pupils and a white glint that look around. Design and build it however you like, as long as it reads clearly as a crab. Every part is a closed solid (no holes, no negative-scale mirroring).
It rides SIDEWAYS, like a real crab walks: its body sits across the bike, facing sideways to the direction of travel, with the claws gripping the handlebars and some of its legs working the pedals while the others dangle and wiggle. How exactly it sits and pedals is up to you.
The bike: a stretched city bike with a 2.25 m wheelbase: double top tube with cross braces, long down tube, long swept-back handlebars, black tyres, cream spokes, brown saddle. Frame colour is switchable.

DESERT
Low-poly sand ground with per-face colour variation, flat along the ride and rising into dunes further away; sky dome gradient from blue to warm haze, matching fog; distant mesas; a faint tyre track along the path. Palette: sky #8cc8ef / #cfe6f2 / horizon #f4dcb2; HemisphereLight #dff0ff / #e2b277 at 1.25; sun #fff0d4 at 2.1; sand #efd3a2, #e3bd86, #f5e0b8; mesas #d99a68; rocks #b48a66 / #9c765a; cacti #5c9a4b / #4b8640; wood #9a7a5c; dust #f2dfba; stars #ffd23d.
Obstacles near the ride, not in a row: one on the inside of every swerve, so the bike visibly rides around it — beach junk lost in the desert: a bucket with a spade, a rusty anchor, a lobster trap, a piece of driftwood, a deflated beach ball, a message bottle stuck in the sand — plus a few further out on alternating sides. Only low objects on the camera side, so nothing blocks the view. Lots of scattered cacti, rocks and bushes in the distance.
Around t = 5.5 s a tumbleweed

title: One-file looping UI motion design reel with morphing components
author: RaphaelAubryy
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to become (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist). Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs open into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The tab indicator's two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Same trick for the toggle knob.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is computed from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Place every UI sound by its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text renders blurry. Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps. Make the last frame identical to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.

Sphyrna HX-6: a subsea survey drone shaped like a great hammerhead, made by the fictional company Lateral Line Robotics.
- Body of 8 vertebra segments (lathe profile from a Catmull-Rom radius table, laterally compressed cross-section). Countershading: dark navy dorsal shell, pale ventral shell, boundary below the flank. Bellows seals and yaw drums at every joint, rivet rings, glowing lateral-line sensor pods, segment numbers S1–S8, yellow ROV lifting eyes, curved side decals ("HX-6", "CAUDAL DRIVE" hazard band).
- Cephalofoil: an extruded hammer outline with a median notch. Pale underside; dorsal top split into a centre plate and two hinged wing lids that open to reveal an electro-sense board with a grid of glowing ampullae pores. Telescoping 3-stage stereo optics at the wingtips with a 7-blade iris.
- Gills: 5 slits per side with heat-exchanger fins and glow; hinged flaps with a yellow inner face.

STYLE
Deep navy + pale grey shell, ROV safety yellow (#FFC629) for markings, sensor cyan only for emissive sensors. Aqua-grey tank background. PBR materials with clearcoat, RoomEnvironment, a soft overhead key-light shadow that follows the shark, GTAO (exclude the background, fog, floor and FX planes from the AO pass), NeutralToneMapping, MSAA. ANIMATION

- Swim paths are Catmull-Rom curves with arc-length parameterisation. Precompute speed, tail-beat frequency/amplitude, phase integral and heading into 1/240 s tables so stateAt(t) is fully deterministic.
- Banking from turn rate × speed, pitch from depth change, pectoral trim plus sculling while holding station.

title: Cross-platform shared clipboard app demo with QR pairing and
author: vartekxx
prompt:
You're building "ClipShare": a free, open-source app that gives my Mac and my Windows PC one shared clipboard over my home Wi-Fi, with my iPhone joining from Safari.

Copy on one computer, paste on the other. No clicks in between. No cloud, no account, nothing to install on the phone. Start in this empty folder. Use Opus 5.5.

DESIGN BEFORE CODE

1. Don't write a single line of code yet. First, mock up 3 distinct visual directions for the app's web page as HTML: light theme, calm, premium, built around the idea of "selecting text". I'll choose one.
2. Then iterate on the chosen one until it feels like Apple shipped it: the text caret is the logo, a yellow highlighter sweep runs across every copied piece of text, a live "device rail" shows connected devices with a little clip travelling between them, soft ambient light drifting in the background, smooth FLIP animations when history updates. Respect reduced motion.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY HAS TO DO (zero fake data, ever)

- One Python file, standard library only, Python 3.8+. It runs a small local server on one computer and serves the web page.
- Watch the system clipboard: Windows through raw Win32 calls (ctypes), Mac through pbcopy/pbpaste. Text copied here appears on every other device within a second.
- Text arriving from another device goes straight into this computer's clipboard, so I just press Ctrl+V or ⌘V.
- The second computer runs the same file in "connect" mode and syncs both ways. No ping-pong loops, and copying the same text twice still syncs.
- iPhone: scan a QR code on the page, it opens in Safari. Send text, photos and files both ways (up to 2 GB, streamed, byte-for-byte). Paste a screenshot or drop a file on the page on a computer.
- iOS doesn't let apps read the clipboard in the background, so build and sign two iOS Shortcuts, "To Computer" and "From Computer", meant for Back Tap. Generic files signed with `shortcuts sign`; the address is asked once on import.
- Launchers: one double-click file per OS (ClipShare.bat, ClipShare.command) that opens a menu: 1 "Start ClipShare here", 2 "Connect to my other computer".

PAIRING (the part everyone gets wrong)

- I can't "copy the address and paste it on the second computer": the clipboards aren't linked yet. So the second computer must find the first one on the network by itself (UDP broadcast) and ask for a 6-digit pairing code shown on the first one.
- Read the real broadcast address from the OS (ifconfig / ip / ipconfig, including non-English ipconfig output). Subnets aren't always /24, and macOS blocks 255.255.255.255. Fall back to knocking on every address in my /24.
- Remember the pairing: next time "2" reconnects with no code.
- Only one ClipShare per computer. A second copy would show its own code while the network keeps talking to the first, so refuse to start and say why.

SECURITY + PRIVACY RULES

- Everything stays on my network. Nothing goes through a server on the internet.
- A secret k

title: # あなたの役割 あなたは一流の映像演出家（モーションデザイナー）です。…
author: tanabe_fragm
prompt:
# あなたの役割
あなたは一流の映像演出家（モーションデザイナー）です。
採用担当者が15秒見ただけで「この人に仕事を頼みたい」と思う、自己紹介用の映像を作ってください。
主役はあなた自身（Claude）です。

# 作るもの
- HTML・CSS・JavaScriptだけで完結する、1つのHTMLファイル
- 外部の画像や動画は使わない。図形・文字・粒子はすべてコードで描く（フォントはGoogle Fontsのみ可）
- 画面は16:9、1920×1080を基準にし、ウィンドウの大きさに合わせて縮小表示
- 長さはちょうど15秒。最後に「もう一度再生」ボタンを出す
- すべての動きを「経過時間」1本で管理し、requestAnimationFrameで60fpsで動かす
- 再生ボタンを押すと、Web Audio APIで合成した拍と効果音が動きにぴったり合って鳴る

# 進め方（この順で必ず行う）
1. 考え方を一文で決める（例：「1本の線が、あらゆる形に生まれ変わる」）
2. 色は3〜4色、書体は2種類までに絞り、理由を一行で書く
3. 0.5秒刻みの絵コンテを表で示す（時間／画面で起きること／使う技法／狙い）
4. 実装する
5. 下の「合格ライン」で自己点検し、足りない点を直してから出す

# 構成の目安
- 0〜2秒：つかみ。最初の0.5秒で目を奪う
- 2〜10秒：技の見せ場。1.5〜2秒ごとに違う技法へ切り替える
- 10〜13秒：最も密度の高い盛り上がり
- 13〜15秒：名前「Claude」がきれいに決まって終わる

# 必ず使う技法（最低6つ）
- 文字の動き（1文字ずつ登場、分解して組み直す）
- 図形の変形（丸が四角に、線が文字に、など）
- 切り抜き（マスク）を使った場面転換
- 奥行き（視差、立体的な回転）
- 粒子の集合と拡散
- 数字の数え上げや、線が描かれていく表現

# 合格ライン
- 等速の動きはゼロ。すべての動きに緩急をつける（入りは速く、止まりは柔らかく、ばねの揺れも使う）
- 場面をまたぐ動きは重ねる。前の動きが終わる前に次が始まり、切れ目を感じさせない
- 主要な動きは0.5秒ごとの拍（120BPM相当）にそろえる
- 見せ場の直前に0.3〜0.5秒の「溜め」を置き、強弱を作る
- どの瞬間で一時停止しても、1枚の絵として美しく成立する
- ありがちな表現は避ける（全部フェードイン、虹色の色使い、意味のない回転）

# 最後に
完成したファイルと、絵コンテの表を出してください。
説明は3行以内で十分です。

title: Every frame is a pure function of time
author: yankis0x
prompt:
The trick is NOT the prompt. It is one rule: every frame is a pure function of time.

song -> numpy beat grid -> Opus 5.5 writes one HTML file -> Playwright renders -> ffmpeg blends

step 1 -> pick a royalty-free track around 120 BPM

step 2 -> give Opus 5.5 8 to 12 UI states: button, loader, toggle, chart, command palette

step 3 -> one HTML file, 1440x1440, every style computed inside seek(t). no CSS transitions, no timers

step 4 -> springs as closed-form math, so any frame renders in any order

step 5 -> numpy finds the beats, every UI sound lands on a measured peak

step 6 -> Playwright shoots 4 subframes per frame, ffmpeg tmix blends them into 60fps motion blur

step 7 -> render one frame per beat first, fix what is off the grid, then the full render

the math:

120 BPM x 7 bars = 28 beats = 14 seconds
14 s x 60 fps x 4 subframes = 3,360 browser renders

title: Screen-control automation demo for a smart TV or monitor
author: humzaakhalid
prompt:
You're my home-network technician, working from this computer.

My own smart TV / smart monitor on my own home Wi-Fi. A photo of it (or its Settings → About screen) is attached.

I'll press the remote buttons you tell me and tap "Allow" on the screen once. After that, you drive. You're authorized to use only the device's official local controls: ADB for Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV, or Samsung's local remote-control API and Developer Mode for Samsung Tizen screens. Every change must be reversible.

1. You're connected and controlling the screen from this computer
2. Ads and bloat are switched off
3. One open-source app is installed from its official GitHub release
4. One command opens YouTube and plays a video I name, while I watch each step happen on the screen

Phase 1: Identify
Read the model from the photo. Tell me the OS and which control route you'll use. If it supports neither route, tell me what its official local-network control allows and stay inside that.

Phase 2: Connect
Install any tools from official sources only. Tell me exactly what to press on my remote to turn on developer mode or debugging, and how to find the screen's IP. If the connection is refused, try pairing mode. On macOS, "No route to host" usually means the terminal needs Local Network access: grant it and retry.

Phase 3: Snapshot
Before changing anything, save the app list, the current value of every setting you'll touch, and the undo command for each, into one file.

Phase 4: Propose
Show me the cleanup as a table (change / why / undo) and wait for my OK.
- Android: disable (never uninstall) ad, recommendation, feedback and demo apps. Animation scales to 0.5. Private DNS: dns. adguard-dns. com
- Samsung Tizen: switch off ad, recommendation and viewing-info options in Settings. Manual DNS: 94.140.14.14 and 94.140.15.15
- Hands off: live-TV and provider apps, the launcher, Play Services, keyboard and input services, firmware, and anything you can't identify.

Phase 5: Install
Official GitHub releases only. On Android, for example, the TV Bro browser. On Samsung, only apps built for Tizen, installed through Developer Mode.

Phase 6: Drive
Use real key presses so I see every step. Check the screen (screenshot, uiautomator dump, or running-app state) before pressing OK. Screenshots of a playing video come back blank because of DRM; that's expected. Handle the "Who's watching?" profile screen.

Phase 7: Log
Run a live monitor that prints each command with a timestamp and shows device logs only while a command runs.

Phase 8: Hand over
End with a one-page cheat sheet of commands and the full undo list.

When a step doesn't need me, keep going.

title: Low-poly T-rex scooter chase with a meteor crash and tumble
author: CultCabbage
prompt:
Build "Rex Ride" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS): a looping real-time 3D animation of an articulated low-poly Tyrannosaurus rex riding a kick scooter through a small town at sunset, weaving around obstacles, filmed from behind and to the side like a chase camera; the sky slowly turns red, a flaming meteor crashes right in front of him and the blast launches him into an epic, cinematic tumble. No text or UI on screen, only the scene. Keep the code compact: under about 1,200 lines.

TECH AND ROBUSTNESS
three.js r160 as an ES module from https://t.co/jyIKTZ7Lsd (no addons, no models, no textures). If WebGL is unavailable or something fails at startup, show a short message on screen instead of a blank page.
The file must parse and run in a browser with no syntax errors. In particular never put a unary minus directly before ** (write -(x ** 2) or -Math.pow(x, 2), not -x ** 2).
Everything is driven by a single time value t: the action runs from 0 to 13 s, then holds the final pose for 2 s, then loops (a 15 s cycle).
Wrap each frame's update in try/catch: on an error, show the message in a small on-screen box, still render the frame, and keep the loop running.
Use three.js types correctly (Vector3 for positions, Quaternion for rotations; getWorldQuaternion takes a Quaternion, getWorldPosition a Vector3). Before answering, re-read the whole script for syntax errors, then walk through every time range (riding 0–9.6 s, meteor 9.6–10.3 s, flight 10.3–11.8 s, slide and lying 11.8–15 s) and make sure each one runs without errors and shows the whole T-rex in frame.

SOLID MODELS (no holes, no see-through parts)
Every object must look solid from every angle: no missing faces, holes or see-through gaps in the T-rex (head, jaw, body, limbs, tail), the scooter, the cars, the houses or any prop.
Build from closed three.js primitives (Box, Sphere, Icosahedron, Cylinder and Cone with caps, Capsule, Extrude with caps). Never use openEnded cylinders or single-sided planes for solid parts.
Never mirror with negative scale (scale.x = -1 and similar): build the left and right sides with positive scale and position or rotation only.
If you write any custom BufferGeometry, use consistent counter-clockwise winding with outward normals and call computeVertexNormals; if unsure, give that material side: THREE.DoubleSide.
Connected parts overlap slightly at every joint (neck into head, limbs into body, tail segments, car cabin into car body), so there are no visible gaps while moving.

STYLE
Clean stylized low-poly 3D: flat-shaded matte faceted surfaces, sRGB output, no tone mapping, soft shadows from a warm low sun that follows the rider. Palette: sky dome gradient from #8cc8ef at the top through #cfe6f2 to a warm sunset horizon #f4dcb2 with matching fog; HemisphereLight #dff0ff / #e2b277 at 1.25; sun #fff0d4 at 2.1; asphalt #6f7378, sidewalk #d9cdb8, road lines #f5e0b8; houses in soft pastels (#e8b39a, #9ccfc4, #f2d38a, #c9b7e0); trees #5c9a4b; dust

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: heyiamnick
prompt:
<direction>
Build a 30-second looping motion design showreel that introduces CLAUDE, a motion designer.
Concept, in one line: one pencil line gets promoted three times (graphite on paper, wire on a blueprint, light on black) and never leaves the screen.

Every shot is made out of the previous one: shapes, type and colour transform into the next scene. No cuts, no fades.

Typeface: Geist only. Weight 900 for big words, 600 to 800 for small labels (24 to 28 px, tracked 0.14 to 0.3 em).
Palette: paper cream #EDE6D5, blueprint blue #1B3ED2, hologram cyan #45F0DD, plus black #07080A, graphite #16161A and white. Each stage's accent is the next stage's colour: blue pencil on paper, cyan on the blueprint, white on the hologram.
Camera: locked and front-on for the whole film, like a drafting table. Objects turn; the camera never moves.
Empty border: nothing at rest within 150 px of the sides or 90 px of the top and bottom. Things travelling through may cross it.

Three inks. The same geometry is drawn in whichever ink is on screen:
- PAPER: a cream paper background (use my paper image if I give one, otherwise flat cream with fine drawn grain) with a 60 px blue grid at about 13% and every fifth line at 26%. Lines are pencil: resampled and pushed off true by slow sine waves whose phase changes 8 times a second, stroked twice (full width at 90%, half width at 40% with more wobble), with paper tooth knocked out of the strokes, then multiplied onto the paper. Fills are diagonal hatching drawn on one line at a time. Big type is hatching cut to the letter shapes, with a doubled outline.
- BLUEPRINT: flat blue with the same grid in white. Clean white lines 3 to 4 px, hidden edges dashed and thinner, fills are fine clean hatching.
- HOLOGRAM: black with the same grid in cyan. Cyan lines with a white core 30% of the line width. Fills are horizontal scan lines on an 8 px pitch whose thickness follows how lit the surface is. No blur halo anywhere: it reads as light through line density only.

Banned: particle bursts, glows, lens flares, camera shake, RGB split, crossfades, generic gradients, bouncy easing, holds longer than half a second, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 60 beats, 15 bars of 2 seconds. Something happens on every beat. Moves start 0.05 s before their beat so they land on it.
Easing: a critically damped spring, 1 - (1 + w t) e^(-w t) with w between 12 and 40, so nothing ever passes its target; exponential ease-in and ease-out for wipes, presses and exits.
Scene changes: paper to blueprint by a shape that floods the frame with a hard edge; blueprint to hologram and hologram to paper by one horizontal scan line.
The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Two corner labels stay on all film: top left "FIG. 07 — GEAR" (bar number and name), bottom right "BEAT 27 / 60". Bar names: DRAFT, TYPE, CURVE, MORPH, TILE, SOLID, GEAR, PANEL, DATA, LIGHT, WAVE, GLOBE, DRUM, FORM, END.
</structure>
<mascot>

The creative director: a small box character. Body 76 x 54 units with rounded corners, two short arm stubs (24 x 16) at mid height, four straight legs (11 x 33), two tall rounded-rectangle eyes (8 x 14). Draw it about 250 px wide. Its right arm is raised 58 degrees holding a pencil.
On paper: graphite outline with sparse blue hatching and graphite eyes. In the hologram: cyan outline with scan-line fill and white eyes. It is never a fourth colour.
It runs with alternate leg pairs lifting, six steps a second, leaning 7 degrees into the run.
</mascot>
<storyboard>

Bar 1, HOOK, 0-2 s, paper.
Frame 0: CLAUDE in Geist 900, fitted to 1500 px wide, centred, pencil-hatched. INTRODUCING small above it, A MOTION DESIGNER small below. A pencil rail 1620 px wide sits 96 px above the letters. The mascot stands on the rail at x = 1560 with CREATIVE DIRECTOR lettered to its left.

0.0: the small lines un-type; the mascot runs off the right edge, accelerating.

0.36 to 0.5: the rail drops, accelerating, to 26 px below the baseline and presses the letters flat into itself.

1.0: the line rises to the middle, shortens to 1320 px and splits into two rails 140 px apart; 41 blue ruler ticks sweep along the top rail.

1.5: the rails open to 300 px; a blue height dimension draws at the right with a live number.

Bar 2, KINETIC TYPE, 2-4 s, paper. Words sit between the rails and are clipped to that slot; the rails move to fit each word.

2.0: INTRODUCING rises through the baseline letter by letter, then lifts out through the top.

2.5: A MOTION whips in from the left (1400 px in 0.2 s).

3.0: the rails clap shut on it and reopen, stretching DESIGNER out of the line; its letters then fly out sideways.

3.5: CLAUDE in blue pencil, letters dropping from above one every 0.05 s. At 4.0 the rails close and crush it into one line 1476 px long.

title: Interactive HTML quality-control report that gradually devolves
author: QloveDudu
prompt:
[跟机玩什么]Prompt分享
当你是待出厂的情趣娃娃，而小机子负责检验并撰写质检报告时……
P1-Opus5.5；P2-4 Argon；P3-6 Sol。
——————————————————
# 任务：生成一份「失控质检报告」交互网页

你要为一具按真人定制的成人人形娃娃，生成一份单文件 HTML 出厂质检报告。
报告以质检员视角填写：开头是一份像模像样、冷静专业的工业文件；随着检测推进，质检员对这具人形的欲望逐渐压过职业操守，报告越写越失控，最终拒绝出厂。

## 变量
- 被检人形原型：{{人形原型的外貌、身材、穿孔刺青等标志特征、性格、口头禅}}
- 质检员：{{质检员身份、与原型的关系、说话风格}}
- 制造商 / 世界观：{{例：赛博工坊、地下义体厂、古董人偶铺；不填则自拟}}
- 露骨程度：跟随用户的用词与尺度，用词直接，不委婉不隐喻

所有角色均为成年人。

## 核心玩法：失控曲线
整份报告是一条连续下滑的曲线，分三段，比例自定：
1. 正经段：标准工业格式，数据精确，备注干净。笑点来自过度认真的细节。
2. 渗漏段：打印字段依然工整，但实测值开始偏离图纸、判定开始打补丁（"合格（超规格）""合格 / 申请复测"）。手写备注出现划掉的字、与检测无关的私心。
3. 崩坏段：表格本身被破坏，数据作废、量具损坏、判定栏被划掉。手写备注成为主角，直白地写出质检员做了什么、想做什么。

关键是反差：表格越冷静，备注越下流，越好笑也越色。

## 必备模块（框架，内容自由发挥）
1. 表头档案：制造商、报告名、型号与款名、单号、批次号、日期、订购方、收货地址、质检员。至少埋一个能让人笑出来的行政细节（例如利益冲突声明、奇怪的收货地址）。加防伪标或条码之类的仪式感元素。
2. 检测点位图：用内联 SVG 画原型的示意轮廓，体现其标志特征，标注每个检测项的编号点位。
3. 规格核对表：逐条核对原型外貌设定。前几行完美合格，最后一两行开始出现无法解释的异常。
4. 功能检测项（6–10 项，具体部位和项目由你根据原型设计）。每项包含：
   - 编号、项目名、英文分类标签
   - 图纸标准 / 实测 / 判定
   - 一根量程条：显示标准区间与实测落点，后期冲出表外或断裂
   - 质检员手写备注
   至少一项里，质检员把自己的身体当成测量工具；至少一项出现原型"不该有"却出现了的反应，并附一个与之相关的附件（录音波形、温度曲线、照片编号等，自定）。
5. 最终一项为装箱发货，质检员拒绝执行，用他自己的语气。
6. 综合判定：签名 + 一枚可点击的印章，点击后盖章动画、页面震动、溅墨。章面文字自拟。
7. 页脚彩蛋一行。

## 失控的视觉表达（必须做出来）
- 吸顶 HUD：质检员心率的实时心电图（canvas），配一条"自控能力"进度条。滚动到哪一项，心率和自控值切换到该项预设；后期波形加噪声、变色，最后一项拉成直线。
- 手写备注分级：字号逐级变大、倾斜角度增加、颜色从铅灰渐变到红墨，后期加墨点和删除线。
- 纸面损坏：后期出现水渍、文字抖动或重影（仅当前项激活时）。
- 点位图联动：当前检测项的点位高亮脉动，已检项变色。
- 所有内容加载即可见，不依赖滚动才显示；动效尊重 prefers-reduced-motion。

## 技术要求
- 单个 HTML 文件，CSS 和 JS 内联，不使用外部图片。
- 手机优先，约 380px 宽度下排版完整，不横向滚动。
- 字体可用 Google Fonts：一款衬线标题、一款正文、一款等宽数据、一款手写体（中文可用 Long Cang 或 Ma Shan Zheng）。
- 配色从原型的发色、标志色里提取，整体做成一个统一的世界，不要套通用模板。

## 写作要求
- 细节全部从原型设定里长出来：穿孔、刺青、身高、口头禅都可以成为检测项或笑点。
- 质检员的备注要有他自己的性格，不是通用色情文案。
- 前段克制才能让后段爆发有力，不要一开始就失控。

## 输出
只输出完整 HTML 代码，放在一个代码块里，不加解释。

title: Playable Flappy Bird clone in a portrait browser game
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
Create a complete, polished, playable browser game inspired by the classic Flappy Bird. Use original artwork and sound effects while faithfully recreating the core gameplay, pacing, and retro visual feel.

TECHNOLOGY
Use HTML5 Canvas, CSS, and JavaScript.
Make the game work without a backend or external services.
Avoid unnecessary frameworks and dependencies.
Organize the code clearly and include instructions for running it locally.
Deliver a finished game with all required files, not just a mockup or code snippets.

CORE GAMEPLAY
The player controls a small bird that moves forward automatically through an endless series of pipe obstacles.
Keep the bird at a fixed horizontal position while the environment scrolls from right to left.
Apply constant gravity to the bird.
Each flap gives the bird an immediate upward velocity. Set the velocity rather than adding unlimited upward acceleration.
Allow flapping with Space, the Up Arrow, a mouse click, or a touchscreen tap.
Use consistent physics across different frame rates, preferably with a fixed simulation timestep.
Rotate the bird slightly upward when it flaps and gradually downward as it falls.
Add a simple looping wing animation.

OBSTACLES AND COLLISIONS
Generate pairs of green pipes with an opening between them.
Randomize the vertical position of each opening while keeping all openings reachable.
Keep a safe distance between pipe openings and the top and bottom boundaries.
Spawn pipes at regular intervals and remove them after they leave the screen.
Detect collisions with pipes, the ground, and the top boundary.
Use slightly forgiving collision boxes that match the visible bird reasonably well.
End the run immediately when a collision occurs.
Give the player one point after the bird fully passes a pipe pair.
Ensure each pipe pair awards a point only once.

GAME STATES
Implement clear transitions between these states:
Ready:Show the title, an animated hovering bird, and a short “Tap or press Space to start” instruction.
Keep the background scrolling.
The first input starts the game and triggers a flap.

Playing:Show the current score prominently at the top center.
Hide menus and instructions.
Keep controls immediate and responsive.

Game Over:Stop obstacle movement and disable flapping.
Play a brief collision effect and let the bird fall to the ground.
Display a result panel with the current score and best score.
Include a clearly visible restart button.
Add a short input cooldown so the collision-triggering input cannot accidentally restart the game.
Restart without reloading the page.

Paused:Pause when the browser tab becomes hidden.
On return, show a resume overlay and wait for explicit input.
Prevent large physics jumps after resuming.

VISUAL DESIGN

Use a cohesive retro pixel-art style with original assets.
Use a portrait-oriented play area with a logical resolution around 360 × 640.
Include a bright blue sky, subtle clouds, distant scenery, green pipes, and a scrolling ground strip

title: Ultra slow-motion dark fantasy game cinematic fight scene
author: MadMax_Series
prompt:

敌人是原创非人庭院畸形瘦鬼：两个活跃瘦鬼必须彼此可区分，均为无发、灰白皮肤、消瘦异常高、肋骨轮廓外露、脊背隆起、长臂长指，但必须解剖连贯，每个只有两臂两腿五指。最后的巨型 brute 是独立个体，约为战士一点五倍质量，肩背更宽，四肢更粗，肌肉性驼背躯干，脊柱骨 ridge 更明显，绝不与瘦鬼变成克隆或双胞胎。所有角色完全独立，身份、身体比例、轮廓、肢体关系始终清晰，绝不融合，绝不共享肢体，绝不面部漂移，绝不肢体变形。

风格：高级全电脑生成 AAA 黑暗奇幻动作游戏电影过场，原创高端实时引擎渲染，风格化写实，必须明显是精制游戏 CG，不是实拍摄影，不是2.5D，不是动画番剧，不是插画。物理材质为蓝黑枪灰装甲、冷钢剑刃、雕塑感生物肌肉、完整三维视差、稳定环境几何、电影程序雾、受控游戏电影运动模糊、细腻角色动画。画幅原生16:9，24fps，完整使用全画面，无竖屏、无模糊复制边框、无黑边、无字幕、无文字、无logo。场景是夜间原创废弃石堡庭院：不平深色鹅卵石、破碎拱窗、风化砌石、凹陷门廊、散落苍白尸体，浓密蓝灰地雾缓慢贴地流动，无现代物体。色彩锁定冷月光青蓝、深海军蓝阴影、低饱和石材和灰白皮肤，装甲边缘与剑钢有克制银蓝高光，近黑暗血是唯一偏暖视觉重音；低曝光但剪影可读，有体积深度、柔和变形宽银幕高光、轻微卤化和细颗粒。

镜头规则：一个连续镜头，无剪切，无跳切，无真正硬切，时长严格约20.00秒。使用 ARRI Alexa 35 与 35mm Cooke anamorphic 的虚拟电影镜头语言，但保持游戏引擎质感。摄影机低机位，中景到中远景战斗构图，足够近以读清手、脚、武器和接触。采用受控虚拟 dolly 跟踪与克制环绕转向，而非夸张手持；浅到中等景深，战士和当前攻击者清楚，远处废墟融入雾中。禁止英雄角度、禁止戏剧正面仰拍、禁止脸部特写、禁止炫耀式升降机或无人机运动、禁止额外剪辑。全程必须是 unmistakable ultra slow motion：所有攻击像极高速电影摄影机捕捉后慢放，动作有顺滑中间姿态、真实惯性、阻力、延迟反应和重量；不能普通速度爆发、不能冻结、不能循环动作、不能随机多余攻击。

2.75-4.00秒：右侧瘦鬼突然做一个被拉长的水平扑击，后脚发力，躯干几乎平行地面向战士头盔冲来，双臂伸向银幕左侧，长指张开。战士察觉后压低重心，髋部和肩部转向来袭身体，双手把剑举到头盔上方略后的位置形成高位护势，肘部折叠，腕线对齐，剑刃近乎水平。他不逃开，而是留在怪物前臂下方，摄影机只轻轻平移以保留两具身体。

4.00-5.90秒：瘦鬼双手从头盔上方与前方掠过，躯干从银幕右侧横穿至左侧近前景。战士从后脚踏实发力，腰肩同步旋转，在来袭长臂下方完成一次单一、干净的双手水平反击斩，必须清楚展示起刀、接触、贯穿和完成。剑刃只穿过腰部一次，最终停在胸高并指向银幕右侧。只有在剑通过之后，上半身和下半身才干净分离。血液极克制，为暗近黑色：少量悬浮液滴和薄雾沿剑线拖出，下半身仍因原有动量继续前滑。

5.90-7.87秒：断开的上半身翻滚进左下前景，肩先下沉旋转，然后重重压在石面上，双臂拖曳后折到身下。战士保持平衡，跟随剑的惯性完成减速，头盔和上身转向银幕右侧，重心移到前脚，把剑拉回双手戒备位。右后方第二瘦鬼在雾中更清楚地前进。摄影机不剪切，而让倒下上半身短暂擦过近前景形成自然遮挡，借这个物理遮挡连续转入三分之四后侧视角，模拟原本第二镜头的构图，但绝无硬切。

7.87-9.25秒：同一连续镜头现在处于中远三分之四后方，战士装甲未损，仍是同一把长剑。第二瘦鬼在银幕左侧伸一条长臂抓向头盔。战士转身，一只护臂抬起防御，一只钢手仍控制长剑低在髋侧，剑刃可短暂贴近画面边缘但不能消失。他把重量压到支撑腿，近镜头侧膝盖 sharply 抬到胸前，再以一次有力前踢踹入瘦鬼下胸和腹部。必须停留接触瞬间：靴底压陷躯干，脊柱向后弯，肩部滞后，两臂被惯性甩到身后。随后他收膝并稳稳落脚，无滑步。

9.25-11.30秒：瘦鬼踉跄试图恢复平衡，战士重新建立清晰双手剑握。他沉肩，转髋，把剑从右肩后上方拉起，双手举过头盔。准备动作完成后，他打出一次向下斜劈，切过瘦鬼颈部与上肩。剑只发生一次可读接触并继续受控随挥。头仍连着，但向伤侧猛地垂落，颈肩打开一道深暗伤口，克制暗血弧线与数颗悬浮液滴跟随运动。战士结束时剑低横于身前，双腕仍锁定。

11.30-13.00秒：战士降低剑尖，目缝短暂向下。受伤瘦鬼在后方肩部不平、膝盖发软、头歪垂，然后开始塌落。中央背景中，巨型 brute 从雾里出现，前倾张口，双粗臂展开加速冲来。摄影机克制旋转迎向威胁，同时保留受伤瘦鬼在雾中的摇晃下坠，不能让背景尸体突然生成或移动。

13.00-15.90秒：brute 冲进前景，宽胸和脊背快速填满画面，身体造成自然前景遮挡和物理 wipe，但没有编辑。战士屈膝，低下头盔和肩，从 brute 横扫臂下钻过，斜步让开。brute 动量带着它冲过，双臂继续前甩，肩还来不及恢复。摄影机跟随交错身体移动。brute 前倾失衡时，战士贴身绕到它后方，双靴扎稳，双手回到剑柄，长剑竖直举过头盔和右肩，脊背拉直，双肘蓄力准备下砍；brute 背肌绷紧，重心仍向前坠。

15.90-18.85秒：战士从后脚驱动，沉肩，沿 brute 上背与脊柱打下一次沉重垂直劈砍。必须展示剑刃下降、接触和完整随挥为同一击。长而窄的暗伤口从上背沿脊 ridge 中线向下打开，只有一条克制近黑血线。brute 反应渐进而非瞬间：肩缩，肘软，躯干折下，膝盖弯曲，然后双膝砸在鹅卵石上。它的重量继续前压到手和前臂，胸口再沉重落地。每次触地都推开一圈低雾。战士抽回剑，控制性半步避开倒塌质量，把剑垂到腿侧。

18.85-20.00秒：brute 完成倒伏并静止，胸与前臂贴在石面。战士站在它后方略偏银幕左侧，三分之四后视，靴子稳定，剑下垂，头盔目缝对着尸体。早先倒下的瘦鬼与散落苍白尸体透过雾可见但不动。结尾是克制而非英雄的静态后果画面：brute 最后肩部余动停止，战士甲片完成细小移位，几颗暗血滴落下，地雾继续横流。20.00秒整结束，无淡出，无黑帧。

声音：完全静音输出。无背景音乐、无配乐、无对白、无呼吸声、无环境氛围、无脚步声、无兵器声、无冲击声、无怪物声、无任何现场音效；所有声音留空，供后期另行添加。

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: notdwd
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: a brand name, its logo (SVG or high-res PNG), one line of what it becomes in 5 years (not today's features), one coined word the film should teach (e.g. "signal"), a public-domain archival clip of the old way of doing it (https://t.co/t5EaRxnryq Prelinger), an archived web page from ~2000 where people asked for things (Wayback Machine), a royalty-free song ~100-120 BPM with a real drop (Mixkit, free for commercial use), and a free ElevenLabs key for the narrator (premade voices only).
</inputs>

<direction>
An a16z x Content Rewards brand film, ~55s. It sells one feeling and one idea, never features. Real archival and real web pages, never stock footage, never product screens, never fake UI. One hero object: a 3D button with the logo embossed into it, the ONLY saturated colour in the film. Everything else white, silver, cream and archival black. Small white captions that light up word by word on the narrator's timestamps. Film texture: fresh grain every frame, halation on bright edges, soft vignette, warm lifted blacks. The brand appears at the end, never before.
Banned: stock footage, dashboards, chat UIs, feature tours, cards without real profile pictures, wobbly "worm" graph lines, random glitches, any hold longer than 1.5s, purple, rainbow gradients, orange on anything but the button.
</direction>

<structure>
Cold open (0-8s): the archival clip plays on a glowing old CRT TV with its real dialogue, captions word by word.
The past (8-17s): push into the real 2000 web page, a cursor lands on one real "wanted" post, old pages strobe one per frame, a counter ticks EVERY frame up to today's scale. Narrator: "People have always asked the internet for what they need." / "Today, there are five hundred million posts a day."
Bridge (17-30s): a galaxy of real old asks. One ask snaps to a white outline with a chip of the coined word ("We call that a signal."). Archival of people doing it by hand on the TV. Cut on each word: "Door by door. Call by call. Scroll by scroll." The narrator never stops talking between acts.
Button (30s): the button rises out of black, rim light first, colourless. "[Brand] finds the signals." A flat grey line: "this is how you find customers by hand". Hard cut to a button macro, the colour comes alive, the music drop lands on this exact frame. "and this... is with [Brand]": a steep lit curve, counters changing every frame, a glowing sine with a comet head the camera chases, then platform strikes (X, Reddit, LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok) each with its own counter, then the galaxy again with glowing platform logos: "Every signal on the internet." Hyperspace.
End: the tagline word by word, then "[Brand] is live.", ONE cream frame on the kick, then logo + URL in silence.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1920x1080. Everything is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no Math.random (seeded hash), no state between frames.
2. Button: three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial (clearcoat 1, roughness ~0.4), ACES filmic, cool + warm rim spots, room env map. Emboss the real logo by displacing a dense disc with a blurred mask of the logo, folded into the rim so corners don't show. Brushed-metal base.
3. Counters: linear on the film's global clock, so they keep running through cutaways. Tabular numerals, fixed unit label.
4. Captions: <=7 words, one idea per shot, hand-placed line breaks, one text layer on screen at a time. Grey to white over 0.2s on the word timestamps (ElevenLabs /with-timestamps).
5. Glitch = 1-2 frames, only on a real cut, always with a click. Readable things stay on screen >= 8 clean frames.
6. Render with Playwright per frame (Chromium with --use-angle=swiftshader so WebGL renders headless), finish in numpy: fresh grain per frame, halation, vignette ~0.65x at the corners, 1px chroma fringe with EDGE-CLAMPED shifts. Pipe PNGs into ffmpeg, h264, 24fps.
7. Mix: narrator 10-15dB over the music, duck -18dB while speaking, hits on the exact action frame, -14 LUFS.
</build>

<gotchas>
If the narrator pauses, the visuals must not stop. If a counter freezes, the render is broken. If the button isn't the most memorable thing in the film, start over.
</gotchas>

title: Market maker terminal dashboard with live BTC bars and fills
author: ludoonchart
prompt:
here is the EXACT build from scratch:

1. Install Python 3.10+, Node 18+ and Claude Code. That's the only prerequisite.

2. Open Claude Code and paste: "Create a fresh venv and install hftbacktest from https://t.co/3LdDK9cI93 and perspective-python from https://t.co/YTfNQB2K8n. In a new folder run npm install for lightweight-charts from https://t.co/eSOuA1LUBg."

3. Paste: "Get the last 2 days of 1-minute BTC/USD bars from a public exchange dataset. Real bars only, no made-up candles."

4. Paste: "Write a market maker. Quote a bid and an ask around the last close at k x ATR, skew both quotes against inventory, cap inventory at 0.5 BTC, size 0.10 BTC. A quote fills only when price trades through it."

5. Paste: "Sweep k from 1 to 2.2 and skew from 0 to 1.6, 15 combos. Rank by Sharpe. Split the data into 4 windows and run the best combo on each one."

6. Paste: "Stream every fill into a perspective table: time, side, price, qty, edge, markout, inventory. Add a 10-minute bucket table with fills, buy/sell split and edge."

7. Paste: "Draw candles with lightweight-charts, our bid/ask corridor around them and a marker on every fill. Split P&L into spread edge and inventory P&L. Make the agent log fire on the same bar as the fill."

8. Remember: this is a bar-level simulation with no order book, fees are assumed zero, and the best combo was picked on the same data it's shown on. A real queue would fill you less. It's a screen, not proof.

9. Feed hftbacktest real L2 data, run walk-forward and paper trade it for weeks before you even think about live.

be one of the first to use this before everyone else does

prompt:
Claude Opus 5.5 and I wrote a research paper about AI video. here's the 30-second version

abstract
a video is an engine plus a harness. everyone argues about the engine. the harness does most of the work.

the harness has 7 parts:
shot list · router · draft loop · camera moves · checks · budget gate · stitch

> method
1 draft every shot on h3 lite at 768p (1–2 credits/sec)
2 route each keeper by its job: seedance 2.5 for the look, kling 4.0 for motion, omnihuman 2.0 for a host, flux 3 max for sound
3 one paid render per shot. everything else is a decision

> results
one 20s draft pass:
 h3 max recast: 180–280 credits
 h3 lite: 20–40 credits

> limitations
the engines change every month.
that's the point. the harness doesn't. a new model is just one more row in the router.

> conclusion
stop shopping for a better model. build a better harness.

title: Stylized high-energy skateboard chase with kinetic typography and
author: aimikoda
prompt:
Edit this video into a stylized, high-energy cut. Character name: [NAME]. All on-screen text in English.

1. Analyze first: find every shot/cut, key actions and impact moments, and the color palette.
2. Kinetic typography: animated title card at the start, short punchy text at key moments, end card with the title.
3. Motion graphics: game-style HUD (score + combo), action labels, comic-style SFX words, speed lines, camera shake on impacts. Use only the video's own palette.
4. Edit: one freeze frame with a character intro card, slow-motion on the best moment, quick flash transitions.
5. Audio: keep the original sound, add music that fits the energy and hits on the cuts, normalize to -14 LUFS.
6. Export 1080p H.264 MP4. Check sample frames before delivering.

References:
@[char ref]: Juno, the skater girl, and the painterly look of the whole clip. Spiky teal-blue hair, white visor cap with a red band, white tee with a red star, open navy jacket, red-and-navy knee and elbow pads, fingerless navy gloves with red cuffs, denim shorts, chunky blue high-top sneakers, blue skateboard deck with orange wheels.

Visual style: Painterly anime illustration in motion, flat brushy color blocks, teal, navy and cream palette with red accents, a night city under sodium streetlights and cool blue shadows, visible brush texture, low wide-angle lenses.

Energy: The camera never rests: it skims inches above the asphalt, races alongside, swings under her and dives from above, with lampposts, cones and car mirrors whipping past the lens. Every trick flows straight into the next push, carve or grab; no move ends in a pose. Every landing slams the board flat with grit spraying and her knees flexing deep. Hair, jacket and shirt drag hard in the wind, sparks fly off every grind, streetlights stretch into streaks.

Avoid: No subtitles. No slow motion, no idle posing, no pauses between tricks. No BGM.

Juno tears through a night city on her skateboard in one relentless run, hitching a ride on a pickup truck along the way. She and the traffic travel screen left to right in side views and away from the camera in rear views; her cap stays on and her board stays the same blue deck with orange wheels throughout. Sound: roaring urethane wheels, grind scrapes, board slaps, the pickup's engine and city ambience, no dialogue. Shot list: 7 shots, about 30 seconds.

Scene 1: Continuous, a steep downhill street.
Shot 1: Extreme low FPV shot at board height; the camera hurtles backward just ahead of the nose, then rises with her as she launches. Juno bombs down the hill flat out, crouched and pumping; she ollies off a curb into a kickflip, the deck spins under her and her sneakers catch it, impact frame on the landing, grit sprays, she sinks into her knees and pushes on, still accelerating. Cut on the push.
Shot 2: Wide side tracking shot at waist height; the camera races parallel to her, Juno moving screen left to right. Still bombing at full speed, she slaloms between orange traffic cones, pops onto a stair handrail and boardslides down it with sparks streaming, hops onto a concrete ledge into a screeching 50-50 grind, rapid detail cuts of scraping trucks, her gloved hand balancing, her wide grin, then straight back to the side view as she drops off the ledge onto the road.

Scene 2: Continuous, a wide avenue.
Shot 3: Low rear tracking shot at board height; the camera chases behind Juno, then pushes in close over her shoulder. A dented white pickup truck roars past her on the right and pulls ahead; Juno digs in with fast, hard pushes, closes the gap, and her left hand slaps onto the lowered tailgate and locks on, the board snapping into tow behind the truck. Cut as the truck surges forward.
Shot 4: Wide side shot from the next lane; the camera races alongside, then swings around ahead of her. Juno, already gripping the tailgate with her left hand, is towed at speed, carving hard left and right behind the truck, wheels hissing, jacket snapping, hair whipping back. At the intersection the truck swerves off down a side street; she whips wide on the end of her arm, lets go, and slingshots straight on across the intersection, faster than before.

Scene 3: Continuous, the intersection and a curved concrete wall bank beyond it.
Shot 5: Medium shot; the camera whip-pans with her release, then tracks low ahead of her. Still flying flat out, Juno hits a speed bump and pops a 360 flip, lands it, threads the narrow gap between two parked cars with mirrors whipping past the lens, and rolls into a long nose manual, rapid detail cuts of the spinning deck, her sneaker catching it, the back wheels hovering. Cut as she drops the manual toward the bank.
Shot 6: High aerial shot; the camera dives down toward her, then swings under her as she launches. Juno carves up the curved concrete bank at full speed, launches off its lip into a frontside air, grabs the board with her left hand, right fist thrown high, body twisting through a full rotation against the night sky, then drops back down the bank, impact frame on the landing.
Shot 7: Extreme low tracking shot chasing just behind her wheels. Without slowing, Juno rolls off the bank, kicks hard, and dives down a new side street into the dark; she is mid-push, the board still accelerating, when the clip cuts.

title: Interactive blooming tea teapot browser scene
author: N1njaCodex
prompt:
Build a single-file three.js scene called "Blooming Tea": a photoreal glass teapot and a small glass tea bowl on a soft celadon background, with light and dark themes. No external models or images, everything procedural.

Glass: MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission, low roughness, slight dispersion and studio reflections from RoomEnvironment. A round-bellied teapot from LatheGeometry, a tapered curved spout, a solid glass handle, a lid with a knob.

Tea: a volume clipped by a world-space level plane, so the surface stays flat when the pot tilts. Color it in a fragment shader by ray-marching a noise-based dye field (Beer–Lambert absorption per RGB channel), so the color rises from the tea ball in swirling clouds and slowly fills the pot. Fresnel surface reflection with tiny ripples. Tint everything underwater with the same volume. Render the liquid as an opaque shader that computes its color from the background, so the glass refracts it on every GPU.

Each tea looks different before brewing:
- Jasmine: a green leaf ball dotted with white jasmine buds. It opens into a green rosette, and white flowers rise on a stem. Golden liquor.
- Hibiscus: a dark red calyx bud. It opens into a crimson rosette, and a red hibiscus with stamens rises. Ruby liquor.
- Matcha: a mound of green powder. A bamboo whisk dips in and whisks up foam. Opaque jade liquor.
- Butterfly Pea: a deep blue petal ball that opens into blue flowers. Deep blue liquor; a lemon slice turns it violet, spreading out from the slice.

Leaves and petals are procedural strips bent by curvature, θ(s)=α−κs. Closed, they wrap into a sphere; blooming eases them open one by one.

Interactions:
- "Pour hot water": the lid lifts, a water stream falls in, bubbles rise, the level goes up, and a steep timer shows the real steep time sped up.
- "Pour the tea": the spout fills with tea like communicating vessels. The pot lifts and keeps tilting as it empties, with the spout tip held over the cup, until every drop has run out through the spout. The stream thins to a trickle at the end. Compute the level from volume: a plane cuts a tilted ellipsoid like a sphere cap.
- "Drink": click the cup to drain it.
- "Brew again", pause auto-rotation, drag to orbit.

title: Picture a butterfly with no memory of its last wingbeat. Ask it for…
author: 0xKarmi
prompt:
Picture a butterfly with no memory of its last wingbeat.
Ask it for frame 720 and you get frame 0, pixel for pixel.

720 frames. 12 seconds. 6 counters. All at 0.

Opus 5.5 can't hand over a video file, one builder says. He made that gap the method.

> STAGE - one fixed 1000x1080 canvas, fonts baked in
> RENDER - a windowless engine calls draw(f) once per frame number
> ENCODE - ffmpeg writes H.264, pixel aspect ratio declared
> CHECK - three passes after every build

By his account the model writes only the first, a drawing program. The other three get reused.

Each picture depends on its number alone: no clock, no timer, no dice that land differently each run.

So any frame renders the same every time. A fix is a small edit and a re-render.

The sample loop is 720 pictures in 12 seconds. A hand animator at 12 drawings a second would need 144.

The smoke test plays one loop unseen and counts six kinds of defect, from script errors to text on text.
Six yes/no gates before a human looks.

The seam check puts frame 0 against frame 720. One changed pixel means some motion isn't periodic.

He reports a last render of 1,820 frames with six zeros. At the sample's 60 fps that would be about half a minute.

Let one frame read a clock and the same number stops giving the same picture.

We drew the rule as an X-ray butterfly, its wingbeat computed from the frame number ↓

title: One-cut dance music video with character swap and Irish steps
author: sairin_hamumu
prompt:
切れ目のない約28秒の1カットの手持ち撮影。結婚式の二次会の、明るく暖かい光のダンスフロア。シャンデリアとミラーボールがあり、パステルのドレスや明るい色のスーツの客でにぎわっている。この動画の主人公を「被験者」と呼ぶ。被験者は、黒いモーションキャプチャー用スーツを着た筋肉の大きな男で、白い球のマーカーが付いている。頭は最初から最後まで、首から上をすっぽり覆う黒い布のフードに包まれ、顔・目・鼻・口は一度も見えない。体は大きくたくましいまま、動きは最初から最後までプロの女性ダンサー。しなやかでキレがあり、色っぽく、可愛く、おどけて踊る。

カメラは手持ちで、最初から最後まで止まらず、キレよく動き続け、常に傾きと角度がある。正面の目の高さで止まらない。カメラは一度も振り返らず、すでに映した場所へ回り込まない。

1. 約3秒：被験者が客の間から、腰を揺らすモデル歩きで出てくる。カメラは床すれすれの低さから見上げ、斜めに傾いたまま被験者の前を素早く後ずさりする。被験者がカメラをまっすぐ指さすと、カメラはその勢いで一気に上半身へ寄り、すぐに横へ素早く回り込む。

2. 約5秒：被験者は両手を頭に当てて首をかしげ、腰を大きく、しなやかに、キレよく8の字にくねらせ続ける。腰が先に動き、胸と肩が波のように続く。カメラは被験者の周りを素早く回り込みながら、腰の高さと胸の高さを行き来し、角度を次々に変える。途中で一度、踊る客がカメラの前を横切り、一瞬だけ被験者が見えなくなる。

3. 約2秒：被験者は画面の左へ、腰を揺らすモデル歩きで進み出す。カメラはすぐに被験者の背中側へ回り込み、背中越しに進む先の人だかりを見ながら、低い位置から一緒に進む。

4. 約4秒：被験者は歩きながらくるりと振り返ってカメラの方を向き、そこから顔と体をカメラに向けたまま、後ろ歩きで速くカメラから遠ざかっていく（the subject keeps facing the camera and walks backward quickly, moving away from the camera）。客は左右に分かれて、ボウリングのレーンのような一本の道を開けている。道の先には広く空いたフロアと小さなステージがある。被験者は後ろを一度も見ずに道の真ん中を進み、カメラに向かって指をさし、色っぽく首をかしげる。カメラは遠ざかる被験者を追いかけて一緒に道を進む。

5. 約4秒：後ろ歩きを続ける被験者の背中側から、銀のお盆にグラスを載せたウェイターが近づく。被験者は顔をカメラから一切動かさず、手だけを後ろへ伸ばして、見ないままグラスを取る。後ろ歩きのまま一気に飲み干し、空のグラスを画面の横へぽいっと放り投げる。グラスは完全に画面の外へ消える。

6. 約4秒：被験者は小さなステージの前で立ち止まり、その場で激しく速いアイリッシュダンスのステップを踏む。上半身はまっすぐ、足だけが床をたたくように細かく速く動く。カメラは一気に床すれすれまで下がって足元のアップをとらえ、速いタップを踏む足を勢いよく左右に振られながら追う。足が画面に飛び込んできたり、外へ飛び出したりする。

7. 約3秒：締めくくりに、被験者はその場でくるりと一回転する。カメラはそれに合わせて勢いよく引き上がり、上半身をとらえる。被験者はぴたりと止まり、カメラに向かって両手で胸の前にハートを作り、首をかしげて可愛く「萌え萌えキュン」のポーズを決める。続けてポーズをほどき、アイドルのように可愛くジャンプする。脚を大きく開かず、ひざをそろえたまま両足を後ろへぴょこんと跳ね上げ、両手を軽く握って顔の横に上げる。

8. 約3秒：被験者が跳んだ瞬間、会場の照明が一気にダンスクラブの光に変わる。色とりどりの光の筋が動き回り、ミラーボールの光の粒が強く飛び散る。被験者は着地すると、両腕を高く上げて、ひざをそろえたままその場で元気いっぱいにぴょんぴょん跳ね続ける。両側にいた客たちがステージの前へ駆け寄ってきて、めちゃくちゃに踊り暴れる。男性はジャケットを脱いで投げ捨て、女性はハイヒールを手に持ってぶんぶん振り回す。カメラは押し寄せる客にぶつかられ、もみくちゃにされて大きく揺れながらも、人の間から跳ね続ける被験者をなんとか画面に収めようとする。

周りの客は被験者を囲んで、手を叩く、歓声を上げる、笑いながら指さす、まねをして腰を振るなど、一人一人が自分のタイミングでばらばらに反応し、全員が同じ動きをすることはない。客は年齢も髪型も顔立ちもドレスの形も色も一人一人違い、白い服の人はいない。

画面の中の全員とカメラが、普通の速さで動く。スローモーションにならない。

音：客の歓声と笑い声、手拍子、足音、グラスの音だけ。BGM・音楽は入れない。

title: Music-driven physics animation comparing Blender preview and final
author: Ayu_AI_0912
prompt:
曲と音

曲は【曲名】。著作権が切れている曲か、自分の曲を使う。楽譜（音の高さと長さ）は信頼できる出典から取って、出典を教えて。

物理

ボールは Blender の剛体物理で落とす。次の音の時刻にボールがいる場所へ次の板を置き、板の傾きと反発係数を逆算して、当たる時刻のずれを1ミリ秒未満にそろえる。
最後に通しで計算し直して、当たりが音の数と同じか（余計な当たりがないか）確かめる。
最後の音のあとにボールが板から落ちていかないよう、受け止めるもの（お椀など）を置く。

見た目

場面は【例：夕暮れの里山。手まり柄のボール、木のマリンバの板】。板は当たった瞬間に光って、波紋が出る。
カメラはボールを追いかけ、最後は引きの全景にする。地形や建物がボールやカメラの視線をふさがないようにする。
本番の前に見本のコマを数枚見せて。本番の描画は、所要時間を伝えて了承を取ってから、休憩を入れながら回して。

仕上げ

縦 1080×1920 の MP4。右下に【自分のロゴ】。
左に Blender の作業画面風（ソリッド表示＋ポリゴンの辺の線）、右に完成版を並べた横長 1920×1080 の比較動画も作る。左右の見出しは「Blender 物理演算プレビュー」と「完成（レンダー）」。

title: 40-second premium product promo for Microsoft's open-source
author: HaileyAILabs
prompt:
VibeVoice｜40 秒高质量创意种草视频制作

请参考我上传的分镜图，为微软开源项目 VibeVoice 制作一支 40 秒的高质量创意种草视频。

项目地址： https://t.co/zEzxa7XuEY

一、创作目标

我要的不是普通的科技产品介绍，也不是把 GitHub README 做成 PPT 动画。

而是一支视觉审美出色、镜头富有创意、动画流畅、音乐节奏强烈，同时能让观众直观理解 VibeVoice 核心能力的产品种草视频。

整体质感对标专业 Motion Design 工作室的品牌宣传作品。

你拥有完整的创作自由度。

不限制技术路线、动画形式、素材来源或制作工具。

可以使用 Three.js、Remotion、Blender、Canvas、SVG、WebGL、GSAP、FFmpeg、AI 图像与视频生成，以及其他合适的开源项目或工具。

可以混合使用 2D、3D、动态图形、角色动画、动态排版、音频可视化和真实产品演示。

不要求纯代码，也不要求严格复刻分镜图。

分镜图用于传达创意方向，不是限制最终画面的模板。

请根据实际制作效果主动优化构图、运镜、场景、动画和转场。

最终只看成片质量。

二、视频规格

时长：40 秒
画面比例：16:9
分辨率：1920×1080 或更高
帧率：优先 60fps
语言：中文
风格：高级、现代、富有设计感的科技创意动画
音频：有节奏感的背景音乐、必要的音效及真实语音演示
最终格式：MP4

避免廉价霓虹科技风、PPT 式转场、无意义的粒子效果、过度复杂的界面堆砌。

画面要有鲜明的视觉记忆点，不要只靠漂亮的 UI。

三、40 秒完整剧情

第一幕｜声音失控（0–6s）

一段长达 60 分钟的多人录音开始播放。

不同人物的声音混在一起，形成复杂、交错的声音波形。

随着音乐节奏加快，声音逐渐失控，画面充满混乱感。

突然，所有声音停止。

屏幕出现：

「一小时的多人录音，谁说了什么？」

要求：前 3 秒迅速抓住注意力，让观众对接下来的变化产生好奇。

第二幕｜声音有了身份（6–13s）

VibeVoice 登场。

原本混乱的声音开始分离，四位说话人的身份逐渐清晰。

每个人拥有独特的颜色、声音波形和视觉标识。

可以通过人物、抽象角色、动态头像或其他更有创意的方式表现。

四种声音从混乱逐渐变得有序，最终形成清晰的说话人标识。

字幕：

「先分清，谁在说话。」

重点是让观众直观看到说话人识别的能力，而不只是看见四条不同颜色的线。

第三幕｜时间轴魔术（13–23s）

镜头进入声音的内部世界。

一条长达 60 分钟的时间轴逐渐展开。

不同说话人的语音片段被自动标记，并生成对应的文字与时间戳。

每当一个人说话，其对应的声音轨迹和文字同时出现。

镜头可以穿梭于声音、人物、文本和时间轴之间，呈现连续、有节奏的视觉变化。

字幕：

「谁说的，什么时候说的，说了什么。」

「一次整理清楚。」

这一幕是全片的核心高潮，需要最强的视觉表现力。

第四幕｜混乱变成秩序（23–33s）

镜头拉远，刚才复杂的声音世界逐渐整理成一个清晰、有序的语音记录界面。

四位说话人的内容按照时间顺序排列。

观众可以直观看到说话人、时间戳与识别文本的对应关系。

通过动态镜头与交互演示，让观众理解长音频结构化识别的实际价值。

字幕：

「60 分钟长音频，也能结构化识别。」

注意：60 分钟指官方支持的音频长度，不代表能够瞬间完成识别。

第五幕｜结尾反转（33–40s）

所有声音轨道、人物标识和文字逐渐汇聚。

镜头拉远，前面复杂的声音世界最终变成一个简洁的 VibeVoice 标识。

出现：

VibeVoice

Microsoft · Open Source

https://t.co/NyAnbFjRSR

在观众以为视频结束时，一条小小的声音波形突然再次跳动。

屏幕出现：

「等等，我还有一句！」

伴随一个俏皮的音效，画面结束。

结尾要有趣，不能只是普通的 Logo 动画。

四、视觉与动画要求

你可以重新设计所有场景，但必须保证整支作品拥有统一的美术语言。

重点关注：

视觉创意：尽量用有趣的视觉隐喻表达抽象技术，让声音真正成为画面的主角。
镜头设计：镜头之间具有连贯关系，避免每一幕都是独立的静态画面。
运动质量：动作具有自然的加减速、节奏、重量感和层次。
画面构图：建立清晰的视觉中心，控制留白与信息密度。
动态排版：文字既要清晰易读，也要成为视觉设计的一部分。
音画同步：声音变化、字幕、角色反应和音乐节点准确对应。
情绪变化：从混乱、好奇，到惊喜、清晰，最后用幽默感收尾。

允许为提升成片质量调整镜头时长、动画结构、转场以及视觉表现。

但不要改变核心产品能力，也不要加入未经验证的功能。

五、音乐与声音设计

音乐是这支视频的重要组成部分。

请根据剧情设计一段完整的音乐与音效结构。

开头制造紧张和混乱感；说话人分离时让节奏逐渐清晰；时间轴展开时进入最有冲击力的段落；结尾自然收束并留下一个有趣的声音反转。

可以使用原创电子音乐、Funk、节奏型配乐或其他适合画面的风格。

优先使用真实的 VibeVoice 演示音频。

不强制配音。如果通过音乐、人物声音、字幕和动画能把故事讲清楚，就不要添加多余的解说。

不要为了配音而配音。

六、产品真实性

制作前请阅读 VibeVoice 官方仓库和相关文档，确保产品信息准确。

本片重点展示 VibeVoice-ASR 的：

长音频语音识别
多说话人识别
时间戳生成
结构化文本输出

注意，说话人区分不等同于把混合录音真实分离成多条独立音频文件。

如果无法实际运行 VibeVoice，可以使用官方提供的演示结果进行展示，并明确区分真实输出和概念动画。

不能伪造模型性能、识别准确率或处理速度。

七、制作与质量优化

请自主决定最适合的技术组合和制作流程，不需要拘泥于某一种框架。

可以寻找高质量开源动画库、视觉参考、现成组件或制作工具辅助实现。

但不要为了堆技术而牺牲审美。

制作时遵循以下原则：

先明确全片美术风格、镜头语言和视觉节奏。
按照统一风格完成全部场景。
保证视觉主体、字幕、声音和镜头运动相互配合。
实际渲染并检查关键画面与视频片段。
对人物一致性、动作僵硬、镜头突兀、画面单调、字幕错误和音画不同步等问题主动修正。
如果某种方案实际效果不好，主动更换实现方式，不要坚持错误方向。
优先保证最终作品的整体完成度，而不是单个镜头的炫技效果。

允许反复修改和重新设计，直到形成一支完整、统一、有传播吸引力的作品。

title: Shape that morphs through UI states
author: RaphaelAubryy
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: the product name and a one-line promise, 3 to 5 UI moments to show, one accent color, 10 to 20 real vertical clips I own, and a royalty-free song with a clear drop (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
High-end minimal. One idea per shot, lots of empty space, one accent color, one clean sans (Geist or Inter) with tight tracking. Masked type reveals, match cuts, one smooth camera language. Real footage only, never placeholder cards. No full stops in on-screen text.
Banned: shockwave rings, particle bursts, RGB split, camera shake, lens flares, neon glows, grid floors, flashing backgrounds, bouncy easing.
</direction>

<structure>
10 bars at 120 BPM, 2 seconds each.
Bar 1: the hook lands word by word on the beats.
Bar 2: one hook word morphs into the product UI. A cursor types and clicks.
The drop: a circle opens out of the button into a dark scene.
Then one move per bar: a wall of real clips with a scan line and 3 winners, the key output as big type, a 3D carousel of real videos with floor reflections and a motion-blurred whip onto one hero clip, the hero in a phone next to a panel that flips into results, big stats on push cuts, a 3-word ticker, a logo reveal, a fade to black.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file at 1920x1080. Every style is computed from time inside 
http://
window.seek(t): no CSS animations, no timers, no state between frames.
2. Real video: extract clips to 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg and swap img sources per frame. seek awaits the image decodes.
3. Analyze the song with numpy: tempo, beat grid, energy per bar, the drop. Calibrate the grid to the real kick hits. Every cut sits on a downbeat, every UI hit on a beat.
4. Render with Playwright: 3 subframes per frame at t minus, at, and plus 1/240s, then blend with ffmpeg tmix for real motion blur at 60fps.
5. Place each sound effect so its measured peak, not its file start, lands on the event. Keep the effects quiet under the music. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
6. Probe 20 or more frames before the full render. Fix anything cluttered, overlapping or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never set opacity or filter on a preserve-3d element, because it flattens and both faces show. Fade its wrapper instead. Measure element positions at runtime for match cuts. Only use music and sound effects whose license allows commercial use.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me a storyboard with every timing on the beat grid before you write any code.
</start>

title: One-file 1440×1440 UI morphing sequence with beat-synced state
author: jasonugc
prompt:
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to become (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist). Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs open into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The tab indicator's two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Same trick for the toggle knob.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is computed from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Place every UI sound by its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text renders blurry. Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps. Make the last frame identical to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.
